Per-frame luma normalization handles gain/offset. 155	| 2026-06-15 | **Static-list highlight reader = per-screen menu geometry (band + ordered items + axis) + per-cell "deviation from unselected baseline" with per-frame colour normalization; argmax over cells.** Scope = the 8 fixed-count static lists; `section_select` (variable list) and `song_select` (fixed-slot) deferred. | GH3 marks selection by *changing* a row (colour shift / highlight bar), not always by making it brightest — a luma/white argmax collided on most screens (flat scores). Comparing each cell to its own learned unselected appearance ("what changed") handles every highlight style and baselines out background art (main_menu / practice_end sit over collage). Baseline uses only *unselected* exemplars per cell so it's non-degenerate at K=2 (a median-over-all collapses to the midpoint and can't separate two items — that bug showed as exactly 1/2 on the three two-item screens). 159	| 2026-06-15 | **Per-frame normalization is on by default; it is required for value-slop robustness.** | The Wii feed is analog component → HDMI, so it carries gain/offset value slop. 165	## Hardware cost note (SAM9X75 port target)
```text
166	
167	ARM926EJ-S, ARMv5TE, single core, up to 800 MHz, no SIMD. The classifier is **memory-bound,
168	not compute-bound** — the dominant cost is reading frame pixels from the uncached DDR
169	framebuffer (~50–150 MB/s sequential; ~50–150 ns per strided single access). Compute
170	(per-region integer sums + an L1 distance over 13 templates ≈ a couple thousand byte ops) is
171	microseconds.
172	
173	- Dense (every pixel, 720×480×3 ≈ 1.04 MB): **~7–20 ms**.
174	- Subsampled lattice (default 12×8 × 5×5 = 2400 reads): **~0.1–0.4 ms**.
175	
176	Either is far from "seconds"; the observer needs only a few Hz for menu navigation, so the
177	subsampled path costs <1% CPU at 5–10 Hz.

274	### 2026-07-10 — streak: audited/cleaned the training set + units-wrap tens carry (fixes the carry lag)
275	
276	Two linked changes after Greg reviewed the corpus by eye:
277	
278	1. **Training-set audit.** The auto-selected units exemplars had let **mid-roll** samples in — a
279	   rolling wheel momentarily reads as a digit but the glyph is half-transitioned, and averaging those
280	   smears the template. Greg reviewed every crop; removed the mid-roll ones and relabelled full-label
281	   crops whose ones was rolling to exclude just the units (`08x`, `11x`, `16x` — keeping their settled
282	   tens/hundreds). Corpus 76→65. **Future policy (Greg): a digit is usable only if it reads identically
283	   across neighbouring frames** — any frame-to-frame change = not settled. (To implement in the
284	   auto-growth tooling.) After cleanup some units digits are thin (2:3, 3:2, 4:3) — re-grow with the
285	   stability gate if they under-detect.
286	
287	2. **Units-wrap tens carry.** Cleaner data made units-9 detect better, which *exposed* the tens carry
288	   lag: at a ten-crossing the units rolls to 0 immediately but the debounced tens lagged, so the
289	   display dipped 49→40→50. Fixed by stepping the tens the instant the units wraps — a confident units
290	   read that dropped by ≥`STREAK_WRAP_MIN`(5) bumps the *current* (debounced) tens by one, cascading to
291	   the hundreds. **Safe against the earlier lock**: it works off the debounced digits and fires only on
292	   a genuine wrap, so it never re-rounds a stale value — if a wrong-high tens was corrected downward,
293	   the units isn't wrapping, no carry fires, and the correction stands. Verified by a regression test
294	   (a 2-frame tens misread commits ~141 then recovers to 11x, *not* stuck) and over the capture:
295	   carry-lag dips 30→0, 0 implausible jumps, anchors exact, 4 transient recoveries, 76 tests green.

297	### 2026-07-10 — integer-math rewrite of the score + streak readers (bit-exact C↔Python; fixes a coverage OOB bug)
298	
299	Rewrote the shared coverage pipeline (luma → ink threshold → grid resize → per-cell coverage) to
300	**pure integer** so the firmware reproduces the host prototype bit-for-bit. Why it mattered for
301	*accuracy*, not just speed: the firmware extracted coverage in float32 while the templates were built
302	and validated in Python float64, with different rounding (`np.round` half-to-even vs C half-up,
303	`np.linspace().round()` vs `lround`) — so the device's reads diverged from the host-validated reads
304	(more hardware misreads than the host showed). Now:
305	- luma = `B*29+G*150+R*77` (no `/256` — cancels in the relative threshold);
306	- ink threshold = a rational `NUM/DEN` of the cell's min..max range (score 3/5, streak 1/2), tested as
307	  `DEN*(luma-lo) ≷ NUM*(hi-lo)`;
308	- grid edges = `(2*i*extent+n)/(2*n)` (round-half-up); per-cell coverage = `(count*255 + npx/2)/npx`.
309	No float remains in the readers (the ARM926 has no FPU). The screen classifier / song matcher (a
310	separate float-normalization path) are untouched — out of scope.
311	
312	**Found + fixed a coverage out-of-bounds bug** doing this: when a glyph's ink bbox is smaller than the
313	grid (e.g. a 6-row bbox stretched to 16 grid rows), the last grid cell's block runs *past the bbox*.
314	numpy silently clamps the slice to empty (→ coverage 0), but the C loop read one row/col beyond, into
315	the **unused tail of the scratch buffer** (stale data) → wrong coverage on short glyphs. Fixed by
316	clamping `yb→rh`, `xb→rw` in both C loops (host made explicit to match). This was present in the float
317	version too — it's why the streak cross-check kept a `known`-flag mismatch on cap4247, and it means
318	the device had real misreads on short glyphs (now gone).
319	
320	Cross-check is now **strict bit-exact** (C == Python on presence, every digit, every confidence flag,
321	all frames). Re-validated: score LOO 54/54, streak in-sample 154/154, capture anchors exact, units
322	detection intact (0/6/9 = 434/335/256). Digit banks in `gameplay_metadata.h` rebuilt with the integer
323	coverage. Remaining edge: a 2-frame song-end slide-out can re-seed on misaligned digits (capture max
324	384) — a brief-dropout-reseed case, separate follow-up.
325

357	### 2026-07-10 — streak tracker: per-place debounce + plausibility clamp (fixes lock, 0↔8 flicker, carry blip)
358	
359	Reworked the streak tracker to fix a reported **lock** and two failures it surfaced. The prior
360	monotonic forward window `[last, last+30]` couldn't represent a value *below* `last`, so a tens
361	misread that nudged `last` up locked in and every units roll then forced the tens higher (11x read as
362	14x, 12x→15x…). Replacing it with plain "confident read trumps" fixed the lock but unmasked two
363	pre-existing misreads the window had hidden: the **tens 0↔8 flicker** (the slashed zero's top loop
364	closes under A2D aliasing → a tens "0" matches the 8-template better and reads 8 *confidently*,
365	alternating frame-to-frame, 100↔180) and a **carry-roll blip** (at 99→100 the mid-roll hundreds wheel
366	reads 9 confidently for ~2 frames → a 900 flash).
367	
368	Fix = two temporal/physical guards, both symmetric so they correct downward and **never lock**:
369	- **Per-place debounce** (`GP_STREAK_DEBOUNCE {2,2,1}`): a *changed* digit commits only after N
370	  consecutive confident reads. Slow wheels (hundreds/tens) N=2 → single-frame flips (0↔8) never
371	  stick; units N=1 → stays responsive (debouncing the fast wheel would freeze it). A committed change
372	  carries (unreadable lower places → 0); an unreadable place holds.
373	- **Plausibility clamp** (`GP_STREAK_MAX_STEP 50`): reject a committed per-frame value change > 50 —
374	  a streak can't gain that much per ~3 Hz poll, so it's a misread that cleared debounce (the 2-frame
375	  carry hundreds read). The seed bypasses it (a real reappearance jumps straight in).
376	
377	Over the 6549-frame capture: **0 implausible jumps (94 → 15 with debounce alone → 0 with the clamp),
378	max back to 304, anchors exact.** `test_streak.py` gains flicker/debounce/clamp cases (74 pass).
379	**Still open — units-9 detection:** the units wheel (dark-on-light) has a fat distance tail, so a
380	correct 9 (dist ~12300) exceeds the `UNK_DIST` gate and is dropped; needs more units exemplars — a
381	corpus-growth pass mining the capture is next.
382	
383	### 2026-07-10 — note-streak counter (odometer OCR + confident-read tracker) → dashboard label
384	
385	Added the last scoring-block value: the **note streak**, a 3-tumbler mechanical odometer (note icon
386	+ hundreds/tens/units) right of the multiplier. Two halves, mirroring the firmware split:
387	
388	- **Stateless reader** (`read_streak`, `score.py`). **Presence = the odometer is *locked at its
389	  final position*, detected from the note icon — NOT the digits** (Greg): the whole counter *slides
390	  in from the bottom, overshoots, and bounces down* to settle (≈20 frames; `score-0335.png` is the
391	  reference locked frame), and mid-slide the digit cells are misaligned → garbage. The fixed gold
392	  note-icon glyph is a position-sensitive fiducial: its coverage matches the locked template (L1 <
393	  `NOTE_MAX_SAD`=2000) only when settled — cleanly separates locked (≤~1300) from slide/overshoot
394	  (~3200–10000) and absent (~17000+). Three fixed digit cells; polarity differs — **units is
395	  dark-on-light** (highlighted), **tens/hundreds white-on-dark** (like the score). Per cell: ink by
396	  polarity → 16×10 coverage grid → integer-L1 argmin over a **per-polarity** 0-9 bank; a cell is
397	  **unreadable** when best-L1/margin fail the gate (mid-roll). *All three wheels roll* (Greg), so no
398	  place is trusted per-frame. ROIs are consistent 8×15 digit cells + a 10×15 note cell (Greg's box
399	  refinement → 100 % in-sample confident-digit accuracy). All positions are **absolute** in the
400	  720×480 frame (fixed rig; the score reader's chrome registration exists but is unused in v0).
401	- **Stateful tracker** (`StreakTracker`). **Presence is binary: not present ⇒ the streak reset ⇒ 0**
402	  (immediate — the counter only vanishes on a miss/below-threshold; the sole reset path). While
403	  present, **a confident wheel read is authoritative for its place** (Greg: "a clear read of a digit
404	  trumps the automatic rollover logic") — it always wins, even if the value drops, so a misread is a
405	  self-correcting one-frame blip, not a permanent lock. An unreadable (rolling) wheel is *filled*:
406	  it holds its last digit, or resets to 0 when a higher place changed this frame (a carry). ≥2
407	  confident wheels seed a first appearance. This **replaced an earlier monotonic constrained-search**
408	  (`[last, last+30]`, ties→smallest): that forward-only window could never represent a value *below*
409	  `last`, so a single tens misread that nudged `last` up got locked in — every subsequent units roll
410	  then forced the tens upward (11x read as 14x, 12x→15x…). Confident-trumps fixes that.
411	
412	**No filename ground truth** (unlike the score), so a **hand-labelled odometer corpus** (`data/streak/`,
413	46 block crops read from capture montages, `x` = mid-roll wheel) builds the banks. Validation over the
414	full **6549-frame capture**: hand-read anchors exact, **0 non-reset decreases**, correct slide-gating
415	(0 through the slide, reads only once locked), max 304; **100 % in-sample confident-digit accuracy**
416	with the refined 8×15 cells.
417	
418	**Known follow-up — the tens 0↔8 confusion (deferred, to fix with a per-place debounce).** Dropping
419	the monotonic window unmasked a *pre-existing* systematic misread the old window had accidentally
420	hidden: the odometer's zero has a center slash, and A2D aliasing closes its top loop on ~half the
421	frames, so a tens "0" wheel genuinely matches the **8** template better (dist 4590 vs 6885) and reads
422	8 *confidently* — alternating 0,8,0,8 frame-to-frame (100↔180, 200↔280, 300↔380; a hundreds variant
423	flashes 900). It is a real per-frame ambiguity, not a template/threshold bug, so it needs **temporal**
424	handling: require a *changed* confident digit to persist ≥2 consecutive reads before committing
425	(debounces the alternation; a sustained real change still commits with ~1-frame lag; cannot lock since
426	it follows reads up *or* down). Committing the lock fix first; debounce is the next change.

497	### 2026-07-09 — score reader reworked: proportional (gap-based) segmentation + 6549-frame capture corpus
498	
499	Greg captured the scoring block at full rate via the new `marvin-perf score-capture`/REGION
500	stream (`captures/web-20260709-142721`, 6549 frames climbing 250→101720) and flagged that the
501	training font is **not monospace** — right-aligned, but digit x-positions shift with the value
502	(a `1` is narrower than an `8`). Confirmed on the capture: fixed-pitch cells can't sit on the
503	digits, but the digits are cleanly **gap-separated** (no touching). So the fixed-pitch grid +
504	blank-class was replaced with **gap-based segmentation**: threshold the digit band (relative
505	`min+0.6·range`, gain/offset-robust), split the column ink profile into digit blobs (right-to-
506	left), resize each blob's bbox to a canonical grid, 1-NN-match. Digit count = blob count (no
507	fixed N, no blank class). Chrome-of-the-block registration retained; block crops are embedded
508	into a full frame (`_ensure_full_frame`) so the absolute ROIs / registration work unchanged.
509	
510	Corpus: extracted the 6549 REGION frames (`export-region`), read **54** spanning 3–6 digits off
511	montages (values cross-checked by the monotonic ordering), committed as
512	`score__training__NNNNNN__capNNNN.png` (replacing the 9-frame set; the capture itself is
513	gitignored). `metadata.SCORE_DIGIT_BAND` (block-relative digit band) replaces the old fixed
```

```text
1	# GH3 (Wii) — Navigation Model
2	
3	Working model of Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock (Wii) screens and the menu
4	graph between them. This is the source artifact for the §4.8 game-state work:
5	the **observer** (M9) classifies the current screen and reads the highlighted
6	selection; the **controller** (M10) plans button sequences along the graph
7	edges below. See [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.8.3 (game catalog & menu metadata).
8	
9	Screen text is transcribed from operator narration; the referenced screens live
10	as a renamed corpus in [`gh3_screens/`](gh3_screens/) (see its README for the
11	name ↔ original-snapshot mapping). Raw `marvin-perf snapshot` captures land in
12	the gitignored `tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/`. Native capture is 720×480.
13	
14	**Scope now:** the navigation *structure* — screens, their items, and the edges
15	between them. The **vision** side is now built: the observer classifier lives in
16	`game/gameplay_classify.c` (`gp_classify()`), and the controller
17	(`game/game_controller.c`) uses it closed-loop (see Navigator notes below). This
18	doc remains the source artifact for the screen/edge model those consume; screen
19	snapshots stay recorded here as the corpus.
20	
21	Status: **in progress** — this navigation map is populated screen-by-screen
22	(`TBD` = not yet captured); the observer + controller that consume it are built.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## Conventions
27	
28	### Inputs
29	- **Strum up / strum down** — move the selection within a list.
30	- **GREEN** — confirm / enter the selected item.
31	- **RED** — back up one level.
32	
33	(Bit names on the wire are the gameplay fret/strum masks; the controller emits
34	the same bits for menu navigation — the fretboard MCU doesn't distinguish menu
35	from gameplay. §4.8.4.) Some menus also use the `+` button (pause) and possibly
36	others beyond fret/strum; the full controller is actuatable in principle —
37	fauxmote emulates the complete guitar extension incl. `+`/`−` — the actuator
38	command protocol just needs to carry those inputs.
39	
40	### Highlight paradigms
41	How "selected" is presented drives what the observer reads. Two kinds so far:
42	
43	- **static-list** — the list is painted at fixed screen positions; a highlight
44	  moves between rows. Observer reads *which row is lit*. (e.g. `main_menu`)
45	- **fixed-slot** — the selected item sits in a fixed, highlighted slot and the
46	  list scrolls underneath it. Observer reads *what occupies the highlight slot*.
47	  (e.g. `song_select`)
48	
49	### Edge notation
50	An edge is `from → to : [inputs]`. `STRUM_DN×n` means n strum-downs. Moving to
51	list index `i` from the top (index 0) on a static list is `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN`.
52

140	### section_select  *(practice — variable per song)*
141	- **reached from:** `difficulty_select` → GREEN.
142	- **paradigm:** static-list (assumed; confirm).
143	- **items:** **song-dependent** (intro / verse / solo / etc.), but **index 0 is
144	  always "FULL SONG"** — `gh3_screens/section_select__full_song.png`. Only FULL SONG is in scope; other
145	  sections are ignored.
146	- **select FULL SONG:** `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` — strum up to the **top** of the
147	  list (FULL SONG = index 0), then confirm. Don't assume the cursor enters at
148	  index 0 (may be sticky / land elsewhere); strumming up saturates at the top so
149	  it lands on FULL SONG regardless of entry position. `N` ≥ the longest section
150	  list (or "until the highlight stops moving"). **Assumes no wrap-around** — see
151	  open items; if the list wraps, read the highlight instead.
152	- **back (RED):** `difficulty_select`.
153	- **leads to:** `speed_select`.

182	  training background is always the same; other modes (career/quickplay) may use

184	- **pause:** the guitar `+` button opens `pause_menu` mid-song.

201	- **leads to:**
202	  - RESUME → `in_song` (resume gameplay)
203	  - RESTART → `loading` → `in_song` (replay current song)
204	  - OPTIONS → options submenu *(out of scope; RED to recover)*
205	  - CHANGE SPEED → `speed_select`

207	  - NEW SONG → `song_select`
208	  - QUIT → `quit_confirm` (confirmation dialog — not straight to main menu)
209	- **`+` actuation:** opening the pause needs the `+` button (not a fret/strum
210	  bit). Actuatable in principle — fauxmote's emulated guitar-extension report
211	  already carries the `+`/`−` buttons ([`firmware/fauxmote`](../../fauxmote/SPEC.md),
212	  §3). The marvin→actuator command path is fret/strum-focused today (§4.3);
213	  carrying `+`/`−` and other controller buttons for menu use is a command-protocol
214	  extension, not a hardware limit.

343	## Menu graph (edges)
344	
345	| from | to | inputs | notes |
346	|------|----|--------|-------|
347	| main_menu | _(per item)_ | `STRUM_DN×index, GREEN` | static list, index per catalog above |
348	| main_menu | training_menu | `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` | TRAINING (index 4) |
349	| training_menu | song_select | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | PRACTICE (index 1) |
350	| song_select | part_select | `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN` | song at list index i; shared node. May skip part_select for some songs |
351	| song_select | bonus list | `BLUE` (back: `YELLOW`) | toggles the song list, not a screen change |
352	| part_select | difficulty_select | LEAD `GREEN` / 2nd `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | items song-dependent |
353	| difficulty_select | section_select | `STRUM_DN×index, GREEN` | EASY 0 / MEDIUM 1 / HARD 2 / EXPERT 3 |
354	| section_select | speed_select | `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` | FULL SONG = top (idx 0); strum up to saturate |
355	| speed_select | loading | `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` | FULL SPEED = top (idx 0); strum up to saturate |
356	| loading | in_song | _(none — wait)_ | transient; auto-advances |
357	| in_song | pause_menu | `+` (guitar plus) | not a fret/strum bit — see caveat |
358	| in_song | practice_end_menu | _(none — song ends)_ | gameplay completes |
359	| pause_menu | in_song | `GREEN` | RESUME (idx 0) |
360	| pause_menu | loading | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | RESTART (idx 1) → replay |
361	| pause_menu | speed_select | `STRUM_DN×3, GREEN` | CHANGE SPEED (idx 3) |
362	| pause_menu | section_select | `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` | CHANGE SECTION (idx 4) |
363	| pause_menu | song_select | `STRUM_DN×5, GREEN` | NEW SONG (idx 5) |
364	| pause_menu | quit_confirm | `STRUM_DN×6, GREEN` | QUIT (idx 6) → confirm dialog |
365	| quit_confirm | pause_menu | `GREEN` | CANCEL (idx 0) |
366	| quit_confirm | main_menu | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | QUIT (idx 1) — confirm |
367	| practice_end_menu | song_select | `GREEN` | CONTINUE (idx 0) |
368	| practice_end_menu | loading | `STRUM_DN×1, GREEN` | RESTART (idx 1) → replay |
369	| practice_end_menu | speed_select | `STRUM_DN×2, GREEN` | CHANGE SPEED (idx 2) |
370	| practice_end_menu | section_select | `STRUM_DN×3, GREEN` | CHANGE SECTION (idx 3) |
371	| practice_end_menu | main_menu | `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` | QUIT (idx 4) |
372	| _any_ | _(parent)_ | `RED` | back up one level |

378	## Navigator notes (implementation)
379	
380	> **Implemented (2026-07-02):** the on-device controller is
381	> `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/game_controller.c` — a port of the offline
382	> `tools/gameplay` `NavController`. Triggered by the dashboard START button or the
383	> console `play` command; reads the committed `Selection`; drives the worked path

388	How the controller (M10) uses this map. Unmapped paths don't need modeling —

391	- **Closed-loop — verify every screen (not a blind macro).** Before issuing a
392	  step's inputs, confirm the observer reports the expected screen; after issuing
393	  them, confirm the expected destination before proceeding. On mismatch, recover
394	  (see below) and re-plan. Never fire a button sequence open-loop and *assume* we
395	  landed where we hoped — drift, sticky defaults, variable/absent screens, and
396	  load times all break that. This is why the observer (M9) gates the controller
397	  (M10). (spec §4.8.1.)

400	  any screen the observer doesn't recognize are treated as "unknown state."

408	### Worked path — training run (main-setlist song `i`, difficulty `d`, LEAD)
409	The nominal input plan. Each step runs **gated on a screen check** (verify the
410	expected screen before, confirm arrival after) per the closed-loop rule above —
411	it is not executed as one blind burst. From `main_menu` (if not there, recover

413	
414	1. `STRUM_DN×4, GREEN` → TRAINING → `training_menu`

420	7. `STRUM_UP×N, GREEN` → FULL SPEED → `loading` (wait) → `in_song` (gameplay)
421
```

```text
102	/* Average BGR over a (2r+1)×(2r+1) patch centered on (px,py), clipping
103	 * to frame bounds. Center is clamped first so a one-pixel-off calibration
104	 * still produces a reading instead of a silent zero. */
105	static void sample_patch_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh,
106	                             uint16_t px, uint16_t py, float out[3])
107	{
108	    int cx = (int)px;
109	    if (cx < 0)        { cx = 0; }
110	    else if (cx >= fw) { cx = fw - 1; }
111	    int cy = (int)py;
112	    if (cy < 0)        { cy = 0; }
113	    else if (cy >= fh) { cy = fh - 1; }
114	
115	    int r = (int)CV_PATCH_RADIUS;
116	    int x0 = cx - r;       if (x0 < 0)  { x0 = 0; }
117	    int y0 = cy - r;       if (y0 < 0)  { y0 = 0; }
118	    int x1 = cx + r + 1;   if (x1 > fw) { x1 = fw; }
119	    int y1 = cy + r + 1;   if (y1 > fh) { y1 = fh; }
120	
121	    uint32_t sum_b = 0u, sum_g = 0u, sum_r = 0u;
122	    uint32_t row_stride = (uint32_t)fw * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
123	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
124	    {
125	        const uint8_t *row = frame
126	                           + (uint32_t)y * row_stride
127	                           + (uint32_t)x0 * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
128	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
129	        {
130	            sum_b += row[0];
131	            sum_g += row[1];
132	            sum_r += row[2];
133	            row   += CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
134	        }
135	    }
136	    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(x1 - x0) * (uint32_t)(y1 - y0);
137	    out[0] = (float)sum_b / (float)n;
138	    out[1] = (float)sum_g / (float)n;
139	    out[2] = (float)sum_r / (float)n;
140	}

142	/* Max channel — triggers on any color or white. */
143	static float brightness(const float bgr[3])
144	{
145	    float m = bgr[0];
146	    if (bgr[1] > m) { m = bgr[1]; }
147	    if (bgr[2] > m) { m = bgr[2]; }
148	    return m;
149	}
150	
151	/* Color-filtered signal scaled by (max-min)/max so white/gray patches
152	 * produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance. */
153	static float color_signal(const float bgr[3], const color_filter_t *f)
154	{
155	    float cmax = brightness(bgr);
156	    if (cmax < 1.0f) { return 0.0f; }
157	    float cmin = bgr[0];
158	    if (bgr[1] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[1]; }
159	    if (bgr[2] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[2]; }
160	    float sat = (cmax - cmin) / cmax;
161	
162	    float target = f->target[0]*bgr[0] + f->target[1]*bgr[1] + f->target[2]*bgr[2];
163	    float reject = f->reject[0]*bgr[0] + f->reject[1]*bgr[1] + f->reject[2]*bgr[2];
164	    if (reject < 0.0f) { reject = 0.0f; }
165	    return (target - reject) * sat;
166	}

170	static void detect_frame(const Video_FrameInfo *frame, QueueHandle_t bus)
171	{
172	    detector_state_t state;
173	    memset(&state, 0, sizeof(state));
174	    state.frame_epoch  = frame->frame_count;
175	    state.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK;
176	    state.detector_id  = (uint8_t)DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1;
177	
178	    const float    hold_release = CV_HOLD_THRESH * CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
179	    const uint8_t *fbuf = (const uint8_t *)frame->buffer;
180	    uint16_t       fw   = frame->width;
181	    uint16_t       fh   = frame->height;
182	
183	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
184	    {
185	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
186	        float hold_bgr[3], edge_bgr[3];
187	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.hx, s.hy, hold_bgr);
188	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.ex, s.ey, edge_bgr);
189	
190	        float hd = brightness(hold_bgr);
191	        float ed = color_signal(edge_bgr, &s_color_filter[i]);
192	        s_hold_dist[i] = hd;
193	        s_edge_dist[i] = ed;
194	
195	        if (!s_pressed[i] && hd > CV_HOLD_THRESH)   { s_pressed[i] = true;  }
196	        else if (s_pressed[i] && hd < hold_release) { s_pressed[i] = false; }
197	
198	        bool edge_on = ed > CV_EDGE_THRESH;
199	        if (edge_on && !s_edge_active[i]) { s_press_count[i]++; }
200	        s_edge_active[i] = edge_on;
201	
202	        state.fret[i].pressed = s_pressed[i] ? 1u : 0u;
203	
204	        /* confidence: edge_dist scaled to 0..65535. ed lives roughly in
205	         * channel-value units (~0..255) so ×256 fills the range. */
206	        float c = ed * 256.0f;
207	        if (c < 0.0f)        { c = 0.0f;     }
208	        if (c > 65535.0f)    { c = 65535.0f; }
209	        state.fret[i].confidence = (uint16_t)c;
210	
211	        /* raw_value: hold_dist (max channel, 0..255). */
212	        float h = hd;
213	        if (h < 0.0f)        { h = 0.0f;     }
214	        if (h > 65535.0f)    { h = 65535.0f; }
215	        state.fret[i].raw_value = (uint16_t)h;
216	    }
217	
218	    (void)xQueueSend(bus, &state, 0);
219	
220	    /* Mirror the same per-frame decision into the perf-log so offline tools
221	     * (marvin-perf, export-ml) can join detector ground truth with sensor
222	     * input. raw_value/confidence already scale 0..65535 to match the
223	     * perf-log struct. masks are LSB-first per fret_t. Default-disabled at
224	     * boot like the other high-rate types; host enables via SET_TYPE_MASK. */
225	    uint16_t hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];
226	    uint16_t edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];
227	    uint8_t  pressed_mask = 0u;
228	    uint8_t  edge_active_mask = 0u;
229	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
230	    {
231	        hold_dist[i] = state.fret[i].raw_value;
232	        edge_dist[i] = state.fret[i].confidence;
233	        if (s_pressed[i])     { pressed_mask     |= (uint8_t)(1u << i); }
234	        if (s_edge_active[i]) { edge_active_mask |= (uint8_t)(1u << i); }
235	    }
236	    PerfLog_EmitDetector(state.frame_epoch, hold_dist, edge_dist,
237	                         pressed_mask, edge_active_mask);
238	}

259	static inline void put_pixel_bgr(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
260	                                 int x, int y,
261	                                 uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
262	{
263	    if (x < 0 || x >= fw || y < 0 || y >= fh) { return; }
264	    uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)fw + (uint32_t)x) * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
265	    p[0] = b; p[1] = g; p[2] = r;
266	}

268	/* Bresenham midpoint circle — perimeter only, 8-way symmetric. */
269	static void draw_ring(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
270	                      int cx, int cy, int radius,
271	                      uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
272	{
273	    int x = radius, y = 0, err = 0;
274	    while (x >= y)
275	    {
276	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy + y, b, g, r);
277	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy + x, b, g, r);
278	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy + x, b, g, r);
279	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy + y, b, g, r);
280	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy - y, b, g, r);
281	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy - x, b, g, r);
282	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy - x, b, g, r);
283	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy - y, b, g, r);
284	        y++;
285	        err += 1 + 2 * y;
286	        if (2 * (err - x) + 1 > 0) { x--; err += 1 - 2 * x; }
287	    }
288	}
289	
290	static void draw_filled_disk(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
291	                             int cx, int cy, int radius,
292	                             uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
293	{
294	    int rr = radius * radius;
295	    for (int dy = -radius; dy <= radius; dy++)
296	    {
297	        for (int dx = -radius; dx <= radius; dx++)
298	        {
299	            if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= rr)
300	            {
301	                put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + dx, cy + dy, b, g, r);
302	            }
303	        }
304	    }
305	}

308	 * detector is firing this frame. Hold dot = white => brightness over
309	 * threshold. Edge dot = fret color => color-filtered edge over threshold.
310	 * Lets the user watch chatter live: a stable note should show a steady
311	 * dot for the hold duration; a strum window should flash the edge dot
312	 * once. Constant flicker = noise pushing thresholds. */
313	#define CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R     1u
314	
315	/* Draw the per-fret rings/dots into `buf` (bw×bh, tightly packed), with sensor
316	 * coords translated by the buffer's frame-space origin (ox, oy). Pixels falling
317	 * outside the buffer are clipped by put_pixel_bgr. */
318	static void draw_overlay(uint8_t *buf, uint16_t bw, uint16_t bh,
319	                         uint16_t ox, uint16_t oy)
320	{
321	    int w = (int)bw, h = (int)bh;
322	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
323	    {
324	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
325	        const uint8_t *e = s_overlay_edge_bgr[i];
326	        int hx = (int)s.hx - (int)ox, hy = (int)s.hy - (int)oy;
327	        int ex = (int)s.ex - (int)ox, ey = (int)s.ey - (int)oy;
328	
329	        draw_ring(buf, w, h, hx, hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
330	                  s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
331	        draw_ring(buf, w, h, ex, ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
332	                  e[0], e[1], e[2]);
333	
334	        if (s_pressed[i])
335	        {
336	            draw_filled_disk(buf, w, h, hx, hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
337	                             s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
338	        }
339	        if (s_edge_active[i])
340	        {
341	            draw_filled_disk(buf, w, h, ex, ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
342	                             e[0], e[1], e[2]);
343	        }
344	    }
345	}
346	
347	/* ─── Detector-config publish ──────────────────────────────────────────── */
348	
349	/* Snapshot the static cv_marvin_v1 tables (sample coords, thresholds,
350	 * color filter weights) into a wire record. Static today; when M6
351	 * calibration UI lands and these become runtime-tunable, this function
352	 * is the single point that re-publishes after each tweak. */
353	static void publish_detector_config(void)
354	{
355	    perf_rec_detector_config_t cfg;
356	    memset(&cfg, 0, sizeof(cfg));
357	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
358	    {
359	        cfg.sensor_hx[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].hx;
360	        cfg.sensor_hy[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].hy;
361	        cfg.sensor_ex[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].ex;
362	        cfg.sensor_ey[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].ey;
363	        cfg.color_target_b[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[0];
364	        cfg.color_target_g[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[1];
365	        cfg.color_target_r[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[2];
366	        cfg.color_reject_b[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[0];
367	        cfg.color_reject_g[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[1];
368	        cfg.color_reject_r[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[2];
369	    }
370	    cfg.hold_thresh       = CV_HOLD_THRESH;
371	    cfg.hold_release_frac = CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
372	    cfg.edge_thresh       = CV_EDGE_THRESH;
373	    PerfLog_EmitDetectorConfig(&cfg);
374	}
375	
376	/* ─── Task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
377	
378	static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
379	{
380	    (void)param;
381	
382	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
383	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
384	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
385	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
386	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
387	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
388	    configASSERT(subscribed);
389	
390	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
391	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
392	
393	    LOG_INFO("CV: cv_marvin_v1 started\r\n");
394	
395	    publish_detector_config();
396	
397	    for (;;)
398	    {
399	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
400	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
401	
402	        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
403	        if (!Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)) { continue; }
404	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                       { continue; }
405	        if (frame.width == 0u || frame.height == 0u)    { continue; }
406	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL){ continue; }
407	
408	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_START, frame.frame_count, 0u);
409	        detect_frame(&frame, bus);
410	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_END, frame.frame_count, 0u);
411	
412	        /* Re-emit detector config at ~1 Hz so a mid-stream host attach
413	         * picks it up within a second of frames flowing. Cheap (~188 B/s
414	         * × 1 record/s). When config becomes runtime-tunable, this becomes
415	         * the heartbeat — on-change emits land via publish_detector_config
416	         * directly from the setter path. */
417	        if ((frame.frame_count % 60u) == 0u) { publish_detector_config(); }
418	
419	        const uint32_t fstride = (uint32_t)frame.width * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
420	
421	        /* STRIKE: the strum trigger zone, copied straight from the frame (no
422	         * sensors there → no rings). */
423	        PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_STRIKE,
424	                                   (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer, fstride,
425	                                   CV_STRIKE_X, CV_STRIKE_Y, CV_STRIKE_W, CV_STRIKE_H);
426	
427	        /* SENSING: copy the sensor row into scratch and (when the overlay sink
428	         * is on) paint the target rings onto the copy before shipping it. The
429	         * source frame is never written, so snapshots and the LVDS panel stay
430	         * clean. Gate the copy on the STRIP mask so it costs nothing when the
431	         * host isn't consuming strips. */
432	        if ((PerfLog_GetEnabledMask() & (1u << PERF_REC_STRIP)) != 0u)
433	        {
434	            const uint8_t *src = (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer
435	                               + (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_Y * fstride
436	                               + (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_X * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
437	            const uint32_t row_bytes = (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_W * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
438	            uint8_t *dst = s_sensing_scratch;
439	            for (uint16_t row = 0u; row < CV_SENSING_H; row++)
440	            {
441	                memcpy(dst, src, row_bytes);
442	                src += fstride;
443	                dst += row_bytes;
444	            }
445	            if ((PerfLog_GetOverlayFlags() & PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP) != 0u)
446	            {
447	                draw_overlay(s_sensing_scratch, CV_SENSING_W, CV_SENSING_H,
448	                             CV_SENSING_X, CV_SENSING_Y);
449	            }
450	            PerfLog_EmitStripPacked(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_SENSING,
451	                                    CV_SENSING_X, CV_SENSING_Y,
452	                                    CV_SENSING_W, CV_SENSING_H, s_sensing_scratch);
453	        }
454	
455	        /* REGION: host-selected sub-region (e.g. the score block), streamed one
456	         * strip per frame when the host has started the stream. No-op otherwise. */
457	        PerfLog_EmitRegionIfEnabled(frame.frame_count, (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer,
458	                                    fstride, frame.width, frame.height);
459	
460	        // /* ~2 Hz signal dump for threshold tuning. hold/edge values shown
461	        //  * vs the 50 threshold, with P/E flags reflecting current state. */
462	        // if ((frame.frame_count % 30u) == 0u)
463	        // {
464	        //     LOG_INFO("CV: G %3d/%3d%c%c R %3d/%3d%c%c Y %3d/%3d%c%c B %3d/%3d%c%c O %3d/%3d%c%c\r\n",
465	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_GREEN],  (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_GREEN],
466	        //              s_pressed[FRET_GREEN]      ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_GREEN]  ? 'E' : '.',
467	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_RED],    (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_RED],
468	        //              s_pressed[FRET_RED]        ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_RED]    ? 'E' : '.',
469	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_YELLOW], (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_YELLOW],
470	        //              s_pressed[FRET_YELLOW]     ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_YELLOW] ? 'E' : '.',
471	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_BLUE],   (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_BLUE],
472	        //              s_pressed[FRET_BLUE]       ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_BLUE]   ? 'E' : '.',
473	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_ORANGE], (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_ORANGE],
474	        //              s_pressed[FRET_ORANGE]     ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_ORANGE] ? 'E' : '.');
475	        // }
476	    }
477	}
478	
479	void CvMarvinV1_Initialize(void)
480	{
481	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(cv_marvin_v1_task,
482	                                       "CvMarvinV1",
483	                                       CV_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
484	                                       NULL,
485	                                       CV_TASK_PRIORITY,
486	                                       s_task_stack,
487	                                       &s_task_tcb);
488	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1, h);
489	}
490
```

```bash
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
import os

SRC = "/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_screens/in_song__training.png"
OUT = os.path.join(os.environ["TMPDIR"], "claude-out", "sp_overlay.png")

sensors = {
    "GREEN":  ((280,311),(293,311),(0,200,0)),
    "RED":    ((317,311),(330,311),(220,0,0)),

}

# strips
x,y,w,h = SENSING

d.text((x+2,y-11),"SENSING",fill=(0,255,255))
x,y,w,h = STRIKE
d.rectangle([x,y,x+w,y+h], outline=(255,0,255), width=1)
d.text((x+2,y-11),"STRIKE",fill=(255,0,255))

def ring(cx,cy,r,col):
    d.ellipse([cx-r,cy-r,cx+r,cy+r], outline=col, width=2)

for name,((hx,hy),(ex,ey),col) in sensors.items():
    # 5x5 sample patch footprint (radius 2)
    d.rectangle([hx-2,hy-2,hx+2,hy+2], outline=(255,255,255))
    d.rectangle([ex-2,ey-2,ex+2,ey+2], outline=col)
    ring(hx,hy,5,(255,255,255))   # hold (brightness) sensor = white
    ring(ex,ey,5,col)             # edge (color) sensor = fret color

im.save(OUT)
print("wrote", OUT)
PY
uv run python $TMPDIR/overlay_sp.py
```

```bash
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
```

```bash
# edge offset sign per fret (SP: G,R,Y toward +x ; B,O toward -x), magnitude ~0.35*pitch
edge_sign={"G":+1,"R":+1,"Y":+1,"B":-1,"O":-1}
strike_y=403
def build(V,rings):
    pts={}

    pitch=(holds["O"]-holds["G"])/4.0
    for f in frets:
        hx=holds[f]; ex=hx+edge_sign[f]*0.35*pitch
        pts[f]=((hx,ys),(ex,ys))
    return pts,ys
def ring(cx,cy,r,col,w=2): d.ellipse([cx-r,cy-r,cx+r,cy+r],outline=col,width=w)
configs={
 "P1":((241,152),[112,170,235,298,358]),
 "P2":((479,152),[390,450,508,562,620]),
}
allcoords={}
for name,(V,rings) in configs.items():
    pts,ys=build(V,rings)
    allcoords[name]=(pts,ys)
    # draw lanes V->ring faint
    for rx in rings:

    # ring markers at strike

    # sensor points

        ring(hx,hy,5,(255,255,255),2)      # hold=white
        ring(ex,ey,5,edgecol[f],2)         # edge=color
    d.text((V[0]-10,V[1]-12),name+" V",fill=(255,255,255))
    d.text((rings[0]-10, int(ys)-14), f"{name} sensors y={int(ys)}", fill=(255,255,255))
out=os.path.join(os.environ["TMPDIR"],"claude-out","p2p_proposal.png"); im.save(out); print(out)
for name,(pts,ys) in allcoords.items():
    print(name,"sensor y=%d"%ys)
    for f in frets:
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 18:30:58Z)**_

```bash

export UV_CACHE_DIR=$TMPDIR/uv-cache
cat > $TMPDIR/trace_rails.py <<'PY'
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np, os
SRC="/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/snapshot-0200.png"
im=np.asarray(Image.open(SRC).convert("RGB")).astype(np.float32)
lum=im.mean(2)
# For each highway, trace outer rails: per row, brightest pixel in a left window and right window.
def trace(rows, lwin, rwin):
    L=[];R=[]
    for y in rows:
        band=lum[y-1:y+2].mean(0)
        lx=lwin[0]+int(np.argmax(band[lwin[0]:lwin[1]]))
        rx=rwin[0]+int(np.argmax(band[rwin[0]:rwin[1]]))
        L.append((lx,y)); R.append((rx,y))
    return np.array(L),np.array(R)
def fit(pts):  # x = a*y+b
    y=pts[:,1]; x=pts[:,0]; a,b=np.polyfit(y,x,1); return a,b
def vanish(aL,bL,aR,bR):
    # aL*y+bL = aR*y+bR
    y=(bR-bL)/(aL-aR); x=aL*y+bL; return x,y
rows=list(range(300,405,7))
# P1: left rail search 95..170, right rail (inner) 300..360
L1,R1=trace(rows,(95,175),(300,360))
aL,bL=fit(L1); aR,bR=fit(R1); vx1,vy1=vanish(aL,bL,aR,bR)
# P2: left(inner) 385..445, right 560..640
L2,R2=trace(rows,(385,450),(555,650))
aL2,bL2=fit(L2); aR2,bR2=fit(R2); vx2,vy2=vanish(aL2,bL2,aR2,bR2)
print("P1 rails L(a,b)=%.3f,%.1f R=%.3f,%.1f  V=(%.0f,%.0f)"%(aL,bL,aR,bR,vx1,vy1))
print("P1 left pts:",L1.tolist())
print("P1 right pts:",R1.tolist())
print("P2 rails L=%.3f,%.1f R=%.3f,%.1f  V=(%.0f,%.0f)"%(aL2,bL2,aR2,bR2,vx2,vy2))
print("P2 left pts:",L2.tolist())
print("P2 right pts:",R2.tolist())
PY
uv run python $TMPDIR/trace_rails.py
```

```bash
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
import os
SRC="/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/snapshot-0200.png"
im=Image.open(SRC).convert("RGB"); d=ImageDraw.Draw(im)
frets=["G","R","Y","B","O"]
col={"G":(0,255,0),"R":(255,0,0),"Y":(255,255,0),"B":(0,120,255),"O":(255,150,0)}
sign={"G":1,"R":1,"Y":1,"B":-1,"O":-1}
strike_y=410; sense_y=311
rings={"P1":[135,180,223,267,310],"P2":[399,443,487,531,574]}
V={"P1":(222,131),"P2":(498,131)}
def ring(cx,cy,r,c,w=2): d.ellipse([cx-r,cy-r,cx+r,cy+r],outline=c,width=w)
out_txt={}
for name in ("P1","P2"):
    vx,vy=V[name]; rs=rings[name]
    s=(sense_y-vy)/(strike_y-vy)
    holds=[vx+s*(rx-vx) for rx in rs]
    pitch=(holds[-1]-holds[0])/4.0
    eoff=0.347*pitch
    # lane lines + strike rings
    for rx,f in zip(rs,frets):
        d.line([vx,vy,rx,strike_y],fill=(60,60,60))
        ring(rx,strike_y,9,col[f],1)
    ring(vx,vy,2,(255,255,255),1)
    hold_i=[]; edge_i=[]
    for f,hx in zip(frets,holds):
        ex=hx+sign[f]*eoff
        ring(hx,sense_y,5,(255,255,255),2)   # hold=white
        ring(ex,sense_y,5,col[f],2)          # edge=color
        hold_i.append(round(hx)); edge_i.append(round(ex))
    out_txt[name]=(hold_i,edge_i,round(pitch,1))
out=os.path.join(os.environ["TMPDIR"],"claude-out","sense_marked.png"); im.save(out); print(out)
for n in ("P1","P2"):
    h,e,p=out_txt[n]; print(f"{n} sense_y=311 pitch={p}\n  hold {list(zip(frets,h))}\n  edge {list(zip(frets,e))}")
PY
```

```text
14	 * A detector is anything that turns observation data into a detector_state_t
15	 * event: cv_marvin_v1 reads captured video frames; adc_fretboard (future)

19	 * Every detector publishes detector_state_t records onto a single FreeRTOS

21	 * consumer in steady state; until it lands a stub task drains the queue so
22	 * producers don't block. */

31	 * because this is also the on-disk format for state.bin (spec §4.6.5). Do not
32	 * reorder fields without bumping the recording schema version. */
33	typedef struct

35	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* master sync token, spec §4.6.4 */
36	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* monotonic, marvin-local */
37	    uint8_t  detector_id;     /* detector_id_t */
38	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
39	    struct
40	    {
41	        uint8_t  pressed;     /* 0/1 hard call */
42	        uint16_t confidence;  /* 0..65535, detector-defined */
43	        uint16_t raw_value;   /* detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc. */
44	    } fret[FRET_COUNT];
45	} detector_state_t;
46

48	 * and (for now) a stub consumer. All detectors start disabled; the app
49	 * must Detector_Enable() each one it wants publishing. Active selection
50	 * defaults to DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1 for symmetry but is independent of
51	 * enabled-state. Call after Video_Initialize so the video frame queue
52	 * can be subscribed to from inside cv_marvin_v1. */
53	void Detector_Initialize(void);
54	
55	/* Producers post records here; consumers (timing pipeline, eventually) read
56	 * them. Returns NULL until Detector_Initialize has run. */

62	 * detectors still consume their input (frames, ADC samples) so input
63	 * queues don't back up; they just don't emit. Bit operations are atomic
64	 * on aligned 32-bit reads; writes use a critical section. */
65	void Detector_Enable(detector_id_t id);
66	void Detector_Disable(detector_id_t id);

72	 * detector_id when it lands; for M1 this is a held setting only. */
73	void          Detector_SetActive(detector_id_t id);
```

```text
48	/* Sensor coordinates in native capture-frame space, anchored to 720×480
49	 * (Wii 480p60 — primary production source). (hx,hy) = brightness sensor,
50	 * (ex,ey) = color-filtered edge sensor; both above the strike line.
51	 * Derived from fret-tuner detect_video.py 1920×1080 defaults via the
52	 * same Elgato HDMI capture, scaled by (3/8, 4/9). Runtime calibration
53	 * UI lands with M6. */
54	typedef struct { uint16_t hx, hy, ex, ey; } sensor_xy_t;

56	static const sensor_xy_t s_sensor_coords[FRET_COUNT] =
57	{
58	    [FRET_GREEN]  = { 280, 311, 293, 311 },
59	    [FRET_RED]    = { 317, 311, 330, 311 },
60	    [FRET_YELLOW] = { 355, 311, 368, 311 },
61	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 393, 311, 380, 311 },
62	    [FRET_ORANGE] = { 430, 311, 417, 311 },
63	};
64	
65	/* Per-fret BGR target / reject weights. Edge signal is
66	 * (target·c − max(0, reject·c)) × sat_ratio. Reject totals exceed 1.0
67	 * so camera-captured whites with color-temperature bias get suppressed,
68	 * not just mathematically perfect whites. */
69	typedef struct { float target[3]; float reject[3]; } color_filter_t;
70	
71	static const color_filter_t s_color_filter[FRET_COUNT] =
72	{
73	    [FRET_GREEN]  = { { 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f }, { 0.7f, 0.0f, 0.7f } },
74	    [FRET_RED]    = { { 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.0f }, { 0.7f, 0.7f, 0.0f } },
75	    [FRET_YELLOW] = { { 0.0f, 0.5f, 0.5f }, { 1.4f, 0.0f, 0.0f } },
76	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { { 1.0f, 0.4f, 0.0f }, { 0.0f, 0.0f, 1.4f } },
77	    [FRET_ORANGE] = { { 0.0f, 0.3f, 0.7f }, { 1.4f, 0.0f, 0.0f } },
78	};
79	
80	/* Per-fret detector state. Private — not on the bus. press_count is the
81	 * rising-edge counter the strum scheduler will eventually consume. */
82	static float    s_hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];
83	static float    s_edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];
84	static bool     s_pressed[FRET_COUNT];
85	static bool     s_edge_active[FRET_COUNT];
86	static uint32_t s_press_count[FRET_COUNT];
87	
88	static StaticQueue_t s_frame_queue_buf;
89	static uint8_t       s_frame_queue_storage[CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(Video_FrameInfo)];
90	
91	/* Tightly-packed scratch for the SENSING strip: the region is row-copied here,
92	 * the rings are painted on the copy, then it's shipped via PerfLog_EmitStripPacked
93	 * — the source capture frame is never written, so snapshots and the LVDS panel
94	 * stay clean. */
95	static uint8_t s_sensing_scratch[CV_SENSING_W * CV_SENSING_H * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL];
96	
97	static StackType_t   s_task_stack[CV_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
98	static StaticTask_t  s_task_tcb;
99	
100	/* ─── Sampling ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
101	
102	/* Average BGR over a (2r+1)×(2r+1) patch centered on (px,py), clipping
103	 * to frame bounds. Center is clamped first so a one-pixel-off calibration
104	 * still produces a reading instead of a silent zero. */
105	static void sample_patch_bgr(const uint8_t *frame, uint16_t fw, uint16_t fh,
106	                             uint16_t px, uint16_t py, float out[3])
107	{
108	    int cx = (int)px;
109	    if (cx < 0)        { cx = 0; }
110	    else if (cx >= fw) { cx = fw - 1; }
111	    int cy = (int)py;
112	    if (cy < 0)        { cy = 0; }
113	    else if (cy >= fh) { cy = fh - 1; }
114	
115	    int r = (int)CV_PATCH_RADIUS;
116	    int x0 = cx - r;       if (x0 < 0)  { x0 = 0; }
117	    int y0 = cy - r;       if (y0 < 0)  { y0 = 0; }
118	    int x1 = cx + r + 1;   if (x1 > fw) { x1 = fw; }
119	    int y1 = cy + r + 1;   if (y1 > fh) { y1 = fh; }
120	
121	    uint32_t sum_b = 0u, sum_g = 0u, sum_r = 0u;
122	    uint32_t row_stride = (uint32_t)fw * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
123	    for (int y = y0; y < y1; y++)
124	    {
125	        const uint8_t *row = frame
126	                           + (uint32_t)y * row_stride
127	                           + (uint32_t)x0 * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
128	        for (int x = x0; x < x1; x++)
129	        {
130	            sum_b += row[0];
131	            sum_g += row[1];
132	            sum_r += row[2];
133	            row   += CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
134	        }
135	    }
136	    uint32_t n = (uint32_t)(x1 - x0) * (uint32_t)(y1 - y0);
137	    out[0] = (float)sum_b / (float)n;
138	    out[1] = (float)sum_g / (float)n;
139	    out[2] = (float)sum_r / (float)n;
140	}
141	
142	/* Max channel — triggers on any color or white. */
143	static float brightness(const float bgr[3])
144	{
145	    float m = bgr[0];
146	    if (bgr[1] > m) { m = bgr[1]; }
147	    if (bgr[2] > m) { m = bgr[2]; }
148	    return m;
149	}
150	
151	/* Color-filtered signal scaled by (max-min)/max so white/gray patches
152	 * produce near-zero signal regardless of camera white balance. */
153	static float color_signal(const float bgr[3], const color_filter_t *f)
154	{
155	    float cmax = brightness(bgr);
156	    if (cmax < 1.0f) { return 0.0f; }
157	    float cmin = bgr[0];
158	    if (bgr[1] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[1]; }
159	    if (bgr[2] < cmin) { cmin = bgr[2]; }
160	    float sat = (cmax - cmin) / cmax;
161	
162	    float target = f->target[0]*bgr[0] + f->target[1]*bgr[1] + f->target[2]*bgr[2];
163	    float reject = f->reject[0]*bgr[0] + f->reject[1]*bgr[1] + f->reject[2]*bgr[2];
164	    if (reject < 0.0f) { reject = 0.0f; }
165	    return (target - reject) * sat;
166	}
167	
168	/* ─── Detection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
169	
170	static void detect_frame(const Video_FrameInfo *frame, QueueHandle_t bus)
171	{
172	    detector_state_t state;
173	    memset(&state, 0, sizeof(state));
174	    state.frame_epoch  = frame->frame_count;
175	    state.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)xTaskGetTickCount() * CV_US_PER_TICK;
176	    state.detector_id  = (uint8_t)DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1;
177	
178	    const float    hold_release = CV_HOLD_THRESH * CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
179	    const uint8_t *fbuf = (const uint8_t *)frame->buffer;
180	    uint16_t       fw   = frame->width;
181	    uint16_t       fh   = frame->height;
182	
183	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
184	    {
185	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
186	        float hold_bgr[3], edge_bgr[3];
187	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.hx, s.hy, hold_bgr);
188	        sample_patch_bgr(fbuf, fw, fh, s.ex, s.ey, edge_bgr);
189	
190	        float hd = brightness(hold_bgr);
191	        float ed = color_signal(edge_bgr, &s_color_filter[i]);
192	        s_hold_dist[i] = hd;
193	        s_edge_dist[i] = ed;
194	
195	        if (!s_pressed[i] && hd > CV_HOLD_THRESH)   { s_pressed[i] = true;  }
196	        else if (s_pressed[i] && hd < hold_release) { s_pressed[i] = false; }
197	
198	        bool edge_on = ed > CV_EDGE_THRESH;
199	        if (edge_on && !s_edge_active[i]) { s_press_count[i]++; }
200	        s_edge_active[i] = edge_on;
201	
202	        state.fret[i].pressed = s_pressed[i] ? 1u : 0u;
203	
204	        /* confidence: edge_dist scaled to 0..65535. ed lives roughly in
205	         * channel-value units (~0..255) so ×256 fills the range. */
206	        float c = ed * 256.0f;
207	        if (c < 0.0f)        { c = 0.0f;     }
208	        if (c > 65535.0f)    { c = 65535.0f; }
209	        state.fret[i].confidence = (uint16_t)c;
210	
211	        /* raw_value: hold_dist (max channel, 0..255). */
212	        float h = hd;
213	        if (h < 0.0f)        { h = 0.0f;     }
214	        if (h > 65535.0f)    { h = 65535.0f; }
215	        state.fret[i].raw_value = (uint16_t)h;
216	    }
217	
218	    (void)xQueueSend(bus, &state, 0);
219	
220	    /* Mirror the same per-frame decision into the perf-log so offline tools
221	     * (marvin-perf, export-ml) can join detector ground truth with sensor
222	     * input. raw_value/confidence already scale 0..65535 to match the
223	     * perf-log struct. masks are LSB-first per fret_t. Default-disabled at
224	     * boot like the other high-rate types; host enables via SET_TYPE_MASK. */
225	    uint16_t hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];
226	    uint16_t edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];
227	    uint8_t  pressed_mask = 0u;
228	    uint8_t  edge_active_mask = 0u;
229	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
230	    {
231	        hold_dist[i] = state.fret[i].raw_value;
232	        edge_dist[i] = state.fret[i].confidence;
233	        if (s_pressed[i])     { pressed_mask     |= (uint8_t)(1u << i); }
234	        if (s_edge_active[i]) { edge_active_mask |= (uint8_t)(1u << i); }
235	    }
236	    PerfLog_EmitDetector(state.frame_epoch, hold_dist, edge_dist,
237	                         pressed_mask, edge_active_mask);
238	}
239	
240	/* ─── Calibration overlay ──────────────────────────────────────────────── */
241	
242	/* Paints a per-fret ring at each sample point onto a target buffer (the SENSING
243	 * strip copy), translated by the buffer's origin in frame space, so the user
244	 * can visually verify alignment with on-screen note targets in the host viewer.
245	 * The source capture frame is never touched. The ring radius is outside the 5×5
246	 * sample patch; the detector has already sampled by the time this runs. */
247	#define CV_OVERLAY_RING_R    4u
248	
249	static const uint8_t s_overlay_hold_bgr[3] = { 255u, 255u, 255u };  /* white */
250	static const uint8_t s_overlay_edge_bgr[FRET_COUNT][3] =
251	{   /* { B,    G,    R } */
252	    [FRET_GREEN]  = {   0u, 255u,   0u },
253	    [FRET_RED]    = {   0u,   0u, 255u },
254	    [FRET_YELLOW] = {   0u, 255u, 255u },
255	    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 255u,   0u,   0u },
256	    [FRET_ORANGE] = {   0u, 165u, 255u },
257	};
258	
259	static inline void put_pixel_bgr(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
260	                                 int x, int y,
261	                                 uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
262	{
263	    if (x < 0 || x >= fw || y < 0 || y >= fh) { return; }
264	    uint8_t *p = frame + ((uint32_t)y * (uint32_t)fw + (uint32_t)x) * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
265	    p[0] = b; p[1] = g; p[2] = r;
266	}
267	
268	/* Bresenham midpoint circle — perimeter only, 8-way symmetric. */
269	static void draw_ring(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
270	                      int cx, int cy, int radius,
271	                      uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
272	{
273	    int x = radius, y = 0, err = 0;
274	    while (x >= y)
275	    {
276	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy + y, b, g, r);
277	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy + x, b, g, r);
278	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy + x, b, g, r);
279	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy + y, b, g, r);
280	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - x, cy - y, b, g, r);
281	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx - y, cy - x, b, g, r);
282	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + y, cy - x, b, g, r);
283	        put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + x, cy - y, b, g, r);
284	        y++;
285	        err += 1 + 2 * y;
286	        if (2 * (err - x) + 1 > 0) { x--; err += 1 - 2 * x; }
287	    }
288	}
289	
290	static void draw_filled_disk(uint8_t *frame, int fw, int fh,
291	                             int cx, int cy, int radius,
292	                             uint8_t b, uint8_t g, uint8_t r)
293	{
294	    int rr = radius * radius;
295	    for (int dy = -radius; dy <= radius; dy++)
296	    {
297	        for (int dx = -radius; dx <= radius; dx++)
298	        {
299	            if (dx * dx + dy * dy <= rr)
300	            {
301	                put_pixel_bgr(frame, fw, fh, cx + dx, cy + dy, b, g, r);
302	            }
303	        }
304	    }
305	}
306	
307	/* Per-fret marker: position ring (always) + center dot when the matching
308	 * detector is firing this frame. Hold dot = white => brightness over
309	 * threshold. Edge dot = fret color => color-filtered edge over threshold.
310	 * Lets the user watch chatter live: a stable note should show a steady
311	 * dot for the hold duration; a strum window should flash the edge dot
312	 * once. Constant flicker = noise pushing thresholds. */
313	#define CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R     1u
314	
315	/* Draw the per-fret rings/dots into `buf` (bw×bh, tightly packed), with sensor
316	 * coords translated by the buffer's frame-space origin (ox, oy). Pixels falling
317	 * outside the buffer are clipped by put_pixel_bgr. */
318	static void draw_overlay(uint8_t *buf, uint16_t bw, uint16_t bh,
319	                         uint16_t ox, uint16_t oy)
320	{
321	    int w = (int)bw, h = (int)bh;
322	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
323	    {
324	        sensor_xy_t s = s_sensor_coords[i];
325	        const uint8_t *e = s_overlay_edge_bgr[i];
326	        int hx = (int)s.hx - (int)ox, hy = (int)s.hy - (int)oy;
327	        int ex = (int)s.ex - (int)ox, ey = (int)s.ey - (int)oy;
328	
329	        draw_ring(buf, w, h, hx, hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
330	                  s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
331	        draw_ring(buf, w, h, ex, ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_RING_R,
332	                  e[0], e[1], e[2]);
333	
334	        if (s_pressed[i])
335	        {
336	            draw_filled_disk(buf, w, h, hx, hy, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
337	                             s_overlay_hold_bgr[0], s_overlay_hold_bgr[1], s_overlay_hold_bgr[2]);
338	        }
339	        if (s_edge_active[i])
340	        {
341	            draw_filled_disk(buf, w, h, ex, ey, (int)CV_OVERLAY_DOT_R,
342	                             e[0], e[1], e[2]);
343	        }
344	    }
345	}
346	
347	/* ─── Detector-config publish ──────────────────────────────────────────── */
348	
349	/* Snapshot the static cv_marvin_v1 tables (sample coords, thresholds,
350	 * color filter weights) into a wire record. Static today; when M6
351	 * calibration UI lands and these become runtime-tunable, this function
352	 * is the single point that re-publishes after each tweak. */
353	static void publish_detector_config(void)
354	{
355	    perf_rec_detector_config_t cfg;
356	    memset(&cfg, 0, sizeof(cfg));
357	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
358	    {
359	        cfg.sensor_hx[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].hx;
360	        cfg.sensor_hy[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].hy;
361	        cfg.sensor_ex[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].ex;
362	        cfg.sensor_ey[i]      = s_sensor_coords[i].ey;
363	        cfg.color_target_b[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[0];
364	        cfg.color_target_g[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[1];
365	        cfg.color_target_r[i] = s_color_filter[i].target[2];
366	        cfg.color_reject_b[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[0];
367	        cfg.color_reject_g[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[1];
368	        cfg.color_reject_r[i] = s_color_filter[i].reject[2];
369	    }
370	    cfg.hold_thresh       = CV_HOLD_THRESH;
371	    cfg.hold_release_frac = CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC;
372	    cfg.edge_thresh       = CV_EDGE_THRESH;
373	    PerfLog_EmitDetectorConfig(&cfg);
374	}
375	
376	/* ─── Task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
377	
378	static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
379	{
380	    (void)param;
381	
382	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
383	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
384	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
385	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
386	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
387	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
388	    configASSERT(subscribed);
389	
390	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
391	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
392	
393	    LOG_INFO("CV: cv_marvin_v1 started\r\n");
394	
395	    publish_detector_config();
396	
397	    for (;;)
398	    {
399	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
400	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
401	
402	        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
403	        if (!Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)) { continue; }
404	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                       { continue; }
405	        if (frame.width == 0u || frame.height == 0u)    { continue; }
406	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL){ continue; }
407	
408	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_START, frame.frame_count, 0u);
409	        detect_frame(&frame, bus);
410	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_END, frame.frame_count, 0u);
411	
412	        /* Re-emit detector config at ~1 Hz so a mid-stream host attach
413	         * picks it up within a second of frames flowing. Cheap (~188 B/s
414	         * × 1 record/s). When config becomes runtime-tunable, this becomes
415	         * the heartbeat — on-change emits land via publish_detector_config
416	         * directly from the setter path. */
417	        if ((frame.frame_count % 60u) == 0u) { publish_detector_config(); }
418	
419	        const uint32_t fstride = (uint32_t)frame.width * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
420	
421	        /* STRIKE: the strum trigger zone, copied straight from the frame (no
422	         * sensors there → no rings). */
423	        PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_STRIKE,
424	                                   (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer, fstride,
425	                                   CV_STRIKE_X, CV_STRIKE_Y, CV_STRIKE_W, CV_STRIKE_H);
426	
427	        /* SENSING: copy the sensor row into scratch and (when the overlay sink
428	         * is on) paint the target rings onto the copy before shipping it. The
429	         * source frame is never written, so snapshots and the LVDS panel stay
430	         * clean. Gate the copy on the STRIP mask so it costs nothing when the
431	         * host isn't consuming strips. */
432	        if ((PerfLog_GetEnabledMask() & (1u << PERF_REC_STRIP)) != 0u)
433	        {
434	            const uint8_t *src = (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer
435	                               + (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_Y * fstride
436	                               + (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_X * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
437	            const uint32_t row_bytes = (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_W * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
438	            uint8_t *dst = s_sensing_scratch;
439	            for (uint16_t row = 0u; row < CV_SENSING_H; row++)
440	            {
441	                memcpy(dst, src, row_bytes);
442	                src += fstride;
443	                dst += row_bytes;
444	            }
445	            if ((PerfLog_GetOverlayFlags() & PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP) != 0u)
446	            {
447	                draw_overlay(s_sensing_scratch, CV_SENSING_W, CV_SENSING_H,
448	                             CV_SENSING_X, CV_SENSING_Y);
449	            }
450	            PerfLog_EmitStripPacked(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_SENSING,
451	                                    CV_SENSING_X, CV_SENSING_Y,
452	                                    CV_SENSING_W, CV_SENSING_H, s_sensing_scratch);
453	        }
454	
455	        /* REGION: host-selected sub-region (e.g. the score block), streamed one
456	         * strip per frame when the host has started the stream. No-op otherwise. */
457	        PerfLog_EmitRegionIfEnabled(frame.frame_count, (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer,
458	                                    fstride, frame.width, frame.height);
459	
460	        // /* ~2 Hz signal dump for threshold tuning. hold/edge values shown
461	        //  * vs the 50 threshold, with P/E flags reflecting current state. */
462	        // if ((frame.frame_count % 30u) == 0u)
463	        // {
464	        //     LOG_INFO("CV: G %3d/%3d%c%c R %3d/%3d%c%c Y %3d/%3d%c%c B %3d/%3d%c%c O %3d/%3d%c%c\r\n",
465	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_GREEN],  (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_GREEN],
466	        //              s_pressed[FRET_GREEN]      ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_GREEN]  ? 'E' : '.',
467	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_RED],    (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_RED],
468	        //              s_pressed[FRET_RED]        ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_RED]    ? 'E' : '.',
469	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_YELLOW], (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_YELLOW],
470	        //              s_pressed[FRET_YELLOW]     ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_YELLOW] ? 'E' : '.',
471	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_BLUE],   (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_BLUE],
472	        //              s_pressed[FRET_BLUE]       ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_BLUE]   ? 'E' : '.',
473	        //              (int)s_hold_dist[FRET_ORANGE], (int)s_edge_dist[FRET_ORANGE],
474	        //              s_pressed[FRET_ORANGE]     ? 'P' : '.', s_edge_active[FRET_ORANGE] ? 'E' : '.');
475	        // }
476	    }
477	}
478	
479	void CvMarvinV1_Initialize(void)
480	{
481	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(cv_marvin_v1_task,
482	                                       "CvMarvinV1",
483	                                       CV_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
484	                                       NULL,
485	                                       CV_TASK_PRIORITY,
486	                                       s_task_stack,
487	                                       &s_task_tcb);
488	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1, h);
489	}
```

```text
1	#ifndef VIDEO_H
2	#define VIDEO_H
3	
4	#include <stdbool.h>
5	#include <stdint.h>
6	
7	#include "FreeRTOS.h"
8	#include "queue.h"
9	
10	/* Video pipeline: HDMI source → TC358743 bridge → CSI-2 → CSI2DC → ISC →
11	 * DDR. This module is the capture *producer*: it owns its own FreeRTOS task
12	 * (tc358743, isc_capture, capture state machine) and fans completed frames out
13	 * to subscribers from the ISC IRQ via xQueueSendFromISR.
14	 *
15	 * Display (the HEO hardware layer that scans a captured frame to the LCD) is
16	 * owned by the compositor (ui_manager), NOT here — capture and display are fully
17	 * independent (the detector/gameplay consume frames whether or not HEO is shown).
18	 * The module notifies the compositor through two registered callbacks so the
19	 * compositor can own all HEO/BASE register writes while keeping the timing this
20	 * task/IRQ already has:
21	 *   - a display-reconcile callback, called each task tick with the current source
22	 *     validity + size, so the compositor can (re)bind/unbind HEO in task context;
23	 *   - a frame-latch callback, called from the ISC IRQ with the freshest completed
24	 *     buffer address, so the compositor can latch HEO to the newest ring slot.
25	 *
26	 * Defaults at Initialize: capture disabled, no callbacks. */
27	
28	void Video_Initialize(void);
29	
30	/* Capture chain control. ENABLE: arm ISC + bridge stream when source
31	 * is locked, re-arm on every lost/regain cycle. DISABLE: stop ISC +
32	 * stream and stay off regardless of lock state. */
33	void Video_CaptureEnable(void);
34	void Video_CaptureDisable(void);
35	
36	/* Register the compositor's HEO hooks (see the module note above). Both are
37	 * optional (NULL = no display). Set before the video task starts.
38	 *   frame-latch: fires in ISC IRQ context with the just-completed buffer address.
39	 *   reconcile:   fires each task tick with (source_valid, src_w, src_h). */
40	void Video_SetFrameLatchCallback(void (*cb)(uint32_t buffer_addr));
41	void Video_SetDisplayReconcileCallback(void (*cb)(bool source_valid,
42	                                                  uint16_t src_w, uint16_t src_h));
43	
44	/* Frame metadata delivered to subscribers on every captured frame. */
45	typedef struct
46	{
47	    void    *buffer;          /* pointer to most-recent complete frame in DDR */
48	    uint32_t frame_count;     /* monotonic since last ISC start */
49	    uint16_t width;
50	    uint16_t height;
51	    uint16_t bytes_per_pixel;
52	} Video_FrameInfo;
53	
54	/* Subscribe a queue to frame-ready events. The video module sends a
55	 * Video_FrameInfo from the ISC frame-done IRQ via xQueueSendFromISR
56	 * each time a frame completes to DDR — fanned out to every subscribed
57	 * queue. Create the queue with:
58	 *   QueueHandle_t q = xQueueCreate(N, sizeof(Video_FrameInfo));
59	 *
60	 * Per-subscriber depth chooses the back-pressure policy. Depth 1 means
61	 * "process most recent frame, drop the rest" — when a frame arrives and
62	 * the queue is full, the IRQ's xQueueSendFromISR returns errQUEUE_FULL
63	 * and the frame is dropped for that subscriber. Deeper queues preserve
64	 * frames at the cost of memory and added latency. Each subscriber chooses
65	 * independently.
66	 *
67	 * The Video_FrameInfo.buffer pointer reflects the buffer that *just*
68	 * completed (one of the descriptor-ring slots). With NUM_BUFFERS > 2 a
69	 * subscriber can hold the pointer for multiple frame-times before the
70	 * ring laps it; with NUM_BUFFERS = 2 the buffer is overwritten on the
71	 * second-next frame.
72	 *
73	 * Returns false if the subscriber table is full. Calling with a queue
74	 * already in the table is a no-op success. Up to VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS
75	 * concurrent subscribers (currently 4). */
76	bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);
77	
78	/* Remove a queue from the subscriber list. Returns false if not found. */
79	bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q);
80	
81	/* Synchronous read of the current frame state. Doesn't block. May
82	 * report frame_count = 0 / buffer = NULL if capture has never armed. */
83	void Video_GetFrameInfo(Video_FrameInfo *info);
84	
85	/* Detected active-picture rectangle within the captured frame.
86	 *
87	 * A component→HDMI source (the Wii bridge) frames its active raster with dead
88	 * black bars whose thickness varies by console/converter, so the active area is
89	 * detected at runtime — the union of the bright-pixel bounds over the first
90	 * frames after capture arms, locked once it clears a minimum size. Detection is
91	 * one-shot per capture arm (reset on re-arm / source-size change).
92	 *
93	 * Returns true with the locked rect (x,y = top-left offset, w,h = size, all in
94	 * source pixels) once detected; false until then, filling *x=*y=0 and *w/*h =
95	 * the full frame — a safe full-frame fallback so callers always get a usable
96	 * rect. Any NULL out-param is skipped. */
97	bool Video_GetActiveRect(uint16_t *x, uint16_t *y, uint16_t *w, uint16_t *h);
98	
99	#endif
```

```text
91	/* Fired by the UI boot task the instant the splash is on screen (registered via
92	 * UiManager_SetSplashShownCallback). Brings up the runtime services in parallel with
93	 * the behind-the-splash screen painting, so the system is warm by the time the
94	 * dashboard is revealed. Video capture is deliberately NOT armed here: the CSI-2
95	 * D-PHY must be brought up against settled display clocks and away from the boot-time
96	 * contention, or it locks marginally and the lanes sit in stop-state (~0 fps). The
97	 * compositor arms capture at the end of the boot sequence instead (see ui_manager). */
98	static void app_on_splash_shown(void)
99	{
100	    App_StartServices();
101	}
102	
103	// *****************************************************************************
104	// *****************************************************************************
105	// Section: Application Initialization and State Machine Functions

113	  Remarks:
114	    See prototype in app.h.
```
