116	
117	void APP_Initialize ( void )
118	{
119	    appData.state = APP_STATE_INIT;
120	
121	    /* Logging shim: thin wrapper over libc printf with severity filter
122	     * and FreeRTOS-aware locking. Initialized first so subsequent code
123	     * (including video task startup) can use LOG_*. Default level is
124	     * INFO; flip to DEBUG via log_set_level() to enable verbose. */
125	    log_init(LOG_LEVEL_INFO);
126	
127	    /* UI manager: the UI orchestrator + compositor. Assigns the per-screen canvas
128	     * surfaces (pre-scheduler) and creates the boot task that runs the bring-up
129	     * sequence (splash → screens → reveal) once the scheduler is up. The callback
130	     * is registered first so the boot task can fire it the moment the splash is on
131	     * screen — that's our cue to start everything else (see app_on_splash_shown). */
132	    UiManager_SetSplashShownCallback(app_on_splash_shown);
133	    UiManager_Initialize();
134	
135	    /* Per-frame performance log: producer-side queues only. Init here so any
136	     * producer that posts has a valid queue; the drain task spawns later in
137	     * App_StartServices (it sits above the SD tasks in priority). */
138	    PerfLog_Initialize();
139	
140	    /* SD-card storage: sets up mount state only (no I/O here — the SDMMC driver
141	     * hasn't analyzed the card pre-scheduler). The splash module mounts it. */
142	    Storage_Initialize();
143	
144	    /* Per-player results log (CSV on the card). State only here; file I/O is
145	     * lazy (mounts on demand) from Results_Append / the player/scores/results
146	     * console commands. */
147	    Results_Initialize();
148	
149	    /* Song catalog (labels keyed by the recognizer's (setlist,index)). State
150	     * only here; the CSV is lazy-loaded from the card on first lookup / the
151	     * `catalog` console command. A missing catalog degrades to "Unknown song"
152	     * and never affects recognition. See game/catalog.h. */
153	    Catalog_Initialize();
154	
155	    /* Album-artwork cache (cover art keyed by (setlist,index)). State only here;
156	     * the covers are decoded from the card into static RGB888 caches by
157	     * Art_LoadAll(), called from the UI boot task during the splash. See
158	     * game/art.h. */
159	    Art_Initialize();
160	
161	    /* The video pipeline, detector, actuator links, gameplay observer, console,
162	     * and perf-log drain are NOT started here — they spawn tasks at priorities
163	     * above the SDMMC/filesystem tasks, so starting them during boot would starve
164	     * the card mount and splash load. App_StartServices brings them up, fired from
165	     * app_on_splash_shown the instant the splash is displayed. */
166	}
167	
168	
169	/* Bring up the runtime subsystems deferred out of APP_Initialize. Called by the
170	 * loader once the splash is up and the dashboard revealed, so none of these
171	 * higher-priority tasks preempt the SDMMC/filesystem tasks during the card mount
172	 * + splash render. Order honors the dependencies: Video first (it owns the frame
173	 * queue the detector + gameplay observer subscribe to from their tasks). */
174	void App_StartServices(void)
175	{
176	    /* Video capture pipeline (ISC, TC358743, HEO unbind) + capture/display
177	     * state machine + bridge-status polling. Spawns VideoTask. */
178	    Video_Initialize();
179	
180	    /* Reference detector (cv_marvin_v1) + detector-state bus. Must follow
181	     * Video_Initialize since cv_marvin_v1 subscribes to the video frame queue
182	     * from inside its task. Detectors default disabled; enable + select the
183	     * active one for the timing pipeline. */
184	    Detector_Initialize();
185	    Detector_Enable(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);
186	    Detector_SetActive(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1);
187	
188	    /* M2 actuator path: fretboard_link owns the submit queue + FLEXCOM1 USART
189	     * writer and the RX parse task (and brings up the T1S link). */
190	    FretboardLink_Initialize();
191	
192	#if (MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT == FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT_T1S)
193	    /* fauxmote command link (ESP32 Wiimote emulator) on FLEXCOM1 — free while the
194	     * guitar node rides T1S. Mirrors every gameplay mask (FretboardLink_Send taps
195	     * Fauxmote_SendGuitarMask). Must precede the mask producers below. */
196	    Fauxmote_Initialize();
197	#endif
198	
199	    /* timing_pipeline runs the chord-window + strum scheduler against the
200	     * active detector and pushes the resulting 7-bit mask through
201	     * FretboardLink_Send. */
202	    TimingPipeline_Initialize();
203	
204	    /* manual_control is a peer producer for direct UI-driven actuation. UI
205	     * buttons are authored in Microchip Graphics Composer; the generated
206	     * screenShow registers the callbacks defined in ui/manual_input.c, so no
207	     * explicit bind step is needed here. */
208	    ManualControl_Initialize();
209	
210	    /* Game-state observer (spec §4.8, M9): a video-frame consumer that classifies
211	     * the current GH3 screen. It subscribes to the video frame queue from its task
212	     * (so it follows Video_Initialize) but observation is synchronous and on-demand —
213	     * it does NOTHING until GameplayEngine_Observe() blocks for a fresh classification
214	     * (called by the game controller). There is no free-running scan: the song_select
215	     * match is ~tens of ms of soft-float on this FPU-less core, and running it unasked
216	     * pegged prio-4 and froze the UI. The dashboard uses the touch Selection; the bus
217	     * has no other consumer. */
218	    GameplayEngine_Initialize();
219	
220	    /* M10 game-state controller: START (dashboard button / `play` console command)
221	     * navigates GH3 to the selected song+difficulty, then hands off to the CV
222	     * detector. Follows the gameplay engine + actuator producers it drives. */
223	    GameController_Initialize();
224	
225	    /* Interactive operator console on FLEXCOM2 (115200), separate from the DBGU
226	     * log channel. Started after the actuator/detector modules so its commands
227	     * can drive their setters. */
228	    Console_Initialize();
229	
230	    /* Per-frame perf-log drain task, launched last so every producer's queue
231	     * handle is already valid when the first records hit the sink. */
232	    PerfLog_Start();
233	
234	    /* Liveness + resource monitor: a just-above-idle task that heartbeats to
235	     * SD + DBGU every minute and dumps the per-task stack table every 10 min,
236	     * so an unattended freeze can be located in time and inspected after the
237	     * fact. Started last — it only observes. See health/health_monitor.h. */
238	    HealthMonitor_Initialize();
239	}

246	  Remarks:

249	
250	void APP_Tasks ( void )
251	{
252	    /* Heap_1 free space at the end of APP_Initialize (heap_1 never frees — free
253	     * space only shrinks). The runtime subsystems spawn later via
254	     * App_StartServices, so this is the pre-services floor, not the final one.
255	     * Surfaces remaining headroom so an allocation walking into the wall is
256	     * visible rather than a silent malloc-failed spin. */
257	    LOG_INFO("freertos heap: %u bytes free\r\n", (unsigned)xPortGetFreeHeapSize());
258	
259	    /* APP is a one-shot launcher — task creation happened in APP_Initialize.
260	     * Self-delete here so the (1024-word) stack and TCB are released to the
261	     * idle task. The MCC-generated lAPP_Tasks loop will not iterate again
262	     * because vTaskDelete(NULL) never returns to its caller. */
263	    vTaskDelete(NULL);
264	}

16	 * remain unaffected if perf-log vanishes.

19	 * xQueueSendFromISR; the task variants use xQueueSend with zero block
20	 * time. Choose by call site — passing the wrong one will not corrupt
21	 * state but may misuse the higher_priority_task_woken pathway. */

1	#ifndef DETECTOR_H
2	#define DETECTOR_H
3	
4	#include <stdint.h>
5	#include <stdbool.h>
6	
7	#include "FreeRTOS.h"
8	#include "queue.h"
9	
10	#include "game/fret.h"
11	
12	/* Detector subsystem — see firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md §4.2.
13	 *
14	 * A detector is anything that turns observation data into a detector_state_t
15	 * event: cv_marvin_v1 reads captured video frames; adc_fretboard (future)
16	 * reads UART-streamed ADC samples from the fretboard MCU; off-board detectors
17	 * may feed state in over UART/Ethernet.
18	 *
19	 * Every detector publishes detector_state_t records onto a single FreeRTOS
20	 * queue (the "detector-state bus"). The timing pipeline (§4.4) is the sole
21	 * consumer in steady state; until it lands a stub task drains the queue so
22	 * producers don't block. */
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	    DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1  = 0,
27	    DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1,
28	} detector_id_t;
29	
30	/* Canonical record. Layout is fixed-width / naturally aligned / little-endian
31	 * because this is also the on-disk format for state.bin (spec §4.6.5). Do not
32	 * reorder fields without bumping the recording schema version. */
33	typedef struct
34	{
35	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* master sync token, spec §4.6.4 */
36	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* monotonic, marvin-local */
37	    uint8_t  detector_id;     /* detector_id_t */
38	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
39	    struct
40	    {
41	        uint8_t  pressed;     /* 0/1 hard call */
42	        uint16_t confidence;  /* 0..65535, detector-defined */
43	        uint16_t raw_value;   /* detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc. */
44	    } fret[FRET_COUNT];
45	} detector_state_t;
46	
47	/* Brings up the detector-state bus queue, the cv_marvin_v1 detector task,
48	 * and (for now) a stub consumer. All detectors start disabled; the app
49	 * must Detector_Enable() each one it wants publishing. Active selection
50	 * defaults to DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1 for symmetry but is independent of
51	 * enabled-state. Call after Video_Initialize so the video frame queue
52	 * can be subscribed to from inside cv_marvin_v1. */
53	void Detector_Initialize(void);
54	
55	/* Producers post records here; consumers (timing pipeline, eventually) read
56	 * them. Returns NULL until Detector_Initialize has run. */
57	QueueHandle_t Detector_BusQueue(void);
58	
59	/* Per-detector enable: controls whether a detector publishes records onto
60	 * the bus. Multiple detectors may be enabled simultaneously — recording
61	 * (§4.6) snoops everything for side-by-side training data. Disabled
62	 * detectors still consume their input (frames, ADC samples) so input
63	 * queues don't back up; they just don't emit. Bit operations are atomic
64	 * on aligned 32-bit reads; writes use a critical section. */
65	void Detector_Enable(detector_id_t id);
66	void Detector_Disable(detector_id_t id);
67	bool Detector_IsEnabled(detector_id_t id);
68	
69	/* Active selector: which detector's records the timing pipeline (§4.4)
70	 * acts on. Only one active at a time, irrespective of how many are
71	 * enabled. The timing pipeline is responsible for filtering by
72	 * detector_id when it lands; for M1 this is a held setting only. */
73	void          Detector_SetActive(detector_id_t id);
74	detector_id_t Detector_GetActive(void);
75	
76	#endif
77

1	#ifndef GAMEPLAY_CLASSIFY_H
2	#define GAMEPLAY_CLASSIFY_H
3	
4	#include <stdint.h>
5	
6	/* Pure screen-classification math, ported from the host prototype
7	 * (tools/gameplay) and driven by the generated game/gameplay_metadata.h tables.
8	 * Deliberately free of FreeRTOS / video dependencies so it compiles and can be
9	 * numerically cross-checked against the Python classifier on a host, then links
10	 * unchanged into the firmware game_task (gameplay_engine.c). Not reentrant — it
11	 * uses a static fingerprint scratch; only the single observer task calls it. */
12	
13	/* Classify a BGR888 frame (3 B/pixel, width*height). Returns a GP_SCREEN_*
14	 * index (see gameplay_metadata.h) or GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN. The frame must be at the
15	 * canonical GP_CANON_W × GP_CANON_H (no resize on-target — the Wii is 720×480);
16	 * any other size returns GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN. When non-NULL, *out_best_dist and
17	 * *out_margin receive the nearest-centroid L1 distance and the second-best−best
18	 * margin. */
19	uint8_t gp_classify(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height,
20	                    int32_t *out_best_dist, int32_t *out_margin);
21	
22	/* Compute the raw fingerprint (GP_FP_LEN uint8 values) for a canonical frame,
23	 * without classifying — exposed for the host cross-validation test. Returns 0
24	 * on success, non-zero if the frame isn't the canonical size. */
25	int gp_fingerprint(const uint8_t *frame, int width, int height, uint8_t *out);
26	
27	#endif

4	#include <stdbool.h>
5	
6	/* M10 — GH3 game-state controller. On Start it reads the committed Selection
7	 * (game/selection.h), navigates the Training/Practice menu path to a FULL SONG /
8	 * FULL SPEED playthrough of the selected song at the selected difficulty, then
9	 * enables the CV timing pipeline so the detector plays it (the timing pipeline's
10	 * in-song gate arms actuation automatically once the observer sees GP_SCREEN_in_song).
11	 *
12	 * Closed-loop and observation-driven: every step verifies the screen the gameplay
13	 * engine reports and recovers with RED on a mismatch — a port of the offline
14	 * NavController in tools/gameplay. Menu inputs are guitar fret/strum masks sent via
15	 * FretboardLink_Send, so they drive both the T1S guitar and fauxmote. See
16	 * firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md.
17	 *
18	 * Initialize once in App_StartServices, after the gameplay engine, timing pipeline,
19	 * and manual_control (it drives their setters). */
20	
21	void GameController_Initialize(void);   /* spawn the controller task (idle) */
22	void GameController_Start(void);        /* begin a run from the committed Selection */
23	void GameController_Stop(void);         /* abort/stop: release the guitar, CV off */
24	bool GameController_IsBusy(void);       /* true while a run is navigating/playing */
25	
26	/* Single status-text observer (e.g. the dashboard Status label), invoked on each
27	 * phase change with a short string ("READY"/"NAVIGATING"/"PLAYING"/"FAILED"/…).
28	 * NULL clears it. Mirrors Selection_SetObserver. */
29	void GameController_SetStatusObserver(void (*cb)(const char *text));
30	
31	#endif /* MARVIN_GAME_CONTROLLER_H */

1	#ifndef GAMEPLAY_ENGINE_H
2	#define GAMEPLAY_ENGINE_H
3	
4	#include <stdint.h>
5	#include <stdbool.h>
6	
7	#include "FreeRTOS.h"
8	#include "queue.h"
9	
10	/* Game-state observer — see firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md §4.8 (M9).
11	 *
12	 * A video-frame consumer (not a detector): it classifies which GH3 screen the
13	 * captured frame shows and publishes typed game_state_t events on its own bus
14	 * (xGameStateQueue), kept separate from the detector-state bus per the §4.2
15	 * multi-detector decision. The recognizer data (region grid, per-class
16	 * centroids, thresholds) is the host-proven metadata frozen into
17	 * game/gameplay_metadata.h by `gameplay export-c`.
18	 *
19	 * Phase 1 (this module): screen classification only. Selection/song readers
20	 * (Phase 2) and the navigator/controller (Phase 3, M10) build on this. */
21	
22	typedef struct
23	{
24	    uint32_t frame_epoch;   /* master sync token, = Video_FrameInfo.frame_count */
25	    uint64_t timestamp_us;  /* monotonic, marvin-local */
26	    uint8_t  screen;        /* GP_SCREEN_* index, or GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN */
27	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
28	    int32_t  best_dist;     /* L1 to the nearest centroid */
29	    int32_t  margin;        /* second-best − best (confidence) */
30	    int16_t  selection;     /* static-list cell, song-template index, or -1 (none) */
31	    int32_t  score;         /* in-song score read (training font), or -1 (not in_song) */
32	    uint8_t  multiplier;    /* in-song score multiplier 1..4, or 0 (not in_song) */
33	    uint16_t streak;        /* in-song note streak (monotonic tracker), 0 = not shown / <~25 */
34	} game_state_t;
35	
36	/* Brings up the game-state bus queue and the observer task. The observer
37	 * subscribes to the video frame queue from inside its task, so call this after
38	 * Video_Initialize. The task idles (draining frames, ~0 CPU) until a
39	 * GameplayEngine_Observe() request arrives. */
40	void GameplayEngine_Initialize(void);
41	
42	/* Game-state event bus. Consumers (operator UI, the controller at M10) read
43	 * here. Returns NULL until GameplayEngine_Initialize has run. */
44	QueueHandle_t GameplayEngine_BusQueue(void);
45	
46	/* Synchronous observation: request a classification of a fresh frame and block
47	 * until the result arrives, or timeout_ms elapses. On success writes the
48	 * {screen, selection, …} into *out and returns true; returns false on timeout or
49	 * a NULL out. This is the only way to read screen state — there is no retained
50	 * "current screen" to poll, so a read never returns stale state.
51	 *
52	 * The classified frame is guaranteed to have been captured after the request
53	 * (the task skips the in-hand frame, which predates it). The sole requester is
54	 * the game controller; do not call concurrently from multiple tasks.
55	 *
56	 * NOTE: GH3 menus take several frames to transition (cursor animation, fades, a
57	 * `loading` screen), so the controller settles/re-observes rather than trusting
58	 * one read the instant after actuating. */
59	bool GameplayEngine_Observe(game_state_t *out, uint32_t timeout_ms);
60	
61	#endif
62

1	#ifndef DETECTOR_H
2	#define DETECTOR_H
3	
4	#include <stdint.h>
5	#include <stdbool.h>
6	
7	#include "FreeRTOS.h"
8	#include "queue.h"
9	
10	#include "game/fret.h"
11	
12	/* Detector subsystem — see firmware/marvin/docs/spec.md §4.2.
13	 *
14	 * A detector is anything that turns observation data into a detector_state_t
15	 * event: cv_marvin_v1 reads captured video frames; adc_fretboard (future)
16	 * reads UART-streamed ADC samples from the fretboard MCU; off-board detectors
17	 * may feed state in over UART/Ethernet.
18	 *
19	 * Every detector publishes detector_state_t records onto a single FreeRTOS
20	 * queue (the "detector-state bus"). The timing pipeline (§4.4) is the sole
21	 * consumer in steady state; until it lands a stub task drains the queue so
22	 * producers don't block. */
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	    DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1  = 0,
27	    DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1,
28	} detector_id_t;
29	
30	/* Canonical record. Layout is fixed-width / naturally aligned / little-endian
31	 * because this is also the on-disk format for state.bin (spec §4.6.5). Do not
32	 * reorder fields without bumping the recording schema version. */
33	typedef struct
34	{
35	    uint32_t frame_epoch;     /* master sync token, spec §4.6.4 */
36	    uint64_t timestamp_us;    /* monotonic, marvin-local */
37	    uint8_t  detector_id;     /* detector_id_t */
38	    uint8_t  reserved[3];
39	    struct
40	    {
41	        uint8_t  pressed;     /* 0/1 hard call */
42	        uint16_t confidence;  /* 0..65535, detector-defined */
43	        uint16_t raw_value;   /* detector-defined: ADC sample, pixel mean, etc. */
44	    } fret[FRET_COUNT];
45	} detector_state_t;
46	
47	/* Brings up the detector-state bus queue, the cv_marvin_v1 detector task,
48	 * and (for now) a stub consumer. All detectors start disabled; the app
49	 * must Detector_Enable() each one it wants publishing. Active selection
50	 * defaults to DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1 for symmetry but is independent of
51	 * enabled-state. Call after Video_Initialize so the video frame queue
52	 * can be subscribed to from inside cv_marvin_v1. */
53	void Detector_Initialize(void);
54	
55	/* Producers post records here; consumers (timing pipeline, eventually) read
56	 * them. Returns NULL until Detector_Initialize has run. */
57	QueueHandle_t Detector_BusQueue(void);
58	
59	/* Per-detector enable: controls whether a detector publishes records onto
60	 * the bus. Multiple detectors may be enabled simultaneously — recording
61	 * (§4.6) snoops everything for side-by-side training data. Disabled
62	 * detectors still consume their input (frames, ADC samples) so input
63	 * queues don't back up; they just don't emit. Bit operations are atomic
64	 * on aligned 32-bit reads; writes use a critical section. */
65	void Detector_Enable(detector_id_t id);
66	void Detector_Disable(detector_id_t id);
67	bool Detector_IsEnabled(detector_id_t id);
68	
69	/* Active selector: which detector's records the timing pipeline (§4.4)
70	 * acts on. Only one active at a time, irrespective of how many are
71	 * enabled. The timing pipeline is responsible for filtering by
72	 * detector_id when it lands; for M1 this is a held setting only. */
73	void          Detector_SetActive(detector_id_t id);
74	detector_id_t Detector_GetActive(void);
75	
76	#endif
77

20	 * GPIO bitmask to the fretboard MCU as a stream of single-byte messages, and
21	 * a parse task that drains the fretboard's 17-byte ADC frames off the RX ring
22	 * into PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW records. Spec §4.4 actuator transport.
23	 * Initialize first among the actuator modules so the submit queue exists by
24	 * the time any producer task starts running. Call after SYS_Initialize so the
25	 * FLEXCOM1 peripheral is up.
26	 *
27	 * Producers — timing_pipeline today, manual_control during operator UI
28	 * mode, future game menu controller (spec §4.8) — all submit through
29	 * FretboardLink_Send and tag themselves with a perf_actuator_producer_t
30	 * id. The id rides on the PERF_REC_ACTUATOR record emitted per Send so
31	 * the host can see which producer owns the wire at any moment (mode-level
32	 * arbitration is invisible from the wire byte alone).
33	 *
34	 * Latest-wins semantics: a newer mask overwrites an unsent older one,
35	 * so a stalled USB write can't accumulate stale state. Mode-level
36	 * arbitration (which producer is allowed to submit when) lives one
37	 * layer up; the link stays dumb. */

7	/* Timing pipeline — spec §4.4. Consumes detector_state_t records from the
8	 * detector-state bus (filtered by Detector_GetActive()), runs the chord-
9	 * window + strum-scheduling state machine ported from
10	 * tools/fret-tuner/actuator.py, and submits a 7-bit GPIO bitmask via
11	 * FretboardLink_Send. One of several possible producers — game menu
12	 * control (spec §4.8) and manual test inputs share the same submit API.
13	 *
14	 * Bit layout matches firmware/fretboard/cmd_receive.h:
15	 *   bit 0 = green   bit 1 = red    bit 2 = yellow
16	 *   bit 3 = blue    bit 4 = orange bit 5 = strum-down bit 6 = strum-up
17	 *
18	 * Time base is detector frame timestamps, not wall clock — replay-
19	 * deterministic and frees the task to advance only when state changes
20	 * (with a periodic timeout for between-frame strum-pulse expiries). */
21	
22	#define TIMING_BIT_GREEN       (1u << 0)
23	#define TIMING_BIT_RED         (1u << 1)
24	#define TIMING_BIT_YELLOW      (1u << 2)
25	#define TIMING_BIT_BLUE        (1u << 3)
26	#define TIMING_BIT_ORANGE      (1u << 4)
27	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN  (1u << 5)
28	#define TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP    (1u << 6)
29	#define TIMING_BIT_FRET_MASK   0x1Fu
30	#define TIMING_BIT_VALID_MASK  0x7Fu
31	
32	void TimingPipeline_Initialize(void);
33

35	 * note highway). When false, the pipeline still advances internal state but
36	 * suppresses actuation so a peer producer (manual_control, future game-state
37	 * controller §4.8) can own the wire; disabling also releases the wire once.
38	 * Internal state stays current so the next advance() after re-enable republishes
39	 * the right mask without a stale frame. */

41	bool TimingPipeline_IsEnabled(void);

142	    uint8_t    frets_active;          /* asserted mask, pre-strum overlay */
143	    uint8_t    strum_active;          /* 0/1 — strum pulse currently held */
144	    uint8_t    release_pending_mask;  /* frets with pending release timer */
145	    uint8_t    publish_mask;          /* final wire output mask */
146	    uint32_t   strum_release_at_ms;   /* deadline for current strum pulse */
147	    uint32_t   release_min_at_ms;     /* earliest pending-release deadline */

150	/* PERF_REC_DROP — drain task emits at 1 Hz. Counters are cumulative
151	 * since session start; host computes deltas. */
152	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
153	{
154	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
155	    uint32_t   dropped_state;
156	    uint32_t   dropped_strip;

161	/* PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER — periodic stack high-water dump. task_id is
162	 * a stable enum mirrored in the host decoder; words is the
163	 * uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark return (StackType_t units).
164	 *
165	 * Marvin-owned tasks (0..5) are registered at task creation. IDLE is
166	 * the FreeRTOS idle task (xTaskGetIdleTaskHandle) — its run_time_counter
167	 * is what makes absolute CPU% computable on the host
168	 * (1 - idle_delta / Σ_all_delta). MCC tasks (LEGATO..APP) are looked up
169	 * by string name with xTaskGetHandle from the perf-drain task at startup.
170	 * OTHER is a pseudo-slot: not a real task, just an aggregate of "all
171	 * tasks not in this enum" that the drain emits each runtime cycle so
172	 * per-window CPU% adds to 100. HWM is meaningless for OTHER (no single
173	 * stack); the runtime-side producer emits TASK_RUNTIME for OTHER but
174	 * skips TASK_HIGHWATER. */
175	typedef enum
176	{
177	    PERF_TASK_VIDEO          = 0,
178	    PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1   = 1,
179	    PERF_TASK_DETECTOR_DRAIN = 2,
180	    PERF_TASK_TIMING         = 3,
181	    PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK = 4,
182	    PERF_TASK_PERF_DRAIN     = 5,
183	    PERF_TASK_IDLE           = 6,
184	    PERF_TASK_LEGATO         = 7,
185	    PERF_TASK_XLCDC          = 8,
186	    PERF_TASK_MAXTOUCH       = 9,
187	    PERF_TASK_SYS_INPUT      = 10,
188	    PERF_TASK_USB_DEVICE     = 11,
189	    PERF_TASK_USB_HOST       = 12,
190	    PERF_TASK_DRV_USB_UDPHS  = 13,
191	    PERF_TASK_DRV_USB_HOST   = 14,
192	    PERF_TASK_APP            = 15,
193	    PERF_TASK_OTHER          = 16,
194	    PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX   = 17,
195	} perf_task_id_t;
196	
197	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
198	{
199	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
200	    uint8_t    task_id;
201	    uint8_t    reserved[3];
202	    uint32_t   words;
203	} perf_rec_task_highwater_t;
204	
205	/* PERF_REC_STRIP — variable-size BGR888 region of interest, kind-tagged.
206	 * Today's producers emit SENSING (row through the sensor patches) and
207	 * STRIKE (row through the strum trigger zone), each 240×32 once per ISC
208	 * frame; SNAPSHOT carries a full frame as a top-to-bottom sequence of
209	 * full-width bands sharing one frame_epoch (last band flags LAST).
210	 * Future kinds (SCORE, MINIMAP, etc.) plug into the same record type —
211	 * adding one is an enum entry plus a producer; no schema bump.
212	 *
213	 * Wire payload size is HDR + 12 B body + w*h*PERF_STRIP_BPP bytes,
214	 * tightly packed. The queue slot is sized to PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES; the
215	 * drain task computes the on-wire length from (w, h) and frames only
216	 * what's used. */
217	typedef enum
218	{
219	    PERF_STRIP_SENSING  = 0,
220	    PERF_STRIP_STRIKE   = 1,
221	    PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT = 2,
222	    PERF_STRIP_REGION   = 3,   /* host-selected sub-region, streamed per frame */
223	} perf_strip_kind_t;
224	
225	/* Strip flags byte (perf_rec_strip_t.flags). SNAPSHOT producers set LAST on
226	 * the final (bottom) band so the host knows the frame is complete without a
227	 * separate end marker. Zero for SENSING/STRIKE. */
228	#define PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST  0x01u
229	
230	#define PERF_STRIP_BPP        3u
231	
232	/* Wire-bound on the strip pixel-data size. Two stacked caps determine
233	 * the maximum payload a strip can carry:
234	 *
235	 *   1. Wire LEN field is u16 → max payload 65535 bytes
236	 *      → max pixel = 65535 − HDR(16) − BODY(12) = 65507
237	 *   2. UDPHS DMA single-transfer cap is
238	 *      DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE × 64 KB
239	 *      (currently 2 × 64 KB = 128 KB; well above the LEN cap)
240	 *
241	 * The u16 LEN field is the binding constraint. Set at 65000 to land just
242	 * under it with a small margin. Producers may use any (w, h) shape as
243	 * long as w * h * PERF_STRIP_BPP <= PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES.
244	 *
245	 * Practical strip-size envelope (pixel area = w*h ≤ ~21666):
246	 *   720×30  640×33  480×45  320×64  290×72
247	 *
248	 * Buffer footprint scales with this:
249	 *   pool      = PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE × (28 + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES)
250	 *   sink ring = SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH × round_up_64(36 + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES)
251	 * Together ~585 KB BSS at 65000; trivially fits in the 240 MB cached DDR.
252	 *
253	 * To go beyond u16 LEN, the wire format itself needs a schema break (LEN
254	 * → u32). Don't do that lightly — at 60 fps × 65 KB = ~3.9 MB/s, this cap
255	 * already lines up with what the wire can sustainably carry. */
256	#define PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES  65000u
257	
258	#define PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES  (sizeof(perf_hdr_t) + 12u)   /* hdr + body */
259	
260	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
261	{
262	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
263	    uint16_t   x, y;          /* top-left in source frame */
264	    uint16_t   w, h;          /* per-record dimensions */
265	    uint8_t    kind;          /* perf_strip_kind_t */
266	    uint8_t    flags;         /* PERF_STRIP_FLAG_* */
267	    uint8_t    reserved[2];
268	    uint8_t    bgr[PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES];   /* sized to max in queue slot */
269	} perf_rec_strip_t;
270	
271	/* PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME — per-task snapshot of state, priority, and
272	 * cumulative run-time counter. Drain task emits one record per known
273	 * task at 1 Hz alongside DROP and TASK_HIGHWATER. Host computes per-
274	 * window CPU% as Δrun_time_counter[task] / ΣΔrun_time_counter. */
275	typedef enum
276	{
277	    PERF_TASK_STATE_RUNNING   = 0,
278	    PERF_TASK_STATE_READY     = 1,
279	    PERF_TASK_STATE_BLOCKED   = 2,
280	    PERF_TASK_STATE_SUSPENDED = 3,
281	    PERF_TASK_STATE_DELETED   = 4,
282	    PERF_TASK_STATE_INVALID   = 5,
283	} perf_task_state_t;
284	
285	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
286	{
287	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
288	    uint8_t    task_id;            /* perf_task_id_t */
289	    uint8_t    state;              /* perf_task_state_t (mirrors eTaskState) */
290	    uint8_t    priority;           /* uxCurrentPriority */
291	    uint8_t    reserved;
292	    uint32_t   run_time_counter;   /* low 32 bits of ulRunTimeCounter */
293	    uint32_t   reserved2;
294	} perf_rec_task_runtime_t;
295	
296	/* PERF_REC_DETECTOR_CONFIG — cv_marvin_v1 per-fret configuration. Static
297	 * today (compile-time tables); becomes runtime-tunable when M6 calibration
298	 * UI lands. Emitted on connect-up edge and on change so the host always
299	 * has a current copy. Sample coords are in capture-frame space (matching
300	 * STRIP record (x, y) anchors). Floats are IEEE 754 little-endian — same
301	 * representation on both sides. Used by the host to render sample
302	 * dots / threshold reference lines onto STRIP canvases. */
303	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
304	{
305	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
306	    uint16_t   sensor_hx[FRET_COUNT];          /* hold-sensor x per fret */
307	    uint16_t   sensor_hy[FRET_COUNT];          /* hold-sensor y per fret */
308	    uint16_t   sensor_ex[FRET_COUNT];          /* edge-sensor x per fret */
309	    uint16_t   sensor_ey[FRET_COUNT];          /* edge-sensor y per fret */
310	    float      hold_thresh;                    /* CV_HOLD_THRESH (brightness) */
311	    float      hold_release_frac;              /* CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC */
312	    float      edge_thresh;                    /* CV_EDGE_THRESH */
313	    float      color_target_b[FRET_COUNT];     /* per-fret target weights */
314	    float      color_target_g[FRET_COUNT];
315	    float      color_target_r[FRET_COUNT];
316	    float      color_reject_b[FRET_COUNT];     /* per-fret reject weights */
317	    float      color_reject_g[FRET_COUNT];
318	    float      color_reject_r[FRET_COUNT];
319	} perf_rec_detector_config_t;
320	
321	/* PERF_REC_ACTUATOR — emitted on every FretboardLink_Send call (i.e. on
322	 * intent), one record per call. Closes the gap between TIMING.publish_mask
323	 * (intent on the timing pipeline side) and FBL_SEND STAMP (a byte hit the
324	 * USB DMA): with multiple producers (timing_pipeline, manual_control, future
325	 * game_state_controller per spec §4.8), the wire byte alone doesn't say
326	 * who asserted what.
327	 *
328	 * intended_mask: what the producer asked for this Send (low 7 bits).
329	 * asserted_mask: what's currently held on the link (last byte queued).
330	 * strum_dir: from the bit pattern (0=none, 1=down, 2=up).
331	 * producer_id: perf_actuator_producer_t — the arbitration signal that's
332	 *              invisible on the wire today.
333	 * last_ack_*:  most recent CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE result and timestamp,
334	 *              snapshotted at Send-time so the host can compute transport-
335	 *              side latency without joining FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE
336	 *              stamps (still useful, but redundant for the common case). */
337	typedef enum
338	{
339	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_NONE     = 0,
340	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_TIMING   = 1,
341	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_MANUAL   = 2,
342	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_GAMEPLAY = 3,   /* M10 game-state controller: menu nav */
343	} perf_actuator_producer_t;
344	
345	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
346	{
347	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
348	    uint8_t    intended_mask;
349	    uint8_t    asserted_mask;
350	    uint8_t    strum_dir;            /* 0=none, 1=down, 2=up */
351	    uint8_t    producer_id;          /* perf_actuator_producer_t */
352	    int32_t    last_ack_result;      /* USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_*, signed for safety */
353	    uint64_t   last_ack_ts_counter;  /* SYS_TIME at most-recent CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE */
354	} perf_rec_actuator_t;
355	
356	/* PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW — one record per parsed 17-byte fretboard data
357	 * frame (firmware/fretboard/data_stream.c). The 5×u16 ADC values are 12-bit
358	 * unsigned (0–4095, lower = brighter sensor) indexed by fret_t (G/R/Y/B/O).
359	 * Fretboard emits at ~240 Hz; with video at 60 Hz the same frame_epoch

# Marvin CV Detector Architecture Map

All paths under `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/`.

## 1. `game/fret.h` — the shared fret primitive

The `fret_t` enum lives in the game domain (shared by detector, actuator, UI), not in detector/:

```c
typedef enum {
    FRET_GREEN=0, FRET_RED=1, FRET_YELLOW=2, FRET_BLUE=3, FRET_ORANGE=4,
    FRET_COUNT=5,
} fret_t;
```

`FRET_COUNT` (5) sizes the per-fret arrays in `detector_state_t` and every static table in `cv_marvin_v1.c`. This is per-highway/per-player conceptually but currently there's exactly one set. For two-player you'd have two independent highways each with 5 frets — the enum itself is fine (frets are the same colors), but every `[FRET_COUNT]`-sized static in cv_marvin_v1 is single-instance (see §4).

---

## 2. `detector/detector.h` + `detector/detector.c` — bus / registry / enable-disable API

### Public API surface (detector.h)
- `void Detector_Initialize(void)` — brings up the bus queue and calls `CvMarvinV1_Initialize()`. Must run after `Video_Initialize`.
- `QueueHandle_t Detector_BusQueue(void)` — the single shared "detector-state bus" all producers post to; NULL before init.
- `void Detector_Enable(detector_id_t id)` / `Detector_Disable(...)` / `bool Detector_IsEnabled(...)` — per-detector publish gate, backed by a bitmask.
- `void Detector_SetActive(detector_id_t id)` / `detector_id_t Detector_GetActive(void)` — which detector the (future) timing pipeline acts on; single active at a time.

### Key enum/struct (detector.h)

`detector_id_t` (detector.h:24-28) — **this is the registry namespace.** Only two IDs today, and they identify detector *algorithms/sources*, not player highways:
```c
typedef enum {
    DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1  = 0,
    DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1,
} detector_id_t;
```
Note for two-player: the enable-mask and active-selector are keyed on `detector_id_t`. If 2p means two instances of the *same* algorithm (2p-left / 2p-right), the current scheme has no way to distinguish them — the id is both the algorithm identity and the on-the-wire `detector_id` field. You'd need either new enum ids (e.g. `DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1_P2`) or a separate player/highway dimension.

`detector_state_t` (detector.h:33-45) — the canonical bus record AND the on-disk `state.bin` format (fixed layout, do not reorder). Carries `detector_id` (uint8) and a `fret[FRET_COUNT]` array of `{pressed, confidence, raw_value}`. There is **no player/highway field** — a two-player design must decide whether to distinguish records by `detector_id`, add a field (schema bump per the header's warning at :30-32), or run two buses.

### Registry implementation (detector.c) — all module-level static
```c
#define DETECTOR_BUS_DEPTH 8u                              // :11
static QueueHandle_t   s_bus_queue;                        // :13  single shared bus
static StaticQueue_t   s_bus_queue_buf;                    // :14
static uint8_t         s_bus_queue_storage[...];           // :15
static volatile uint32_t s_enabled_mask;                   // :17  bit N = detector_id N
static volatile uint8_t  s_active_id = DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1; // :18
```
- Enable/disable are `1u << id` bit ops in a critical section (:36-48); `Detector_IsEnabled` is a lock-free bit test (:50-53).
- `Detector_Initialize` (:20-29): creates the static bus queue, `configASSERT`s it, then calls `CvMarvinV1_Initialize()` directly. **This is the sole wiring from the registry into the CV detector** — the registry hard-codes the one detector's init call. Adding instances means adding calls here (or a table).
- The bus is a single queue shared by all producers/consumers; depth 8 sized for "~one detector × one frame-time at 60 Hz" (:8-10) — two producers at 60 Hz would want a rethink of depth.

---

## 3. `detector/cv_marvin_v1.h` — the CV detector's public surface

Entire public API is one function (cv_marvin_v1.h:9):
```c
void CvMarvinV1_Initialize(void);
```
No handle returned, no parameters, no instance concept. Everything else in the module is file-static.

---

## 4. `detector/cv_marvin_v1.c` — task, subscription, publish, and ALL single-instance static state

### How the task is created (cv_marvin_v1.c:479-489)
```c
void CvMarvinV1_Initialize(void)
{
    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(cv_marvin_v1_task,
                                       "CvMarvinV1",
                                       CV_TASK_STACK_WORDS,   // 1024
                                       NULL,                  // no param passed
                                       CV_TASK_PRIORITY,      // 4
                                       s_task_stack,          // static
                                       &s_task_tcb);          // static
    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1, h);
}
```
Static task creation with a **static stack (`s_task_stack`, :97) and TCB (`s_task_tcb`, :98)**, a **hard-coded task name `"CvMarvinV1"`**, and **`NULL` param** — there is no mechanism to pass an instance/context pointer to the task. It also registers a single perf-log highwater slot `PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1`. Two instances would each need their own stack/TCB, a unique name, a distinct perf-log task id, and a context arg (the `void *param` is currently `(void)param`'d at :380).

### How it subscribes to video frames (cv_marvin_v1.c:382-388, inside the task)
```c
QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,   // depth 1, drop-intermediate
                                          sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
                                          s_frame_queue_storage,   // static, :89
                                          &s_frame_queue_buf);     // static, :88
configASSERT(frames != NULL);
bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
configASSERT(subscribed);
```
The frame queue is built from **static storage (`s_frame_queue_storage` :89, `s_frame_queue_buf` :88)** with `CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH = 1` (:18, "drop-intermediate policy"). It then grabs the shared bus via `Detector_BusQueue()` (:390-391).

### How it publishes `detector_state_t` (cv_marvin_v1.c:170-218, `detect_frame`)
Builds a `detector_state_t` on the stack, sets `frame_epoch = frame->frame_count`, `timestamp_us` from tick count, and `detector_id = DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1` (**hard-coded** at :176 — a second instance would still stamp the same id unless changed). Fills `state.fret[i]` for each fret, then `xQueueSend(bus, &state, 0)` (:218, non-blocking). Also mirrors the decision to the perf-log via `PerfLog_EmitDetector` (:236-237).

### The task loop and gating (cv_marvin_v1.c:397-476)
Blocks on `xQueueReceive(frames, ..., portMAX_DELAY)`. Always drains; only processes when `Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)` (:403 — again the hard-coded id gates this instance). Validates `frame.buffer`, `width/height`, and `bytes_per_pixel == CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL` (:404-406). Emits perf stamps, runs `detect_frame`, republishes config at ~1 Hz (:417), and ships STRIKE/SENSING/REGION strips to the host viewer.

### ALL module-level `static` state that is inherently single-instance

**Const config tables (read-only, but describe one highway's geometry — would need per-instance copies or per-instance calibration for 2p, since left/right highways sit at different screen coords):**
- `s_sensor_coords[FRET_COUNT]` (:56-63) — `sensor_xy_t` sample points in native 720×480 capture space. **Hard-coded to one highway's pixel positions.** For 2p-left/2p-right these are the *primary* thing that differs (two highways = two coordinate sets). Currently `static const`.
- `s_color_filter[FRET_COUNT]` (:71-78) — per-fret BGR target/reject weights. `static const`, could be shared read-only across instances but the config-publish path treats them as this-detector's config.
- `s_overlay_hold_bgr[3]` (:249) and `s_overlay_edge_bgr[FRET_COUNT][3]` (:250-257) — overlay colors, `static const`, shareable.

**Mutable per-fret detector state (the core problem — one set of frets, would be corrupted if two instances shared it):**
```c
static float    s_hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];    // :82
static float    s_edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];    // :83
static bool     s_pressed[FRET_COUNT];      // :84  hold latch, hysteresis state
static bool     s_edge_active[FRET_COUNT];  // :85  edge-detect latch
static uint32_t s_press_count[FRET_COUNT];  // :86  rising-edge counter
```
These carry frame-to-frame hysteresis/latch state (:192-200, :202, :233-234, :334-343). Two players pressing frets independently would clobber each other's press/edge latches. **These must become per-instance for 2p.**

**Task/queue/scratch statics (single-instance resources):**
```c
static StaticQueue_t s_frame_queue_buf;                         // :88
static uint8_t       s_frame_queue_storage[...];                // :89  frame queue backing
static uint8_t       s_sensing_scratch[W*H*3];                  // :95  strip-overlay scratch
static StackType_t   s_task_stack[CV_TASK_STACK_WORDS];         // :97  task stack
static StaticTask_t  s_task_tcb;                                // :98  task TCB
```
`s_sensing_scratch` (:95) is a shared paint buffer written each frame (:438-452); two tasks writing it concurrently would tear. The queue backing, stack, and TCB are all one-per-module.

**Module-level `#define` constants that bake in one highway's geometry:** `CV_SENSING_X/Y/W/H` (:39-42) and `CV_STRIKE_X/Y/W/H` (:43-46) — the host-viewer strip regions, hard-coded to one highway's location on screen. Thresholds `CV_HOLD_THRESH`, `CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC`, `CV_EDGE_THRESH` (:30-32) are shareable but are published as "this detector's config."

### Perf-log coupling (would also need per-instance identity)
- `PerfLog_EmitDetector(...)` (:236) — one detector's ground-truth stream.
- `publish_detector_config()` (:353-374) emits `perf_rec_detector_config_t` built from the static tables — "the single point that re-publishes" (:349-352). A second instance needs its own config channel/identity.
- `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame/EmitStripPacked/EmitRegionIfEnabled` and `PERF_STRIP_SENSING`/`PERF_STRIP_STRIKE` (:423-457) — single strip identities per region; two highways would collide on these host-viewer strip slots.

---

## 5. `app.c` / `app.h` — how the detector is wired into startup

### `CvMarvinV1_Initialize` is NOT called from app.c directly
It's called indirectly: `App_StartServices()` → `Detector_Initialize()` → `CvMarvinV1_Initialize()`. App only touches the registry API.

### Startup path
- `APP_Initialize()` (app.c:117-166) sets up only splash-critical modules (log, UI manager, perf-log producer queues, storage, results, catalog, art). It registers `app_on_splash_shown` (:132) as the splash callback. The video/detector/actuator/console are explicitly deferred (:161-165).
- `app_on_splash_shown()` (:98-101) simply calls `App_StartServices()`.
- `App_StartServices()` (app.c:174-239) — **task creation order matters:**
  1. `Video_Initialize()` (:178) — first, because it owns the frame queue the detector subscribes to.
  2. `Detector_Initialize()` (:184), then `Detector_Enable(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)` (:185) and `Detector_SetActive(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)` (:186). **This is the only place the CV detector is enabled/selected.** For 2p you'd enable/select both highways here (and today there's no distinct id to enable a second one).
  3. `FretboardLink_Initialize()`, optional `Fauxmote_Initialize()`, `TimingPipeline_Initialize()` (:202 — the future consumer of the active detector), `ManualControl_Initialize()`, `GameplayEngine_Initialize()` (:218 — another video-frame subscriber), `GameController_Initialize()`, `Console_Initialize()` (:228 — can drive detector setters), `PerfLog_Start()`, `HealthMonitor_Initialize()`.
- `APP_Tasks()` (app.c:250-264) is a one-shot; logs heap and `vTaskDelete(NULL)`.

The comment at app.c:182-186 confirms the intended model: "Detectors default disabled; enable + select the active one for the timing pipeline." `TimingPipeline` (:199-202) "runs … against the active detector" — so the active-selector currently assumes a single winner, which conflicts with two simultaneously-active highways.

---

## 6. `video/video.h` — frame subscription / queue model

### Public API
- `void Video_Initialize(void)` — capture disabled, no callbacks by default.
- `Video_CaptureEnable/Disable(void)`.
- `Video_SetFrameLatchCallback(...)` / `Video_SetDisplayReconcileCallback(...)` — compositor HEO hooks (ISR + task tick).
- `bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)` (:76) / `bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)` (:79).
- `void Video_GetFrameInfo(Video_FrameInfo *info)` (:83) — non-blocking synchronous read.
- `bool Video_GetActiveRect(uint16_t *x,*y,*w,*h)` (:97) — runtime-detected active-picture rectangle (letterbox crop).

### `Video_FrameInfo` struct (video.h:45-52)
```c
typedef struct {
    void    *buffer;          /* most-recent complete frame in DDR */
    uint32_t frame_count;     /* monotonic since last ISC start */
    uint16_t width;
    uint16_t height;
    uint16_t bytes_per_pixel;
} Video_FrameInfo;
```
It carries a pointer to the **full** frame plus dimensions — no per-highway cropping. Both 2p highways would receive the identical full frame and each crop/sample its own region via its own `s_sensor_coords`.

### Queue / subscriber model (video.h:54-79) — **this is the good news for 2p**
- **Multiple subscribers are explicitly supported.** The ISC frame-done IRQ does `xQueueSendFromISR` to **every** subscribed queue (:55-57). Up to `VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS` concurrent (documented as **currently 4**, :74-75). Today the CV detector uses 1 slot and the gameplay engine uses another, so there is headroom for a second CV instance.
- Each subscriber creates its own queue and **chooses its own depth / back-pressure policy independently** (:59-72). Depth 1 = "process most recent, drop the rest"; on full, the IRQ's send returns `errQUEUE_FULL` and drops for that subscriber only.
- Re-subscribing an already-present queue is a no-op success; `Video_SubscribeFrames` returns false only if the table is full (:73-75).

So a two-player refactor can create a second frame queue and subscribe it without touching the video module — the fan-out already handles N subscribers. The constraint is `VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS` (4), shared with the gameplay engine and any other consumers.

---

## Summary of two-player / pluggable-detector friction points

Single-instance couplings that a refactor must address (all in cv_marvin_v1.c unless noted):
1. **Hard-coded `detector_id` identity** at build/enable/publish time: detector.c registry keys enable-mask and active-selector on `detector_id_t` (only 2 algorithm ids exist); cv_marvin_v1 stamps and gates on `DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1` literally (cv_marvin_v1.c:176, :403). No player/highway dimension exists in `detector_state_t` (detector.h:33-45) — and that struct is also the on-disk format, so adding a field is a schema bump.
2. **Mutable per-fret latch state** `s_hold_dist/s_edge_dist/s_pressed/s_edge_active/s_press_count` (cv_marvin_v1.c:82-86) — must be per-instance.
3. **Task resources** `s_task_stack/s_task_tcb` (:97-98), hard-coded task name `"CvMarvinV1"`, `NULL` param (no context passed to the task, :383/:380), single perf highwater id `PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1` (:488).
4. **Frame-queue + scratch statics** `s_frame_queue_buf/_storage` (:88-89), `s_sensing_scratch` (:95).
5. **Geometry baked in**: `s_sensor_coords` (:56-63) and the `CV_SENSING_*` / `CV_STRIKE_*` strip defines (:39-46) describe one highway's screen position — the primary per-player difference.
6. **Registry wiring** hard-codes one init call: `Detector_Initialize` → `CvMarvinV1_Initialize()` (detector.c:28); app enables/selects exactly one (app.c:184-186); `TimingPipeline` assumes a single "active" detector (app.c:199-202).
7. **Video is already multi-subscriber** (video.h:74-75, up to 4) — the frame-distribution side does *not* block two instances; the constraint is the shared `VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS` budget.

No changes made — this is a read-only map.

192	def _decode_task_runtime(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> TaskRuntime:
193	    _check(payload, TaskRuntime.SIZE, "TaskRuntime")
194	    task_id, state, priority, _reserved, run_time_counter, _reserved2 = (
195	        TaskRuntime._BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
196	    )
197	    return TaskRuntime(
198	        hdr=hdr,
199	        task_id=task_id,
200	        state=state,
201	        priority=priority,
202	        run_time_counter=run_time_counter,
203	    )
204	
205	
206	def _decode_strip(hdr: Header, payload: bytes) -> Strip:
207	    if len(payload) < STRIP_HDR_BYTES:
208	        raise DecodeError(
209	            f"Strip: payload {len(payload)} < header {STRIP_HDR_BYTES}"
210	        )
211	    x, y, w, h, kind, flags, _reserved = _STRIP_BODY.unpack_from(payload, HDR_SIZE)
212	    expected_pixels = w * h * STRIP_BPP
213	    if expected_pixels > STRIP_MAX_BYTES:
214	        raise DecodeError(
215	            f"Strip: w*h*bpp {expected_pixels} > max {STRIP_MAX_BYTES}"
216	        )
217	    expected_total = STRIP_HDR_BYTES + expected_pixels
218	    if len(payload) != expected_total:
219	        raise DecodeError(
220	            f"Strip: payload {len(payload)} != expected {expected_total} "
221	            f"({w}×{h}×{STRIP_BPP})"
222	        )
223	    bgr = bytes(payload[STRIP_HDR_BYTES:expected_total])
224	    return Strip(hdr=hdr, x=x, y=y, w=w, h=h, kind=kind, flags=flags, bgr=bgr)
225	
226	
227	_DISPATCH = {
228	    RecordType.SESSION: _decode_session,
229	    RecordType.STAMP: _decode_stamp,
230	    RecordType.DETECTOR: _decode_detector,
231	    RecordType.TIMING: _decode_timing,
232	    RecordType.DROP: _decode_drop,
233	    RecordType.TASK_HIGHWATER: _decode_task_highwater,
234	    RecordType.TASK_RUNTIME: _decode_task_runtime,
235	    RecordType.STRIP: _decode_strip,
236	    RecordType.DETECTOR_CONFIG: _decode_detector_config,
237	    RecordType.ACTUATOR: _decode_actuator,
238	    RecordType.FRETBOARD_RAW: _decode_fretboard_raw,
239	}
240	
241	
242	def decode_record(payload: bytes) -> Record:
243	    """Decode an FCS-validated frame payload into a typed Record dataclass.
244	
245	    Caller (framing.iter_frames) has already verified FCS and length sanity.
246	    Unknown record types are surfaced as UnknownRecord so a forward-schema
247	    firmware does not crash an older host.
248	    """
249	    if len(payload) < HDR_SIZE:
250	        raise DecodeError(f"payload {len(payload)} < HDR_SIZE {HDR_SIZE}")
251	    hdr = Header.unpack(payload)
252	    if hdr.magic != PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC:
253	        raise DecodeError(f"bad magic 0x{hdr.magic:04x}")
254	
255	    decoder = _DISPATCH.get(hdr.type)
256	    if decoder is None:
257	        return UnknownRecord(hdr=hdr, raw=payload)
258	    return decoder(hdr, payload)
259

321	/* PERF_REC_ACTUATOR — emitted on every FretboardLink_Send call (i.e. on
322	 * intent), one record per call. Closes the gap between TIMING.publish_mask
323	 * (intent on the timing pipeline side) and FBL_SEND STAMP (a byte hit the
324	 * USB DMA): with multiple producers (timing_pipeline, manual_control, future
325	 * game_state_controller per spec §4.8), the wire byte alone doesn't say
326	 * who asserted what.
327	 *
328	 * intended_mask: what the producer asked for this Send (low 7 bits).
329	 * asserted_mask: what's currently held on the link (last byte queued).
330	 * strum_dir: from the bit pattern (0=none, 1=down, 2=up).
331	 * producer_id: perf_actuator_producer_t — the arbitration signal that's
332	 *              invisible on the wire today.
333	 * last_ack_*:  most recent CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE result and timestamp,
334	 *              snapshotted at Send-time so the host can compute transport-
335	 *              side latency without joining FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE
336	 *              stamps (still useful, but redundant for the common case). */
337	typedef enum
338	{
339	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_NONE     = 0,
340	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_TIMING   = 1,
341	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_MANUAL   = 2,
342	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_GAMEPLAY = 3,   /* M10 game-state controller: menu nav */
343	} perf_actuator_producer_t;
344	
345	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
346	{
347	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
348	    uint8_t    intended_mask;
349	    uint8_t    asserted_mask;
350	    uint8_t    strum_dir;            /* 0=none, 1=down, 2=up */
351	    uint8_t    producer_id;          /* perf_actuator_producer_t */
352	    int32_t    last_ack_result;      /* USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_*, signed for safety */
353	    uint64_t   last_ack_ts_counter;  /* SYS_TIME at most-recent CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE */
354	} perf_rec_actuator_t;
355	
356	/* PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW — one record per parsed 17-byte fretboard data
357	 * frame (firmware/fretboard/data_stream.c). The 5×u16 ADC values are 12-bit
358	 * unsigned (0–4095, lower = brighter sensor) indexed by fret_t (G/R/Y/B/O).
359	 * Fretboard emits at ~240 Hz; with video at 60 Hz the same frame_epoch
360	 * value tags ~4 consecutive records — ts_counter (stamped by hdr_fill at
361	 * record-emit time) disambiguates within the frame.
362	 *
363	 * fb_sample_seq and applied_mask are stamped by the fretboard itself and
364	 * carried on the wire: the sequence counter (one per fretboard tick) lets the
365	 * host reconstruct true sample order and detect frames dropped in transit,
366	 * and applied_mask is the actuator bitmask the fretboard was driving during
367	 * this very scan — so sensor and actuator state are paired atomically at the
368	 * source instead of joined across marvin's TX/RX clocks. Default-disabled at
369	 * boot like the other high-rate types. */
370	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
371	{
372	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
373	    uint16_t   adc[FRET_COUNT];      /* 5 × 2 = 10 B */
374	    uint32_t   fb_sample_seq;        /* fretboard tick counter (monotonic) */
375	    uint8_t    applied_mask;         /* actuator bitmask driven this scan */
376	    uint8_t    reserved;
377	} perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t;
378	
379	/* ─── Host→device commands ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
380	 *
381	 * Wrapped in the same SOF/LEN/CRC framer as TX records. Magic is distinct
382	 * from PERF_LOG_HDR_MAGIC so a misrouted record frame can't be parsed as
383	 * a command (or vice versa). The device reads commands on the CDC OUT
384	 * endpoint; the host writes them via marvin-perf's set-mask path. */
385	
386	#define PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC   0x4D43u   /* 'M','C' little-endian */
387	
388	typedef enum
389	{
390	    PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK = 0x01u,
391	    PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT      = 0x02u,
392	    PERF_CMD_SET_OVERLAY   = 0x03u,
393	    PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM = 0x04u,
394	} perf_cmd_t;
395	
396	/* Overlay sinks for the per-fret target rings, gated independently via
397	 * PERF_CMD_SET_OVERLAY. STRIP draws the rings onto the SENSING strip copy
398	 * that ships to the host viewer (never the capture buffer, so snapshots and
399	 * the LVDS panel stay clean). PANEL is reserved for a future LVDS demo
400	 * overlay and is a no-op today. */
401	#define PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP   0x01u
402	#define PERF_OVERLAY_PANEL   0x02u
403	
404	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
405	{
406	    uint16_t magic;        /* PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC */
407	    uint8_t  cmd_id;       /* perf_cmd_t */
408	    uint8_t  reserved;
409	} perf_cmd_hdr_t;
410	
411	/* PERF_CMD_SET_TYPE_MASK — bit i (i = perf_rec_type_t value) gates record
412	 * type i. SESSION is always emitted regardless of mask so the host can
413	 * still derive timer_freq_hz on attach. */
414	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
415	{
416	    perf_cmd_hdr_t hdr;
417	    uint32_t       enabled_mask;
418	} perf_cmd_set_mask_t;
419	
420	/* PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT — capture the current full video frame and stream it back
421	 * as a top-to-bottom sequence of full-width PERF_REC_STRIP records (kind
422	 * SNAPSHOT), all sharing one frame_epoch, the last flagged LAST. Header-only;
423	 * "current frame, full resolution" needs no parameters. Not gated by the
424	 * STRIP type mask — the command itself is the request. */
425	
426	/* PERF_CMD_SET_OVERLAY — set the active overlay sinks (PERF_OVERLAY_* bits).
427	 * Bits not set disable that sink. */
428	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
429	{
430	    perf_cmd_hdr_t hdr;
431	    uint32_t       flags;
432	} perf_cmd_set_overlay_t;
433	
434	/* PERF_CMD_REGION_STREAM — start/stop continuously streaming a fixed sub-region
435	 * of each video frame back as one PERF_REC_STRIP (kind REGION) per frame via the
436	 * pooled strip path (drop-on-full). `enable`=1 starts with the given rect
437	 * (source-frame pixels); `enable`=0 stops (rect ignored). This command is the
438	 * gate, so REGION strips are emitted independent of the STRIP type mask (which
439	 * gates the fretboard SENSING/STRIKE strips). The rect is host-selected so it
440	 * can be repointed without a firmware rebuild. */
441	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
442	{
443	    perf_cmd_hdr_t hdr;
444	    uint8_t        enable;
445	    uint8_t        reserved;
446	    uint16_t       x, y, w, h;
447	} perf_cmd_region_stream_t;

449	#endif /* PERF_LOG_RECORDS_H */

633	/* Claim a free strip pool slot and fill its header. Returns the slot pointer
634	 * (writing its index to *out_idx) or NULL when the args are invalid, the pool
635	 * is empty (drop counted), or — when honor_mask is set — STRIP is masked off.
636	 * honor_mask=false is for the REGION stream, which has its own start/stop
637	 * command as its gate (default off), so it toggles independently of the STRIP
638	 * type mask that gates the fretboard SENSING/STRIKE strips. The caller fills
639	 * r->bgr then calls strip_slot_commit. No struct memcpy in the queue critical
640	 * section — only a 1-byte index transfer. */
641	static perf_rec_strip_t *strip_slot_claim(uint32_t frame_epoch, perf_strip_kind_t kind,
642	                                          uint16_t x, uint16_t y,
643	                                          uint16_t w, uint16_t h,
644	                                          bool honor_mask, uint8_t *out_idx)
645	{
646	    if (s_strip_q == NULL || s_strip_free_q == NULL) { return NULL; }
647	    if (honor_mask && !type_enabled(PERF_REC_STRIP)) { return NULL; }
648	    if (w == 0u || h == 0u) { return NULL; }
649	    if ((uint32_t)w * (uint32_t)h * PERF_STRIP_BPP > PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES) { return NULL; }
650	
651	    uint8_t slot_idx;
652	    if (xQueueReceive(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0) != pdTRUE)
653	    {
654	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
655	        return NULL;
656	    }
657	
658	    perf_rec_strip_t *r = &s_strip_pool[slot_idx];
659	    memset(r, 0, PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES);
660	    hdr_fill(&r->hdr, PERF_REC_STRIP, 0u, frame_epoch);
661	    r->x    = x;
662	    r->y    = y;
663	    r->w    = w;
664	    r->h    = h;
665	    r->kind = (uint8_t)kind;
666	    *out_idx = slot_idx;
667	    return r;
668	}
669	
670	static void strip_slot_commit(uint8_t slot_idx)
671	{
672	    if (xQueueSend(s_strip_q, &slot_idx, 0) != pdTRUE)
673	    {
674	        /* In-flight queue full (pool sized depth+2 makes this rare; only
675	         * possible if the drain task is blocked while strip_q is at depth
676	         * and the producer also holds a slot). Return slot to free pool. */
677	        (void)xQueueSend(s_strip_free_q, &slot_idx, 0);
678	        counter_add_task(&s_drop_strip, 1u);
679	    }
680	}
681	
682	/* Strip producer: claim a free slot, row-copy a w×h BGR888 region out of the
683	 * strided source frame directly into the slot, then enqueue the slot index.
684	 * Total pixel bytes (w*h*3) must fit the slot's bgr[] (PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES);
685	 * per-axis shape is unconstrained beyond that. Drop-on-pool-empty. */
686	static void emit_strip_from_frame(uint32_t frame_epoch, perf_strip_kind_t kind,
687	                                  const uint8_t *frame, uint32_t frame_stride,
688	                                  uint16_t x, uint16_t y, uint16_t w, uint16_t h,
689	                                  bool honor_mask)
690	{
691	    if (frame == NULL) { return; }
692	
693	    uint8_t slot_idx;
694	    perf_rec_strip_t *r = strip_slot_claim(frame_epoch, kind, x, y, w, h, honor_mask, &slot_idx);
695	    if (r == NULL) { return; }
696	
697	    const uint32_t row_bytes = (uint32_t)w * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
698	    const uint8_t *src = frame + (uint32_t)y * frame_stride + (uint32_t)x * PERF_STRIP_BPP;
699	    uint8_t *dst = r->bgr;
700	    for (uint16_t row = 0u; row < h; row++)
701	    {
702	        memcpy(dst, src, row_bytes);
703	        src += frame_stride;
704	        dst += row_bytes;
705	    }
706	
707	    strip_slot_commit(slot_idx);
708	}
709	
710	void PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(uint32_t frame_epoch,
711	                                perf_strip_kind_t kind,
712	                                const uint8_t *frame, uint32_t frame_stride,
713	                                uint16_t x, uint16_t y,
714	                                uint16_t w, uint16_t h)
715	{
716	    emit_strip_from_frame(frame_epoch, kind, frame, frame_stride, x, y, w, h, true);
717	}
718	
719	void PerfLog_EmitStripPacked(uint32_t frame_epoch,
720	                             perf_strip_kind_t kind,
721	                             uint16_t x, uint16_t y,
722	                             uint16_t w, uint16_t h,
723	                             const uint8_t *pixels)
724	{
725	    if (pixels == NULL) { return; }
726	
727	    uint8_t slot_idx;
728	    perf_rec_strip_t *r = strip_slot_claim(frame_epoch, kind, x, y, w, h, true, &slot_idx);
729	    if (r == NULL) { return; }
730	
731	    memcpy(r->bgr, pixels, (uint32_t)w * (uint32_t)h * PERF_STRIP_BPP);
732	    strip_slot_commit(slot_idx);
733	}
734	
735	/* ─── Emit (ISR context) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
736	
737	void PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(perf_stage_t stage,
738	                              uint32_t frame_epoch,
739	                              uint32_t aux,
740	                              BaseType_t *higher_priority_task_woken)
741	{
742	    if (s_state_q == NULL) { return; }
743	    if (!type_enabled(PERF_REC_STAMP)) { return; }
744	    perf_rec_state_slot_t slot;
745	    memset(&slot, 0, sizeof(slot));
746	    hdr_fill(&slot.stamp.hdr, PERF_REC_STAMP, PERF_FLAG_FROM_ISR, frame_epoch);
747	    slot.stamp.stage_id = (uint8_t)stage;
748	    slot.stamp.aux      = aux;
749	    if (xQueueSendFromISR(s_state_q, &slot, higher_priority_task_woken) != pdTRUE)
750	    {
751	        counter_add_isr(&s_drop_state, 1u);
752	    }
753	}
754	
755	/* ─── Sink-side drop accounting ──────────────────────────────────────────── */
756	
757	void PerfLog_NoteSinkDrop(uint32_t bytes_dropped)
758	{
759	    counter_add_task(&s_drop_sink, bytes_dropped);
760	}
761	
762	/* ─── Snapshot request ───────────────────────────────────────────────────── */

116	 * closed-loop. Blind-strums the signed delta from the observed cursor (sticky-
117	 * default-safe), then re-observes and repeats if it under/overshoots. GREEN is
118	 * pressed only once the observed cursor == target while still on `expect_screen`.
119	 * Returns false (never pressing GREEN) if the screen isn't the expected one, the
120	 * selection is unreadable, or the cursor won't settle — the caller recovers. */
121	static bool select_and_confirm(uint8_t expect_screen, int target)
122	{
123	    for (int attempt = 0; attempt < GC_MAX_CONFIRM; attempt++)
124	    {

126	        if (!observe(&sc, &cur))     { return false; }
127	        if (sc != expect_screen)     { return false; }
128	        if (cur < 0)                 { return false; }
129	        if ((int)cur == target)      { send_input(GC_GREEN); return true; }
130	
131	        int delta = target - (int)cur;
132	        uint8_t move = (delta > 0) ? GC_STRUM_DOWN : GC_STRUM_UP;
133	        int n = gc_abs(delta);
134	        if (n > GC_MAX_MOVE) { n = GC_MAX_MOVE; }
135	        for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { send_input(move); }
