175	}
176	
177	/* Move to the top item and GREEN — the always-want-the-top steps (FULL SONG /
178	 * FULL SPEED = index 0). Where the row is readable (speed_select) strum up until
179	 * the selection reports the top (strumming up can't overshoot — no wrap). Where
180	 * it isn't (section_select has no row reader) GREEN through, assuming the top is
181	 * already selected — we only reach it with FULL SONG selected. See
182	 * firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md for the deferred section_select FULL SONG reader.
183	 * Returns false only if the screen isn't the expected one or an observation fails. */
184	static bool saturate_top(uint8_t expect_screen)
185	{
186	    uint8_t sc; int16_t cur;
187	    if (!observe(&sc, &cur)) { return false; }
188	    if (sc != expect_screen) { return false; }
189	
190	    for (int i = 0; i < GC_SATURATE_STRUMS && cur > 0; i++)
191	    {
192	        send_input(GC_STRUM_UP);
193	        if (!observe(&sc, &cur)) { return false; }
194	        if (sc != expect_screen) { return false; }
195	    }
196	    send_input(GC_GREEN);
197	    return true;
198	}
199	
200	static bool wait_for(uint8_t target, uint32_t timeout_ms)
201	{
202	    TickType_t start = xTaskGetTickCount();
203	    for (;;)
204	    {
205	        uint8_t sc; int16_t sel;
206	        if (observe(&sc, &sel) && sc == target) { return true; }
207	        if (s_stop_req) { return false; }
208	        if ((TickType_t)(xTaskGetTickCount() - start) > pdMS_TO_TICKS(timeout_ms)) { return false; }
209	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(GC_STEP_POLL_MS));
210	    }
211	}
212	
213	/* Block until the observed screen leaves `from` (the transition completed) or a
214	 * timeout. This is what keeps a step from re-firing on a not-yet-transitioned
215	 * screen — and prevents a stray confirm/strum from leaking onto the next screen. */
216	static bool wait_screen_change(uint8_t from, uint32_t timeout_ms)
217	{
218	    TickType_t start = xTaskGetTickCount();
219	    for (;;)
220	    {
221	        uint8_t sc; int16_t sel;
222	        if (observe(&sc, &sel) && sc != from) { return true; }
223	        if (s_stop_req) { return false; }
224	        if ((TickType_t)(xTaskGetTickCount() - start) > pdMS_TO_TICKS(timeout_ms)) { return false; }
225	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(GC_STEP_POLL_MS));
226	    }
227	}
228	
229	/* ── plan ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
230	
231	static void build_plan(const selection_t *sel)
232	{
233	    int n = 0;
234	    s_plan[n++] = (gc_step_t){ GP_SCREEN_main_menu,        ACT_SELECT_INDEX, 4, GP_SCREEN_training_menu,    "TRAINING" };
235	    s_plan[n++] = (gc_step_t){ GP_SCREEN_training_menu,    ACT_SELECT_INDEX, 1, GP_SCREEN_song_select,      "PRACTICE" };
236	    s_plan[n++] = (gc_step_t){ GP_SCREEN_song_select,      ACT_SELECT_SONG,  0, GP_SCREEN_part_select,      "song" };
237	    s_plan[n++] = (gc_step_t){ GP_SCREEN_part_select,      ACT_SELECT_INDEX, 0, GP_SCREEN_difficulty_select,"LEAD" };
238	    s_plan[n++] = (gc_step_t){ GP_SCREEN_difficulty_select,ACT_SELECT_INDEX, (int16_t)sel->difficulty, GP_SCREEN_section_select, "difficulty" };
239	    s_plan[n++] = (gc_step_t){ GP_SCREEN_section_select,   ACT_SATURATE_TOP, 0, GP_SCREEN_speed_select,     "FULL SONG" };
240	    s_plan[n++] = (gc_step_t){ GP_SCREEN_speed_select,     ACT_SATURATE_TOP, 0, GP_SCREEN_loading,          "FULL SPEED" };
241	    s_plan[n++] = (gc_step_t){ GP_SCREEN_loading,          ACT_WAIT,         0, GP_SCREEN_in_song,          "loading" };
242	    s_plan_len = n;
243	}
244	
245	static const gc_step_t *step_for(uint8_t screen)
246	{
247	    for (int i = 0; i < s_plan_len; i++)
248	    {
249	        if (s_plan[i].from == screen) { return &s_plan[i]; }
250	    }
251	    return NULL;
252	}
253	
254	/* Run a step closed-loop. Returns true only if the step's activation was
255	 * confirmed (cursor landed then GREEN, or the WAIT reached its target); false
256	 * means "did not activate" — the caller re-observes and retries / recovers. */
257	static bool execute(const gc_step_t *st)
258	{
259	    switch (st->act)
260	    {
261	        case ACT_SELECT_INDEX:  return select_and_confirm(st->from, st->index);
262	        case ACT_SELECT_SONG:   return select_song();
263	        case ACT_SATURATE_TOP:  return saturate_top(st->from);
264	        case ACT_WAIT:          return wait_for(st->to, GC_LOADING_TIMEOUT_MS);
265	        default:                return false;
266	    }
267	}
268	
269	/* ── run ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
270	
271	/* Release the wire, disable CV, report a terminal status. */
272	static void finish(const char *st)
273	{
274	    TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false);   /* also sends one release */
275	    status(st);
276	    s_busy = false;
277	}
278	
279	/* Return to main_menu from wherever we are. RED backs up the forward-nav menus,
280	 * but the terminal overlays (practice-end / quit-confirm / pause) don't reliably
281	 * accept RED, so QUIT out of those explicitly. Used both to anchor a run and to
282	 * clear the end-of-song menus when a run finishes. */
283	static bool nav_to_main_menu(void)
284	{
285	    for (int i = 0; i < GC_MAX_EXIT_ITERS; i++)
286	    {
287	        uint8_t sc; int16_t sel;
288	        if (!observe(&sc, &sel)) { vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(GC_SETTLE_MS)); continue; }
289	        if (sc == GP_SCREEN_main_menu) { return true; }
290	        if (s_stop_req) { return false; }
291	
292	        switch (sc)
293	        {
294	            case GP_SCREEN_practice_end_menu: (void)select_and_confirm(sc, 4); break;  /* QUIT → main_menu */
295	            case GP_SCREEN_quit_confirm:      (void)select_and_confirm(sc, 1); break;  /* QUIT (confirm) → main_menu */
296	            case GP_SCREEN_pause_menu:        (void)select_and_confirm(sc, 6); break;  /* QUIT → quit_confirm */
297	            default:                          send_input(GC_RED);              break;  /* back up one level */
298	        }
299	        (void)wait_screen_change(sc, GC_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS);
300	    }
301	    uint8_t sc; int16_t sel;
302	    return observe(&sc, &sel) && sc == GP_SCREEN_main_menu;
303	}
304	
305	/* CV plays; hold until the song ends (practice_end_menu), we leave gameplay, or
306	 * Stop is requested. Poll via observe() to detect the end — a classify during
307	 * in_song is cheap (no song-match). The timing pipeline actuates for the whole
308	 * enabled window; the controller owns that window (enable here, disable on exit). */
309	static void play_until_done(void)
310	{
311	    status("PLAYING");
312	    TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(true);   /* controller owns the actuation window */
313	    TickType_t play_start = xTaskGetTickCount();
314	    DashboardFeed_PostPlaytime(0u);    /* reset the dashboard playtime bar (run reset the rest) */
315	
316	    uint32_t final_score = 0u;   /* last CV-read score this run (the song total) */
317	    uint16_t peak_streak = 0u;   /* longest note streak this run — persists across misses */
318	
319	    for (;;)
320	    {
321	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(GC_PLAY_POLL_MS));
322	        if (s_stop_req) { break; }
323	
324	        DashboardFeed_PostPlaytime((uint32_t)(xTaskGetTickCount() - play_start)
325	                                   * portTICK_PERIOD_MS);
326	
327	        /* Observe the full state so the CV-read score can ride the dashboard feed;
328	         * the same read detects the song ending (screen leaves gameplay). */
329	        game_state_t gs;
330	        if (GameplayEngine_Observe(&gs, GC_OBS_TIMEOUT_MS))
331	        {
332	            if (gs.screen == GP_SCREEN_in_song)
333	            {
334	                if (gs.score >= 0) { final_score = (uint32_t)gs.score; DashboardFeed_PostScore(final_score); }
335	                if (gs.multiplier >= 1u) { DashboardFeed_PostMultiplier(gs.multiplier); }
336	                if (gs.streak > peak_streak) { peak_streak = gs.streak; }
337	                DashboardFeed_PostStreak(gs.streak);
338	            }
339	            else if (gs.screen != GP_SCREEN_loading && gs.screen != GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN)
340	            {
341	                break;   /* song ended (practice_end_menu) or left gameplay */
342	            }
343	        }
344	    }
345	
346	    uint32_t play_ms = (uint32_t)(xTaskGetTickCount() - play_start) * portTICK_PERIOD_MS;
347	    LOG_INFO("GC: playtime %lu.%03lu s\r\n",
348	             (unsigned long)(play_ms / 1000u), (unsigned long)(play_ms % 1000u));
349	    /* Run result — the values the results writer will persist once the score-file
350	     * write path is wired (spec §4.8.6 Results_Append). */
351	    LOG_INFO("GC: result score %lu, peak streak %u\r\n",
352	             (unsigned long)final_score, (unsigned)peak_streak);
353	
354	    /* Leave GH3 on the end screen; just release CV and go idle. The next run's
355	     * anchor (nav_to_main_menu) QUITs out of the end/pause menus when START is
356	     * pressed again. */
357	    finish("READY");
358	}
359	
360	/* Make sure fauxmote is connected to the Wii before a run (it's the actuation path
361	 * to the console). Reconnect if the link is bonded-but-down; sets a descriptive
362	 * status and returns false if it can't get there. */
363	#if (MARVIN_FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT == FRETBOARD_TRANSPORT_T1S)
364	static bool ensure_wii_connected(void)
365	{
366	    uint8_t flags;
367	    if (!Fauxmote_GetStatus(&flags, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL))
368	    {
369	        /* No STATUS from fauxmote (UART link down / not running) — can't manage the
370	         * BT link here; proceed so a T1S guitar can still actuate. */
371	        LOG_WARN("GC: no fauxmote status; skipping Wii connect check\r\n");
372	        return true;
373	    }
374	    if (flags & MF_ST_CONNECTED) { return true; }
375	    if (!(flags & MF_ST_BONDED))
376	    {
377	        status("PAIR WII");   /* never synced — needs a manual red-SYNC pairing */
378	        return false;
379	    }
380	
381	    status("CONNECTING");
382	    Fauxmote_SendCmd(MF_CMD_RECONNECT);
383	    TickType_t start = xTaskGetTickCount();
384	    while ((TickType_t)(xTaskGetTickCount() - start) < pdMS_TO_TICKS(GC_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS))
385	    {
386	        if (s_stop_req) { return false; }
387	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(500));
388	        if (Fauxmote_GetStatus(&flags, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL) && (flags & MF_ST_CONNECTED))
389	        {
390	            return true;
391	        }
392	    }
393	    status("NO WII");
394	    return false;
395	}
396	#else
397	static bool ensure_wii_connected(void) { return true; }
398	#endif
399	
400	static void run(void)
401	{
402	    const selection_t *sel = Selection_Get();
403	    if (!sel->valid)
404	    {
405	        status("NO SONG");
406	        return;
407	    }
408	
409	    s_busy = true;
410	
411	    /* Clear the ROBOT telemetry the instant a run is requested — score/multiplier/
412	     * streak zero out on Play, without waiting to navigate into gameplay. */
413	    DashboardFeed_PostScore(0u);
414	    DashboardFeed_PostMultiplier(1u);
415	    DashboardFeed_PostStreak(0u);
416	
417	    /* Pre-flight: the Wii link must be up (fauxmote is how we reach the console). */
418	    if (!ensure_wii_connected())
419	    {
420	        s_busy = false;   /* status already set (CONNECTING→NO WII / PAIR WII) */
421	        return;
422	    }
423	
424	    status("NAVIGATING");
425	
426	    /* Own the wire: manual off, timing off (set timing off *after* manual, since
427	     * ManualControl_SetEnabled(false) flips timing on — the arbitration trap). */
428	    if (ManualControl_IsEnabled()) { ManualControl_SetEnabled(false); }
429	    TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false);
430	
431	    if (!nav_to_main_menu())
432	    {
433	        finish(s_stop_req ? "READY" : "FAILED");
434	        return;
435	    }
436	
437	    build_plan(sel);
438	
439	    int recover = 0;
440	    int confirm_fail = 0;
441	    for (int iter = 0; iter < GC_MAX_ITERS; iter++)
442	    {
443	        if (s_stop_req) { finish("READY"); return; }
444	
445	        uint8_t sc; int16_t s;
446	        if (!observe(&sc, &s)) { continue; }
447	
448	        if (sc == GP_SCREEN_in_song)
449	        {
450	            play_until_done();
451	            return;
452	        }
453	
454	        const gc_step_t *st = step_for(sc);
455	        if (st != NULL)
456	        {
457	            LOG_INFO("GC: %s\r\n", st->desc);
458	            if (execute(st))
459	            {
460	                /* Wait for the transition off this screen before re-evaluating, so
461	                 * the same step can't re-fire (and a stray input can't hit the next
462	                 * screen). ACT_WAIT already blocked until its target screen. */
463	                if (st->act != ACT_WAIT)
464	                {
465	                    (void)wait_screen_change(st->from, GC_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS);
466	                }
467	                recover = 0;
468	                confirm_fail = 0;
469	            }
470	            else
471	            {
472	                /* Couldn't confirm the cursor/activation on a known screen — never
473	                 * press GREEN blind. Re-observe and retry; give up if it persists. */
474	                if (++confirm_fail > GC_MAX_CONFIRM_FAIL) { finish("FAILED"); return; }
475	                LOG_INFO("GC: unconfirmed on screen %u — retrying\r\n", (unsigned)sc);
476	            }
477	        }
478	        else
479	        {
480	            if (++recover > GC_MAX_RECOVER) { finish("FAILED"); return; }
481	            LOG_INFO("GC: recover (RED) from screen %u\r\n", (unsigned)sc);
482	            send_input(GC_RED);
483	            (void)wait_screen_change(sc, GC_STEP_TIMEOUT_MS);
484	        }
485	    }
486	    finish("FAILED");   /* step budget exhausted */
487	}
488	
489	static void gc_task(void *param)
490	{
491	    (void)param;
492	    for (;;)
493	    {
494	        if (xSemaphoreTake(s_start_sig, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
495	        run();
496	    }
497	}

517	    (void)xSemaphoreGive(s_start_sig);
518	}

80	    mask: int = 0xFFFFFFFF
81	    # Mirrors the device's boot default (PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP on). Tracked so a
82	    # late-attaching WS client can render the toggle in the right state.
83	    overlay_enabled: bool = True
84	    # Region stream (score-block capture). Off at device boot; the strips ride
85	    # the normal record path into the capture .bin like any other record.
86	    region_enabled: bool = False
87	    region_rect: tuple[int, int, int, int] = DEFAULT_REGION_RECT
88	    started_at: str | None = None
89	    framing_stats: FrameStats = field(default_factory=FrameStats)
90	    last_session_dict: dict[str, Any] | None = None
91	    # Most-recent framed bytes of records that should be prepended to a
92	    # new recording so the bin is self-contained from byte 0. Keyed by
93	    # record-class name. SESSION is one-shot per sink-attach (firmware
94	    # only emits it on connect-up edge) so without prepending we'd miss
95	    # timer_freq_hz. DETECTOR_CONFIG re-emits at ~1 Hz, but a short
96	    # capture might end before the next heartbeat — prepending keeps
97	    # STRIP-overlay rendering correct even on sub-second captures.
98	    prepend_framed: dict[str, bytes] = field(default_factory=dict)

64	static void console_write_char(EmbeddedCli *cli, char c)
65	{
66	    (void)cli;
67	    /* TX ring drains at line rate regardless of any listener (the UART clocks
68	     * bytes onto the wire), so a bounded retry only ever waits for ring space,
69	     * never for a reader. Cap it so a pathological full-ring can't spin. */
70	    for (uint32_t tries = 0u; tries < 1000u; tries++)
71	    {
72	        if (FLEXCOM2_USART_Write((uint8_t *)&c, 1u) == 1u) { return; }
73	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(1));
74	    }
75	}

89	static int parse_onoff(const char *s)

93	    if (strcmp(s, "off") == 0 || strcmp(s, "0") == 0) { return 0; }

97	static int parse_detector(const char *s)
98	{
99	    if (s == NULL) { return -1; }
100	    if (strcmp(s, "cv") == 0)  { return DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1; }
101	    if (strcmp(s, "adc") == 0) { return DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD; }
102	    return -1;
103	}
104	
105	static int parse_fret(const char *s)
106	{
107	    if (s == NULL || s[0] == '\0' || s[1] != '\0') { return -1; }
108	    switch (s[0])
109	    {
110	        case 'g': case 'G': return FRET_GREEN;
111	        case 'r': case 'R': return FRET_RED;
112	        case 'y': case 'Y': return FRET_YELLOW;
113	        case 'b': case 'B': return FRET_BLUE;
114	        case 'o': case 'O': return FRET_ORANGE;
115	        default:            return -1;
116	    }
117	}
118	
119	static uint32_t parse_u32(const char *s, uint32_t dflt)
120	{
121	    if (s == NULL || s[0] == '\0') { return dflt; }
122	    uint32_t v = 0u;
123	    for (const char *p = s; *p != '\0'; p++)
124	    {
125	        if (*p < '0' || *p > '9') { return dflt; }
126	        v = (v * 10u) + (uint32_t)(*p - '0');
127	    }
128	    return v;
129	}
130	
131	/* Pull up to n non-negative integers out of s, separated by any run of
132	 * non-digit characters (so "2026-06-23" and "14:03:00" both parse). Returns
133	 * the count parsed. */
134	static int parse_ints(const char *s, int *out, int n)
135	{
136	    int got = 0;
137	    if (s == NULL) { return 0; }
138	    while (got < n && *s != '\0')
139	    {
140	        while (*s != '\0' && (*s < '0' || *s > '9')) { s++; }
141	        if (*s < '0' || *s > '9') { break; }
142	        int v = 0;
143	        while (*s >= '0' && *s <= '9') { v = (v * 10) + (*s - '0'); s++; }
144	        out[got++] = v;
145	    }
146	    return got;
147	}
148	
149	/* Day of week (0 = Sunday) for a Gregorian date, matching struct tm's tm_wday.
150	 * Sakamoto's method; m is 1-12. */
151	static int day_of_week(int y, int m, int d)
152	{
153	    static const int t[] = { 0, 3, 2, 5, 0, 3, 5, 1, 4, 6, 2, 4 };
154	    if (m < 3) { y -= 1; }
155	    return (y + y / 4 - y / 100 + y / 400 + t[m - 1] + d) % 7;
156	}

219	static void cmd_time(EmbeddedCli *cli, char *args, void *ctx)
220	{
221	    (void)cli; (void)ctx;
222	    const char *sub = embeddedCliGetToken(args, 1);
223	
224	    if (sub == NULL)
225	    {
226	        struct tm now;
227	        memset(&now, 0, sizeof(now));
228	        RTC_TimeGet(&now);
229	        int wd = (now.tm_wday >= 0 && now.tm_wday <= 6) ? now.tm_wday : 0;
230	        console_printf("%04d-%02d-%02dT%02d:%02d:%02dZ (%s)",
231	                       now.tm_year + 1900, now.tm_mon + 1, now.tm_mday,
232	                       now.tm_hour, now.tm_min, now.tm_sec, k_wday[wd]);
233	        return;
234	    }
235	
236	    if (strcmp(sub, "set") == 0)
237	    {
238	        int ymd[3], hms[3];
239	        if (parse_ints(embeddedCliGetToken(args, 2), ymd, 3) != 3 ||
240	            parse_ints(embeddedCliGetToken(args, 3), hms, 3) != 3)
241	        {
242	            console_printf("usage: time set YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS  (UTC)");
243	            return;
244	        }
245	        int Y = ymd[0], Mo = ymd[1], D = ymd[2];
246	        int h = hms[0], mi = hms[1], s = hms[2];
247	        if (Y < 1970 || Y > 2099 || Mo < 1 || Mo > 12 || D < 1 || D > 31 ||
248	            h > 23 || mi > 59 || s > 59)
249	        {
250	            console_printf("out of range (expect UTC YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)");
251	            return;
252	        }
253	
254	        struct tm t;
255	        memset(&t, 0, sizeof(t));
256	        t.tm_year = Y - 1900;
257	        t.tm_mon  = Mo - 1;
258	        t.tm_mday = D;
259	        t.tm_hour = h;
260	        t.tm_min  = mi;
261	        t.tm_sec  = s;
262	        t.tm_wday = day_of_week(Y, Mo, D);
263	
264	        if (RTC_TimeSet(&t))
265	        {
266	            console_printf("set %04d-%02d-%02dT%02d:%02d:%02dZ", Y, Mo, D, h, mi, s);
267	        }
268	        else
269	        {
270	            console_printf("RTC set failed");
271	        }
272	        return;
273	    }
274	
275	    console_printf("usage: time [set YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS]");
276	}

819	/* ---- transport ---------------------------------------------------------- */
820	
821	static void rx_event_handler(FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT event, uintptr_t context)
822	{
823	    (void)context;
824	    BaseType_t hpw = pdFALSE;
825	
826	    switch (event)
827	    {
828	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_THRESHOLD_REACHED:
829	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_BUFFER_FULL:
830	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
831	            break;
832	        case FLEXCOM_USART_EVENT_READ_ERROR:
833	            (void)FLEXCOM2_USART_ErrorGet();
834	            (void)xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(s_rx_notify, &hpw);
835	            break;
836	        default:
837	            break;
838	    }
839	
840	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(hpw);
841	}
842	
843	static void console_task(void *param)
844	{
845	    (void)param;
846	
847	    LOG_INFO("CON: console started (FLEXCOM2)\r\n");
848	
849	    for (;;)
850	    {
851	        if (FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadCountGet() == 0u)
852	        {
853	            (void)xSemaphoreTake(s_rx_notify, pdMS_TO_TICKS(CON_RX_WAIT_MS));
854	        }
855	
856	        uint8_t c;
857	        while (FLEXCOM2_USART_Read(&c, 1u) == 1u)
858	        {
859	            embeddedCliReceiveChar(s_cli, (char)c);
860	        }
861	
862	        embeddedCliProcess(s_cli);
863	    }
864	}
865	
866	void Console_Initialize(void)
867	{
868	    EmbeddedCliConfig *cfg = embeddedCliDefaultConfig();
869	    cfg->invitation        = "marvin> ";
870	    cfg->rxBufferSize      = 64u;
871	    cfg->cmdBufferSize     = 64u;
872	    cfg->historyBufferSize = 128u;
873	    cfg->maxBindingCount   = 24u;
874	    cfg->enableAutoComplete = true;
875	    cfg->cliBuffer         = s_cli_buf;
876	    cfg->cliBufferSize     = sizeof(s_cli_buf);
877	
878	    configASSERT(embeddedCliRequiredSize(cfg) <= sizeof(s_cli_buf));
879	
880	    s_cli = embeddedCliNew(cfg);
881	    configASSERT(s_cli != NULL);
882	    s_cli->writeChar = console_write_char;
883	
884	    register_commands();
885	
886	    s_rx_notify = xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(&s_rx_notify_buf);
887	    configASSERT(s_rx_notify != NULL);
888	
889	    /* Arm continuous RX: the ring fills from the FLEXCOM2 ISR; a persistent
890	     * 1-byte threshold notification wakes console_task on each inbound byte. */
891	    FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadCallbackRegister(rx_event_handler, 0u);
892	    FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadThresholdSet(CON_RX_THRESHOLD);
893	    (void)FLEXCOM2_USART_ReadNotificationEnable(true, true);
894	
895	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(console_task,
896	                            "Console",
897	                            CON_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
898	                            NULL,
899	                            CON_TASK_PRIORITY,
900	                            s_task_stack,
901	                            &s_task_tcb);
902	}

13	 * Single-finger momentary model. Legato's input dispatch routes each touch

15	 * inputs aren't supported here — would require a custom maxtouch dispatcher,
16	 * and menu navigation doesn't need them.
17	 *
18	 * Mode arbitration with timing_pipeline lives in SetEnabled: entering manual
19	 * mode gates the pipeline off, exiting hands the wire back. */

33	 * detector-driven gameplay path (timing_pipeline) does its own one-shot

I have everything I need. Here is the detailed architecture map.

---

# Marvin CV Detector Architecture Map

All paths under `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/`.

## 1. `game/fret.h` — the shared fret primitive

The `fret_t` enum lives in the game domain (shared by detector, actuator, UI), not in detector/:

```c
typedef enum {
    FRET_GREEN=0, FRET_RED=1, FRET_YELLOW=2, FRET_BLUE=3, FRET_ORANGE=4,
    FRET_COUNT=5,
} fret_t;
```

`FRET_COUNT` (5) sizes the per-fret arrays in `detector_state_t` and every static table in `cv_marvin_v1.c`. This is per-highway/per-player conceptually but currently there's exactly one set. For two-player you'd have two independent highways each with 5 frets — the enum itself is fine (frets are the same colors), but every `[FRET_COUNT]`-sized static in cv_marvin_v1 is single-instance (see §4).

---

## 2. `detector/detector.h` + `detector/detector.c` — bus / registry / enable-disable API

### Public API surface (detector.h)
- `void Detector_Initialize(void)` — brings up the bus queue and calls `CvMarvinV1_Initialize()`. Must run after `Video_Initialize`.
- `QueueHandle_t Detector_BusQueue(void)` — the single shared "detector-state bus" all producers post to; NULL before init.
- `void Detector_Enable(detector_id_t id)` / `Detector_Disable(...)` / `bool Detector_IsEnabled(...)` — per-detector publish gate, backed by a bitmask.
- `void Detector_SetActive(detector_id_t id)` / `detector_id_t Detector_GetActive(void)` — which detector the (future) timing pipeline acts on; single active at a time.

### Key enum/struct (detector.h)

`detector_id_t` (detector.h:24-28) — **this is the registry namespace.** Only two IDs today, and they identify detector *algorithms/sources*, not player highways:
```c
typedef enum {
    DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1  = 0,
    DETECTOR_ADC_FRETBOARD = 1,
} detector_id_t;
```
Note for two-player: the enable-mask and active-selector are keyed on `detector_id_t`. If 2p means two instances of the *same* algorithm (2p-left / 2p-right), the current scheme has no way to distinguish them — the id is both the algorithm identity and the on-the-wire `detector_id` field. You'd need either new enum ids (e.g. `DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1_P2`) or a separate player/highway dimension.

`detector_state_t` (detector.h:33-45) — the canonical bus record AND the on-disk `state.bin` format (fixed layout, do not reorder). Carries `detector_id` (uint8) and a `fret[FRET_COUNT]` array of `{pressed, confidence, raw_value}`. There is **no player/highway field** — a two-player design must decide whether to distinguish records by `detector_id`, add a field (schema bump per the header's warning at :30-32), or run two buses.

### Registry implementation (detector.c) — all module-level static
```c
#define DETECTOR_BUS_DEPTH 8u                              // :11
static QueueHandle_t   s_bus_queue;                        // :13  single shared bus
static StaticQueue_t   s_bus_queue_buf;                    // :14
static uint8_t         s_bus_queue_storage[...];           // :15
static volatile uint32_t s_enabled_mask;                   // :17  bit N = detector_id N
static volatile uint8_t  s_active_id = DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1; // :18
```
- Enable/disable are `1u << id` bit ops in a critical section (:36-48); `Detector_IsEnabled` is a lock-free bit test (:50-53).
- `Detector_Initialize` (:20-29): creates the static bus queue, `configASSERT`s it, then calls `CvMarvinV1_Initialize()` directly. **This is the sole wiring from the registry into the CV detector** — the registry hard-codes the one detector's init call. Adding instances means adding calls here (or a table).
- The bus is a single queue shared by all producers/consumers; depth 8 sized for "~one detector × one frame-time at 60 Hz" (:8-10) — two producers at 60 Hz would want a rethink of depth.

---

## 3. `detector/cv_marvin_v1.h` — the CV detector's public surface

Entire public API is one function (cv_marvin_v1.h:9):
```c
void CvMarvinV1_Initialize(void);
```
No handle returned, no parameters, no instance concept. Everything else in the module is file-static.

---

## 4. `detector/cv_marvin_v1.c` — task, subscription, publish, and ALL single-instance static state

### How the task is created (cv_marvin_v1.c:479-489)
```c
void CvMarvinV1_Initialize(void)
{
    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(cv_marvin_v1_task,
                                       "CvMarvinV1",
                                       CV_TASK_STACK_WORDS,   // 1024
                                       NULL,                  // no param passed
                                       CV_TASK_PRIORITY,      // 4
                                       s_task_stack,          // static
                                       &s_task_tcb);          // static
    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1, h);
}
```
Static task creation with a **static stack (`s_task_stack`, :97) and TCB (`s_task_tcb`, :98)**, a **hard-coded task name `"CvMarvinV1"`**, and **`NULL` param** — there is no mechanism to pass an instance/context pointer to the task. It also registers a single perf-log highwater slot `PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1`. Two instances would each need their own stack/TCB, a unique name, a distinct perf-log task id, and a context arg (the `void *param` is currently `(void)param`'d at :380).

### How it subscribes to video frames (cv_marvin_v1.c:382-388, inside the task)
```c
QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,   // depth 1, drop-intermediate
                                          sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
                                          s_frame_queue_storage,   // static, :89
                                          &s_frame_queue_buf);     // static, :88
configASSERT(frames != NULL);
bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
configASSERT(subscribed);
```
The frame queue is built from **static storage (`s_frame_queue_storage` :89, `s_frame_queue_buf` :88)** with `CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH = 1` (:18, "drop-intermediate policy"). It then grabs the shared bus via `Detector_BusQueue()` (:390-391).

### How it publishes `detector_state_t` (cv_marvin_v1.c:170-218, `detect_frame`)
Builds a `detector_state_t` on the stack, sets `frame_epoch = frame->frame_count`, `timestamp_us` from tick count, and `detector_id = DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1` (**hard-coded** at :176 — a second instance would still stamp the same id unless changed). Fills `state.fret[i]` for each fret, then `xQueueSend(bus, &state, 0)` (:218, non-blocking). Also mirrors the decision to the perf-log via `PerfLog_EmitDetector` (:236-237).

### The task loop and gating (cv_marvin_v1.c:397-476)
Blocks on `xQueueReceive(frames, ..., portMAX_DELAY)`. Always drains; only processes when `Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)` (:403 — again the hard-coded id gates this instance). Validates `frame.buffer`, `width/height`, and `bytes_per_pixel == CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL` (:404-406). Emits perf stamps, runs `detect_frame`, republishes config at ~1 Hz (:417), and ships STRIKE/SENSING/REGION strips to the host viewer.

### ALL module-level `static` state that is inherently single-instance

**Const config tables (read-only, but describe one highway's geometry — would need per-instance copies or per-instance calibration for 2p, since left/right highways sit at different screen coords):**
- `s_sensor_coords[FRET_COUNT]` (:56-63) — `sensor_xy_t` sample points in native 720×480 capture space. **Hard-coded to one highway's pixel positions.** For 2p-left/2p-right these are the *primary* thing that differs (two highways = two coordinate sets). Currently `static const`.
- `s_color_filter[FRET_COUNT]` (:71-78) — per-fret BGR target/reject weights. `static const`, could be shared read-only across instances but the config-publish path treats them as this-detector's config.
- `s_overlay_hold_bgr[3]` (:249) and `s_overlay_edge_bgr[FRET_COUNT][3]` (:250-257) — overlay colors, `static const`, shareable.

**Mutable per-fret detector state (the core problem — one set of frets, would be corrupted if two instances shared it):**
```c
static float    s_hold_dist[FRET_COUNT];    // :82
static float    s_edge_dist[FRET_COUNT];    // :83
static bool     s_pressed[FRET_COUNT];      // :84  hold latch, hysteresis state
static bool     s_edge_active[FRET_COUNT];  // :85  edge-detect latch
static uint32_t s_press_count[FRET_COUNT];  // :86  rising-edge counter
```
These carry frame-to-frame hysteresis/latch state (:192-200, :202, :233-234, :334-343). Two players pressing frets independently would clobber each other's press/edge latches. **These must become per-instance for 2p.**

**Task/queue/scratch statics (single-instance resources):**
```c
static StaticQueue_t s_frame_queue_buf;                         // :88
static uint8_t       s_frame_queue_storage[...];                // :89  frame queue backing
static uint8_t       s_sensing_scratch[W*H*3];                  // :95  strip-overlay scratch
static StackType_t   s_task_stack[CV_TASK_STACK_WORDS];         // :97  task stack
static StaticTask_t  s_task_tcb;                                // :98  task TCB
```
`s_sensing_scratch` (:95) is a shared paint buffer written each frame (:438-452); two tasks writing it concurrently would tear. The queue backing, stack, and TCB are all one-per-module.

**Module-level `#define` constants that bake in one highway's geometry:** `CV_SENSING_X/Y/W/H` (:39-42) and `CV_STRIKE_X/Y/W/H` (:43-46) — the host-viewer strip regions, hard-coded to one highway's location on screen. Thresholds `CV_HOLD_THRESH`, `CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC`, `CV_EDGE_THRESH` (:30-32) are shareable but are published as "this detector's config."

### Perf-log coupling (would also need per-instance identity)
- `PerfLog_EmitDetector(...)` (:236) — one detector's ground-truth stream.
- `publish_detector_config()` (:353-374) emits `perf_rec_detector_config_t` built from the static tables — "the single point that re-publishes" (:349-352). A second instance needs its own config channel/identity.
- `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame/EmitStripPacked/EmitRegionIfEnabled` and `PERF_STRIP_SENSING`/`PERF_STRIP_STRIKE` (:423-457) — single strip identities per region; two highways would collide on these host-viewer strip slots.

---

## 5. `app.c` / `app.h` — how the detector is wired into startup

### `CvMarvinV1_Initialize` is NOT called from app.c directly
It's called indirectly: `App_StartServices()` → `Detector_Initialize()` → `CvMarvinV1_Initialize()`. App only touches the registry API.

### Startup path
- `APP_Initialize()` (app.c:117-166) sets up only splash-critical modules (log, UI manager, perf-log producer queues, storage, results, catalog, art). It registers `app_on_splash_shown` (:132) as the splash callback. The video/detector/actuator/console are explicitly deferred (:161-165).
- `app_on_splash_shown()` (:98-101) simply calls `App_StartServices()`.
- `App_StartServices()` (app.c:174-239) — **task creation order matters:**
  1. `Video_Initialize()` (:178) — first, because it owns the frame queue the detector subscribes to.
  2. `Detector_Initialize()` (:184), then `Detector_Enable(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)` (:185) and `Detector_SetActive(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)` (:186). **This is the only place the CV detector is enabled/selected.** For 2p you'd enable/select both highways here (and today there's no distinct id to enable a second one).
  3. `FretboardLink_Initialize()`, optional `Fauxmote_Initialize()`, `TimingPipeline_Initialize()` (:202 — the future consumer of the active detector), `ManualControl_Initialize()`, `GameplayEngine_Initialize()` (:218 — another video-frame subscriber), `GameController_Initialize()`, `Console_Initialize()` (:228 — can drive detector setters), `PerfLog_Start()`, `HealthMonitor_Initialize()`.
- `APP_Tasks()` (app.c:250-264) is a one-shot; logs heap and `vTaskDelete(NULL)`.

The comment at app.c:182-186 confirms the intended model: "Detectors default disabled; enable + select the active one for the timing pipeline." `TimingPipeline` (:199-202) "runs … against the active detector" — so the active-selector currently assumes a single winner, which conflicts with two simultaneously-active highways.

---

## 6. `video/video.h` — frame subscription / queue model

### Public API
- `void Video_Initialize(void)` — capture disabled, no callbacks by default.
- `Video_CaptureEnable/Disable(void)`.
- `Video_SetFrameLatchCallback(...)` / `Video_SetDisplayReconcileCallback(...)` — compositor HEO hooks (ISR + task tick).
- `bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)` (:76) / `bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)` (:79).
- `void Video_GetFrameInfo(Video_FrameInfo *info)` (:83) — non-blocking synchronous read.
- `bool Video_GetActiveRect(uint16_t *x,*y,*w,*h)` (:97) — runtime-detected active-picture rectangle (letterbox crop).

### `Video_FrameInfo` struct (video.h:45-52)
```c
typedef struct {
    void    *buffer;          /* most-recent complete frame in DDR */
    uint32_t frame_count;     /* monotonic since last ISC start */
    uint16_t width;
    uint16_t height;
    uint16_t bytes_per_pixel;
} Video_FrameInfo;
```
It carries a pointer to the **full** frame plus dimensions — no per-highway cropping. Both 2p highways would receive the identical full frame and each crop/sample its own region via its own `s_sensor_coords`.

### Queue / subscriber model (video.h:54-79) — **this is the good news for 2p**
- **Multiple subscribers are explicitly supported.** The ISC frame-done IRQ does `xQueueSendFromISR` to **every** subscribed queue (:55-57). Up to `VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS` concurrent (documented as **currently 4**, :74-75). Today the CV detector uses 1 slot and the gameplay engine uses another, so there is headroom for a second CV instance.
- Each subscriber creates its own queue and **chooses its own depth / back-pressure policy independently** (:59-72). Depth 1 = "process most recent, drop the rest"; on full, the IRQ's send returns `errQUEUE_FULL` and drops for that subscriber only.
- Re-subscribing an already-present queue is a no-op success; `Video_SubscribeFrames` returns false only if the table is full (:73-75).

So a two-player refactor can create a second frame queue and subscribe it without touching the video module — the fan-out already handles N subscribers. The constraint is `VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS` (4), shared with the gameplay engine and any other consumers.

---

## Summary of two-player / pluggable-detector friction points

Single-instance couplings that a refactor must address (all in cv_marvin_v1.c unless noted):
1. **Hard-coded `detector_id` identity** at build/enable/publish time: detector.c registry keys enable-mask and active-selector on `detector_id_t` (only 2 algorithm ids exist); cv_marvin_v1 stamps and gates on `DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1` literally (cv_marvin_v1.c:176, :403). No player/highway dimension exists in `detector_state_t` (detector.h:33-45) — and that struct is also the on-disk format, so adding a field is a schema bump.
2. **Mutable per-fret latch state** `s_hold_dist/s_edge_dist/s_pressed/s_edge_active/s_press_count` (cv_marvin_v1.c:82-86) — must be per-instance.
3. **Task resources** `s_task_stack/s_task_tcb` (:97-98), hard-coded task name `"CvMarvinV1"`, `NULL` param (no context passed to the task, :383/:380), single perf highwater id `PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1` (:488).
4. **Frame-queue + scratch statics** `s_frame_queue_buf/_storage` (:88-89), `s_sensing_scratch` (:95).
5. **Geometry baked in**: `s_sensor_coords` (:56-63) and the `CV_SENSING_*` / `CV_STRIKE_*` strip defines (:39-46) describe one highway's screen position — the primary per-player difference.
6. **Registry wiring** hard-codes one init call: `Detector_Initialize` → `CvMarvinV1_Initialize()` (detector.c:28); app enables/selects exactly one (app.c:184-186); `TimingPipeline` assumes a single "active" detector (app.c:199-202).
7. **Video is already multi-subscriber** (video.h:74-75, up to 4) — the frame-distribution side does *not* block two instances; the constraint is the shared `VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS` budget.

## How gameplay mode / player context is represented in marvin today

### Summary answer up front

There **is** a 1P-vs-2P notion in the firmware, but it lives **only** in the operator-facing UI selection (`sel_mode_t`), and it is a dead-end today: nothing downstream of the song-select dialog reads it. The **screen classifier has no concept of players** — `GP_SCREEN_in_song` is a single class with no 1p/2p variant. The **CV detector is hardwired to one highway of 5 frets**. So today the system would learn "we are in 2-player mode" only from the human who tapped the 2P radio button in song-select; it is never derived from video, and the automation ignores it entirely.

---

### 1. The `game/` directory — how "screen" is classified and where player/mode lives

**Screen classification** is a nearest-centroid fingerprint match with a fixed 13-class vocabulary. `game/gameplay_metadata.h:17-37`:

```
#define GP_N_SCREENS 13
#define GP_SCREEN_in_song 1        // ← single class, no 1p/2p variant
... difficulty_select, loading, main_menu, part_select, pause_menu,
    practice_end_menu, quit_confirm, section_select, song_select,
    speed_select, training_menu, tutorials_menu
```

`gp_classify()` (`game/gameplay_classify.h:19`) returns one of these indices or `GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN`. **There is no `in_song_2p`, no player count, no highway index** anywhere in the classifier or its metadata.

`game_state_t` (`game/gameplay_engine.h:22-34`) is the published event. Its fields — `screen`, `selection`, `score`, `multiplier`, `streak` — are all **single-valued**. There is no per-player score/streak, no player-count field. The `selection` field is a menu cursor cell or song-template index, not a player.

The only place the strings "multiplayer" / "co_op" appear is as **menu item labels** for cursor navigation, not screen classes — `game/gameplay_metadata.h:58`:
```c
gp_menu_main_menu_items[7] = {"career","co_op_career","quickplay","multiplayer","training","options","nintendo_wfc"};
```
These are cells the navigator can move a cursor onto; they don't tell the firmware anything about being *in* a 2-player song.

**The actual 1P/2P notion** is `sel_mode_t` in `game/selection.h:22-36`:
```c
typedef enum { SEL_MODE_1P_ROBOT = 0, SEL_MODE_1P_HUMAN, SEL_MODE_2P } sel_mode_t;
typedef struct {
    bool valid; uint8_t setlist; uint8_t index;
    uint8_t difficulty; uint8_t mode;   /* sel_mode_t */
} selection_t;
```
This is a **committed operator choice**, set via `Selection_Set(...)`.

**Who sets it / reads it (the whole picture):**
- Set once: `ui/screens/song_select/screen_song_select.c:336` — `Selection_Set(e->setlist, e->index, s_difficulty, s_mode)`, where `s_mode` comes from a 3-way radio group (`1P_ROBOT / 1P_HUMAN / 2P_ROBOT_vs_HUMAN`, lines 50-94, 133-138).
- Read for display only: `ui/screens/dashboard/screen_dashboard.c:205-207,307` — `mode_text()` renders "1P ROBOT / 1P HUMAN / 2P R vs H".
- **Not read anywhere else.** Critically, `game_controller.c`'s `build_plan()` (`game/game_controller.c:231-243`) hardcodes a **single-player Training→Practice→LEAD** path and never inspects `sel->mode`. It reads `sel->difficulty`, `sel->setlist`, `sel->index` only (`select_song()` at line 144, `build_plan` at line 238). So even in `SEL_MODE_2P` the controller navigates the same 1P practice highway.

### 2. Detector output consumers and the single-highway assumption

`detector_state_t` (`detector/detector.h:33-45`) carries exactly `fret[FRET_COUNT]` = **5 frets, one set** (`game/fret.h:9-17`, `FRET_COUNT = 5`). There is one shared detector-state bus (`Detector_BusQueue()`), and the **timing pipeline is the sole consumer** (`actuator/timing_pipeline.h:7-9`, filtered by `Detector_GetActive()`).

**The single-highway assumption is baked into the CV detector geometry** — `detector/cv_marvin_v1.c:56-63`:
```c
static const sensor_xy_t s_sensor_coords[FRET_COUNT] = {
    [FRET_GREEN]  = { 280, 311, 293, 311 },
    [FRET_RED]    = { 317, 311, 330, 311 },
    [FRET_YELLOW] = { 355, 311, 368, 311 },
    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 393, 311, 380, 311 },
    [FRET_ORANGE] = { 430, 311, 417, 311 },
};
```
One hardcoded set of 5 sensor coordinates in 720×480 space, anchored to a single (left/only) highway. The detect loop iterates `for (i=0; i<FRET_COUNT; i++)` over these (line 183). There is no second coordinate set for a right-player highway, and no parameterization by player.

**Actuator path:** `FretboardLink_Send(mask, producer_id)` (`actuator/fretboard_link.h:40`) ferries a single **7-bit GPIO bitmask** (5 frets + 2 strum bits, `actuator/timing_pipeline.h:22-30`) to one fretboard MCU. One wire, one guitar. Nothing in this path is player-indexed.

### 3. The existing "mode / producer arbiter" pattern you could mirror

Two distinct selection patterns already exist:

**(a) Detector active-selector** (`detector/detector.h:69-74`):
```c
void          Detector_SetActive(detector_id_t id);
detector_id_t Detector_GetActive(void);
```
Multiple detectors may be *enabled* (publish to the bus) but only one is *active* (the timing pipeline acts on it). `detector_id_t` currently = `{CV_MARVIN_V1, ADC_FRETBOARD}` (`detector.h:24-28`). Selected at boot in `app.c:185-186` and switchable live via the console `active` command (`console/console.c:507-518`).

**(b) Actuator producer arbiter** — the "who owns the wire" pattern. Producers self-tag with `perf_actuator_producer_t` (`perf_log/perf_log_records.h:337-343`): `NONE / TIMING / MANUAL / GAMEPLAY`. The arbitration itself is **mutual-exclusion via enable flags**, implemented in `actuator/manual_control.c:42-67`:
```c
void ManualControl_SetEnabled(bool enabled) {
    if (enabled) { TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false); s_enabled = true; }   // gate peer, take wire
    else { s_enabled = false; TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(true); }           // release, hand back
}
```
And the game controller asserts ownership the same way (`game/game_controller.c:428-429`): turns manual off, timing off, drives menus itself, then `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(true)` during `play_until_done()` (line 312). `FretboardLink` itself stays "dumb" latest-wins (`fretboard_link.h:30-37`); arbitration lives one layer up. This enable-gate + producer-tag pattern is the closest existing template for a mode arbiter.

### 4. The console / CLI

Yes — a full embedded-cli command surface in `console/console.c`. Relevant bring-up commands (registered at `console.c:786-811`):
- `detect <cv|adc> <on|off>` → `Detector_Enable/Disable` (`cmd_detect`, line 491)
- `active <cv|adc>` → `Detector_SetActive` (`cmd_active`, line 507) — the manual "which detector" selector
- `timing <on|off>` (line 520), `manual <on|off>` (line 533) — producer enable toggles
- `fret <g|r|y|b|o> <0|1>` and `strum <down|up>` (lines 546, 564) — direct single-highway actuation
- `play [stop|status]` → `GameController_Start/Stop` (line 756), which reads the committed `Selection` (setlist/index/difficulty — **not mode**, line 780)

`parse_detector()` (line 97) only knows `cv`/`adc`. There is **no console command that selects player count, highway, or 1p/2p mode** today — the only mode-ish knob is the detector active-selector, which is orthogonal to players.

---

### How the system would currently learn it is in 2-player mode

1. **From the screen classifier?** No. `GP_SCREEN_in_song` is one undifferentiated class; the recognizer metadata has no 2p centroid/variant.
2. **From a manual command?** No. The console has detector/producer/actuation toggles but nothing that sets player count or 1p/2p.
3. **From the operator UI?** Partially — this is the *only* source. A human taps the `2P` radio in song-select, which sets `selection_t.mode = SEL_MODE_2P` (`selection.c:13`). But that value is consumed **only by the dashboard label** (`screen_dashboard.c:307`). The navigator (`game_controller.c`), the CV detector (`cv_marvin_v1.c`), the timing pipeline, and the fretboard link **all ignore it** and behave identically to 1P.

So in practice: **the game's actual 1p/2p state is not represented at the detection/actuation layer at all.** The single authority that "knows" is the operator's radio-button choice held in `selection_t.mode`, and that knowledge currently dies at the dashboard label — it never reaches the detector, which remains locked to one 5-fret highway.

**Most relevant files for your planned work:**
- `game/selection.h` (the existing `sel_mode_t`, the one place 1p/2p is modeled)
- `detector/cv_marvin_v1.c:56-63` (single hardcoded highway geometry — the thing that must become player-aware)
- `detector/detector.h` (`detector_state_t`, the enable/active-selector arbiter pattern)
- `actuator/manual_control.c:42-67` + `perf_log_records.h:337-343` (the producer/enable arbiter to mirror)
- `game/game_controller.c:231-243` (the navigator that ignores `sel->mode` today)
- `console/console.c:97-103,491-518` (where a mode/detector selector command would slot in)
</output>

**The actual 1P/2P notion** is `sel_mode_t` in `game/selection.h:22-36`:

typedef enum { SEL_MODE_1P_ROBOT = 0, SEL_MODE_1P_HUMAN, SEL_MODE_2P } sel_mode_t;

    uint8_t difficulty; uint8_t mode;   /* sel_mode_t */
} selection_t;
```
This is a **committed operator choice**, set via `Selection_Set(...)`.

**Who sets it / reads it (the whole picture):**
- Set once: `ui/screens/song_select/screen_song_select.c:336` — `Selection_Set(e->setlist, e->index, s_difficulty, s_mode)`, where `s_mode` comes from a 3-way radio group (`1P_ROBOT / 1P_HUMAN / 2P_ROBOT_vs_HUMAN`, lines 50-94, 133-138).
- Read for display only: `ui/screens/dashboard/screen_dashboard.c:205-207,307` — `mode_text()` renders "1P ROBOT / 1P HUMAN / 2P R vs H".

It reads `sel->difficulty`, `sel->setlist`, `sel->index` only (`select_song()` at line 144, `build_plan` at line 238). So even in `SEL_MODE_2P` the controller navigates the same 1P practice highway.

### 2. Detector output consumers and the single-highway assumption

`detector_state_t` (`detector/detector.h:33-45`) carries exactly `fret[FRET_COUNT]` = **5 frets, one set** (`game/fret.h:9-17`, `FRET_COUNT = 5`). There is one shared detector-state bus (`Detector_BusQueue()`), and the **timing pipeline is the sole consumer** (`actuator/timing_pipeline.h:7-9`, filtered by `Detector_GetActive()`).

**The single-highway assumption is baked into the CV detector geometry** — `detector/cv_marvin_v1.c:56-63`:
```c
static const sensor_xy_t s_sensor_coords[FRET_COUNT] = {
    [FRET_GREEN]  = { 280, 311, 293, 311 },
    [FRET_RED]    = { 317, 311, 330, 311 },
    [FRET_YELLOW] = { 355, 311, 368, 311 },
    [FRET_BLUE]   = { 393, 311, 380, 311 },
    [FRET_ORANGE] = { 430, 311, 417, 311 },
};
```
One hardcoded set of 5 sensor coordinates in 720×480 space, anchored to a single (left/only) highway. The detect loop iterates `for (i=0; i<FRET_COUNT; i++)` over these (line 183). There is no second coordinate set for a right-player highway, and no parameterization by player.

**Actuator path:** `FretboardLink_Send(mask, producer_id)` (`actuator/fretboard_link.h:40`) ferries a single **7-bit GPIO bitmask** (5 frets + 2 strum bits, `actuator/timing_pipeline.h:22-30`) to one fretboard MCU. One wire, one guitar. Nothing in this path is player-indexed.

### 3. The existing "mode / producer arbiter" pattern you could mirror

Two distinct selection patterns already exist:

**(a) Detector active-selector** (`detector/detector.h:69-74`):
```c
void          Detector_SetActive(detector_id_t id);
detector_id_t Detector_GetActive(void);
```
Multiple detectors may be *enabled* (publish to the bus) but only one is *active* (the timing pipeline acts on it). `detector_id_t` currently = `{CV_MARVIN_V1, ADC_FRETBOARD}` (`detector.h:24-28`). Selected at boot in `app.c:185-186` and switchable live via the console `active` command (`console/console.c:507-518`).

**(b) Actuator producer arbiter** — the "who owns the wire" pattern. Producers self-tag with `perf_actuator_producer_t` (`perf_log/perf_log_records.h:337-343`): `NONE / TIMING / MANUAL / GAMEPLAY`. The arbitration itself is **mutual-exclusion via enable flags**, implemented in `actuator/manual_control.c:42-67`:
```c
void ManualControl_SetEnabled(bool enabled) {
    if (enabled) { TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(false); s_enabled = true; }   // gate peer, take wire
    else { s_enabled = false; TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(true); }           // release, hand back
}
```
And the game controller asserts ownership the same way (`game/game_controller.c:428-429`): turns manual off, timing off, drives menus itself, then `TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(true)` during `play_until_done()` (line 312). `FretboardLink` itself stays "dumb" latest-wins (`fretboard_link.h:30-37`); arbitration lives one layer up. This enable-gate + producer-tag pattern is the closest existing template for a mode arbiter.

### 4. The console / CLI

Yes — a full embedded-cli command surface in `console/console.c`. Relevant bring-up commands (registered at `console.c:786-811`):
- `detect <cv|adc> <on|off>` → `Detector_Enable/Disable` (`cmd_detect`, line 491)
- `active <cv|adc>` → `Detector_SetActive` (`cmd_active`, line 507) — the manual "which detector" selector
- `timing <on|off>` (line 520), `manual <on|off>` (line 533) — producer enable toggles
- `fret <g|r|y|b|o> <0|1>` and `strum <down|up>` (lines 546, 564) — direct single-highway actuation
- `play [stop|status]` → `GameController_Start/Stop` (line 756), which reads the committed `Selection` (setlist/index/difficulty — **not mode**, line 780)

`parse_detector()` (line 97) only knows `cv`/`adc`. There is **no console command that selects player count, highway, or 1p/2p mode** today — the only mode-ish knob is the detector active-selector, which is orthogonal to players.

### How the system would currently learn it is in 2-player mode

1. **From the screen classifier?** No. `GP_SCREEN_in_song` is one undifferentiated class; the recognizer metadata has no 2p centroid/variant.
2. **From a manual command?** No. The console has detector/producer/actuation toggles but nothing that sets player count or 1p/2p.
3. **From the operator UI?** Partially — this is the *only* source. A human taps the `2P` radio in song-select, which sets `selection_t.mode = SEL_MODE_2P` (`selection.c:13`). But that value is consumed **only by the dashboard label** (`screen_dashboard.c:307`). The navigator (`game_controller.c`), the CV detector (`cv_marvin_v1.c`), the timing pipeline, and the fretboard link **all ignore it** and behave identically to 1P.

So in practice: **the game's actual 1p/2p state is not represented at the detection/actuation layer at all.** The single authority that "knows" is the operator's radio-button choice held in `selection_t.mode`, and that knowledge currently dies at the dashboard label — it never reaches the detector, which remains locked to one 5-fret highway.

- `game/game_controller.c:231-243` (the navigator that ignores `sel->mode` today)
- `console/console.c:97-103,491-518` (where a mode/detector selector command would slot in)

### Detector-id / instance-id in the config record — ANSWER: NONE
`perf_rec_detector_config_t` carries **no detector-id or instance-id field**. 43	static uint8_t       s_frame_queue_storage[GAME_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH * sizeof(Video_FrameInfo)];
44	
45	static StackType_t   s_task_stack[GAME_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
46	static StaticTask_t  s_task_tcb;
47	
48	static volatile bool s_req_pending;
49	
50	/* Streak tracker state: advanced by the observer across in_song reads, reset when
51	 * gameplay is left (owned solely by game_task; not shared). */
52	static gp_streak_state_t s_streak;
53	
54	static const char *screen_name(uint8_t idx)
55	{
56	    return (idx < GP_N_SCREENS) ? gp_screen_ids[idx] : "unknown";
57	}
58	
59	/* Read the selection for the classified screen: static-list cell index, the
60	 * song-template index on song_select, or -1 where there's no selection concept
61	 * (gameplay / loading / unknown). `name`/`name2` receive log-friendly labels. */
62	static int16_t read_selection(const uint8_t *frame, int w, int h, uint8_t screen,
63	                              const char **name, const char **name2)
64	{
65	    *name = NULL;
66	    *name2 = NULL;
67	    const gp_menu_layout_t *menu = gp_menu_for_screen(screen);
68	    if (menu != NULL)
69	    {
70	        int cell = gp_read_selection(frame, w, h, menu);
71	        if (cell >= 0 && cell < menu->count) { *name = menu->items[cell]; }
72	        return (int16_t)cell;
73	    }
74	    if (screen == GP_SCREEN_song_select)
75	    {
76	        gp_song_t song;
77	        if (gp_read_song(frame, w, h, &song) == 0 && song.tmpl >= 0)
78	        {
79	            *name = (song.setlist == GP_SETLIST_BONUS) ? "bonus" : "main";
80	            *name2 = gp_song_templates[song.tmpl].song_id;
81	            return song.tmpl;
82	        }
83	    }
84	    return -1;
85	}
86	
87	static void game_task(void *param)
88	{
89	    (void)param;
90	
91	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(GAME_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
92	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
93	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
94	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
95	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
96	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
97	    configASSERT(subscribed);
98	
99	    LOG_INFO("GAME: gameplay_engine started\r\n");
100	
101	    uint8_t   last_screen = GP_SCREEN_UNKNOWN;
102	    int16_t   last_sel    = -2;  /* != any real selection or -1, so first read logs */
103	    bool      armed       = false;  /* pre-request frame discarded; next one is fresh */
104	
105	    for (;;)
106	    {
107	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
108	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
109	
110	        /* Drain every frame so the queue never backs up. Classify only while a
111	         * request is pending — no free-running scan. */
112	        if (!s_req_pending) { armed = false; continue; }
113	
114	        /* The frame in hand when the request arrived predates it; skip it so the
115	         * classified frame is guaranteed to have been captured after the request. */
116	        if (!armed) { armed = true; continue; }
117	
118	        /* A bad frame leaves the request pending so the next valid one serves it. */
119	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                          { continue; }
120	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != GAME_BYTES_PER_PIXEL) { continue; }
121	
122	        TickType_t now = xTaskGetTickCount();
123	        const uint8_t *buf = (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer;
124	        int w = (int)frame.width, h = (int)frame.height;
125	
126	        int32_t best_dist = 0, margin = 0;
127	        uint8_t screen = gp_classify(buf, w, h, &best_dist, &margin);
128	
129	        const char *sel_name = NULL, *sel_name2 = NULL;
130	        int16_t sel = read_selection(buf, w, h, screen, &sel_name, &sel_name2);
131	
132	        /* In-song: read the open-ended score (training font) + multiplier + the note
133	         * streak. Sentinels (-1 / 0) elsewhere. The streak tracker is stateful: it
134	         * advances across in_song observations and resets whenever gameplay is left
135	         * (a fresh run re-seeds from the odometer). */
136	        int32_t score = -1;
137	        uint8_t multiplier = 0;
138	        uint16_t streak = 0;
139	        if (screen == GP_SCREEN_in_song)
140	        {
141	            gp_score_t sc;
142	            if (gp_read_score(buf, w, h, GP_SCORE_MODE_TRAINING, &sc) == 0) { score = sc.value; }
143	            multiplier = (uint8_t)gp_read_multiplier(buf, w, h);
144	            gp_streak_raw_t sr;
145	            if (gp_read_streak(buf, w, h, &sr) == 0) { streak = gp_streak_track(&s_streak, &sr); }
146	        }
147	        else
148	        {
149	            gp_streak_reset(&s_streak);
150	        }
151	
152	        game_state_t ev;
153	        memset(&ev, 0, sizeof(ev));
154	        ev.frame_epoch  = frame.frame_count;
155	        ev.timestamp_us = (uint64_t)now * GAME_US_PER_TICK;
156	        ev.screen       = screen;
157	        ev.best_dist    = best_dist;
158	        ev.margin       = margin;
159	        ev.selection    = sel;
160	        ev.score        = score;
161	        ev.multiplier   = multiplier;
162	        ev.streak       = streak;
163	
164	        /* Answer the requester first (clear pending before the send so a follow-up
165	         * Observe that wakes on the response can't have its new request cleared). */
166	        armed = false;
167	        taskENTER_CRITICAL();
168	        s_req_pending = false;
169	        taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
170	        (void)xQueueSend(s_resp_queue, &ev, 0);
171	
172	        if (screen != last_screen || sel != last_sel)
173	        {
174	            (void)xQueueSend(s_bus_queue, &ev, 0);
175	
176	            if (sel_name2 != NULL)  /* song_select: "<setlist> #<idx> <song>" */
177	            {
178	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s / %s #%d %s\r\n",
179	                         screen_name(screen), sel_name,
180	                         (int)gp_song_templates[sel].index, sel_name2);
181	            }
182	            else if (sel_name != NULL)  /* static-list: "<screen> / <item>" */
183	            {
184	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s / %s\r\n", screen_name(screen), sel_name);
185	            }
186	            else if (screen == GP_SCREEN_in_song)  /* "in_song / score N x<mult> streak<s>" */
187	            {
188	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s / score %ld x%u streak%u\r\n",
189	                         screen_name(screen), (long)score, (unsigned)multiplier, (unsigned)streak);
190	            }
191	            else
192	            {
193	                LOG_INFO("GAME: %s\r\n", screen_name(screen));
194	            }
195	            last_screen = screen;
196	            last_sel    = sel;
197	        }
198	    }
199	}
200	
201	void GameplayEngine_Initialize(void)
202	{
203	    s_bus_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(GAME_BUS_DEPTH,
204	                                     sizeof(game_state_t),
205	                                     s_bus_queue_storage,
206	                                     &s_bus_queue_buf);
207	    configASSERT(s_bus_queue != NULL);
208	
209	    s_resp_queue = xQueueCreateStatic(1, sizeof(game_state_t),
210	                                      s_resp_queue_storage, &s_resp_queue_buf);
211	    configASSERT(s_resp_queue != NULL);
212	
213	    (void)xTaskCreateStatic(game_task, "GameEngine", GAME_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
214	                            NULL, GAME_TASK_PRIORITY, s_task_stack, &s_task_tcb);
215	}
216	
217	QueueHandle_t GameplayEngine_BusQueue(void)
218	{
219	    return s_bus_queue;
220	}
221	
222	bool GameplayEngine_Observe(game_state_t *out, uint32_t timeout_ms)
223	{
224	    if (out == NULL) { return false; }
225	
226	    /* Discard any stale response (e.g. from a prior timed-out request), then post
227	     * the request and block for the result. */
228	    game_state_t drain;
229	    while (xQueueReceive(s_resp_queue, &drain, 0) == pdTRUE) { }
230	
231	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
232	    s_req_pending = true;
233	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
234	
235	    return (xQueueReceive(s_resp_queue, out, pdMS_TO_TICKS(timeout_ms)) == pdTRUE);
236	}
237
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 18:56:00Z)**_

Critical detail: `gameplay_engine` is a **synchronous request/response observer** — it only classifies when `GameplayEngine_Observe()` is called (by the controller), not free-running. So config selection happens at gameplay *entry* (once per song, mode doesn't change mid-song), not per-frame. That plus the "left-only, human P2, fauxmote" scope makes this a right-sized, phaseable change. Let me write the plan.

# Plan — CV detector: config-selectable for 1p vs 2p-left (robot) highway

## Context

Marvin's note detector (`cv_marvin_v1`, spec §4.2) is hard-wired to one highway: a single
file-static `s_sensor_coords[FRET_COUNT]` and single `CV_SENSING_*`/`CV_STRIKE_*` strip ROIs, all
anchored to the single-player centered highway. We want marvin to play the **left (robot) highway of
a 2-player game** — a different, smaller, perspective-skewed highway whose sensor coordinates we just
calibrated (host-side, recorded in `tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md`, 2026-07-14).

Confirmed scope (Greg):
- **Left/robot highway only.** P2 (right) is a **human** — no right-side detector, no second detector
  instance, no two-guitar actuation, no `detector_state_t`/perf-log schema changes.
- The CV detector must be **config-selectable** between the **1p** and **2p-left** highway geometry —
  this is the "pass in configuration" seam the refactor is about.
- The **screen classifier must distinguish 1p in_song from 2p in_song** so the correct config can be
  applied from what's on screen (not just the operator radio button).
- **Fauxmote** is the actuation sink for the robot in this test (existing plumbing — marvin still
  drives its one guitar exactly as in 1p; only the *detector geometry* differs).

Outcome: on a live 2-player game, marvin samples the left highway's five lanes at the calibrated
2p-left coordinates and drives its guitar, with the mode chosen from the on-screen 1p/2p distinction
(and a console override for bench bring-up).

## Design overview

Keep **one** `cv_marvin_v1` task (single instance — one robot highway). Lift its geometry out of
file-scope `const`/`#define`s into a **passed-in config struct**, provide two `const` configs
(`1P`, `2P_LEFT`), and add a setter to swap the active config at runtime. Selection is driven at
gameplay entry by the screen class (`in_song` → 1p, `in_song_2p` → 2p-left), with a console override.
Color filters and thresholds stay shared (note colors are identical); they can move into the config
later if the 2p highway needs different thresholds.

This is deliberately **not** a full multi-instance/vtable refactor — that's unneeeded while only the
left highway is detected. The config seam leaves the door open (a future second highway or algorithm
would add a second instance behind the same config type).

Phased so Greg can validate the calibrated 2p-left coords on real hardware **first** (via the console
override + host viewer), exactly like the original 1p bring-up, before the classifier/auto-select
work.

## Phase 1 — Parameterize `cv_marvin_v1` by a config struct + console override

**`detector/cv_marvin_v1.h`** — add the public config type + API:
\```c
typedef struct { uint16_t hx, hy, ex, ey; } cv_sensor_xy_t;   /* was file-static sensor_xy_t */
typedef struct {
    const char     *name;                  /* "1p" / "2p-left" — log + config publish */
    cv_sensor_xy_t  sensor[FRET_COUNT];
    uint16_t sensing_x, sensing_y, sensing_w, sensing_h;   /* host-viewer SENSING strip */
    uint16_t strike_x,  strike_y,  strike_w,  strike_h;    /* host-viewer STRIKE strip  */
} cv_marvin_v1_config_t;

extern const cv_marvin_v1_config_t CV_MARVIN_CFG_1P;
extern const cv_marvin_v1_config_t CV_MARVIN_CFG_2P_LEFT;

void CvMarvinV1_Initialize(void);
void CvMarvinV1_SetConfig(const cv_marvin_v1_config_t *cfg);  /* swap active geometry */
const cv_marvin_v1_config_t *CvMarvinV1_GetConfig(void);
\```

**`detector/cv_marvin_v1.c`** changes:
- Replace the file-static `s_sensor_coords` and the `CV_SENSING_*`/`CV_STRIKE_*` `#define`s with the
  two `const cv_marvin_v1_config_t` tables. `CV_MARVIN_CFG_1P` = today's values (coords
  `{280,317,355,393,430}` hold / `{293,330,368,380,417}` edge @ y311; SENSING `(265,300,185,32)`;
  STRIKE `(212,395,290,32)`). `CV_MARVIN_CFG_2P_LEFT` = the calibrated values:

  | fret | hx | hy | ex | ey |
  |--|--|--|--|--|
  | G | 166 | 311 | 176 | 311 |
  | R | 195 | 311 | 204 | 311 |
  | Y | 223 | 311 | 233 | 311 |
  | B | 251 | 311 | 242 | 311 |
  | O | 279 | 311 | 269 | 311 |

  SENSING `(150,300,155,32)`, STRIKE `(120,395,205,34)` (cover the 2p-left sensor row + rings; tunable
  in the host viewer during bring-up).
- Add `static const cv_marvin_v1_config_t *volatile s_active_cfg = &CV_MARVIN_CFG_1P;` (default 1p) and
  a `s_pending_cfg`. `CvMarvinV1_SetConfig` stores to `s_pending_cfg`. The task, at the top of each
  loop iteration, picks up a changed pending config, swaps `s_active_cfg`, **resets the per-fret latch
  state** (`s_hold_dist/s_edge_dist/s_pressed/s_edge_active/s_press_count`), and re-publishes detector
  config. Lock-light; a config change is a rare event.
- `detect_frame`, the SENSING/STRIKE strip copy, `draw_overlay`, and `publish_detector_config` all read
  `sensor`/strip ROIs from `s_active_cfg` instead of the removed statics. `publish_detector_config`
  keeps emitting the (shared) thresholds/color filters unchanged.
- Size `s_sensing_scratch` to the **max** of the two SENSING strips (1p's 185×32 dominates) via a
  `CV_SENSING_MAX_W/H` constant, so a config swap can't overflow it.
- `detector_id` stamping (`DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1`) and the enable/active gate are unchanged — still one
  detector identity.

**`console/console.c`** — add a `cvcfg <1p|2pl>` command (mirror `cmd_detect`/`cmd_active` at
`console.c:491-518`): calls `CvMarvinV1_SetConfig`; bare `cvcfg` prints `CvMarvinV1_GetConfig()->name`.
This is the bring-up/validation tool.

*Phase-1 gate: Greg builds in MPLAB, runs a live 2-player game, `detect cv on` + `cvcfg 2pl`, opens the
host viewer, confirms the SENSING overlay rings land on the left highway's five lanes and the fret P/E
flags fire on notes — the on-hardware analog of the host `sense_marked.png` overlay.*

## Phase 2 — Distinguish 1p vs 2p `in_song` in the screen classifier

Host-side, in `tools/gameplay/` (uv env; set `UV_CACHE_DIR=$TMPDIR/uv-cache`):
- Add screen id `in_song_2p` to the screen id map and label the available 2p frames
  (`tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/snapshot-0200..0203.png` + `web-20260714-112721.png`) into the corpus
  as that class.
- Re-run `gameplay export-c` to regenerate
  `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_metadata.h` (adds `GP_SCREEN_in_song_2p`, its centroid,
  and the screen-id table entry). This file is generated (not MCC) — safe to regenerate.
- Run the `tools/gameplay` pytest suite + `gameplay eval` to confirm 1p `in_song` still classifies as
  `in_song` and the 2p frames classify as `in_song_2p` (they're visually very distinct — two highways,
  different stage — so a whole-frame centroid should separate them cleanly).

Firmware consumers of `GP_SCREEN_in_song`:
- `gameplay_engine.c:139` — the 1p score/multiplier/streak readers stay gated on `GP_SCREEN_in_song`
  **only** (2p uses the separate amp scoreboards, a different WIP). `in_song_2p` publishes screen state
  but runs no 1p readers.
- `game_controller.c` — wherever it treats `in_song` as "gameplay active" for the play/handoff logic,
  accept `in_song_2p` as gameplay too.

Caveat: only ~5 labelled 2p frames today (single-centroid, no LOO). Fine for a visually-distinct class;
capture more 2p `in_song` frames later to measure in-class spread (mirrors the existing single-sample
class note in the gameplay journal open questions).

## Phase 3 — Auto-select config at gameplay entry + fauxmote

- **Auto-select:** in `game_controller.c`, at the loading→gameplay transition it already observes via
  `GameplayEngine_Observe`. Use the observed screen to set the detector geometry once per run:
  `in_song_2p` → `CvMarvinV1_SetConfig(&CV_MARVIN_CFG_2P_LEFT)`, `in_song` → `..._1P`. (Optionally seed
  from `selection_t.mode == SEL_MODE_2P` as a hint; the screen class is authoritative.) The console
  `cvcfg` override remains for bench use.
- **Fauxmote / actuation:** marvin still drives its single guitar exactly as in 1p — the actuation path
  (`FretboardLink` / `Fauxmote`, enabled in `app.c` `App_StartServices`) is **unchanged**. Confirm the
  fauxmote sink is enabled for the 2p run; no detector-side change. (If "fauxmote activation" means a
  specific enable step in the 2p flow, it's a small wiring confirmation — quick look at
  `Fauxmote_Initialize`/the actuator arbiter, not a detector change.)

## Files touched

- `firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.h` — config type + setter API.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c` — config tables, active/pending config,
  read-from-config, scratch sizing.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/console/console.c` — `cvcfg` command.
- `tools/gameplay/` (host) — screen id map, corpus labels, re-export.
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_metadata.h` — regenerated (`in_song_2p`).
- `firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_engine.c` / `game_controller.c` — accept `in_song_2p`;
  controller sets config at gameplay entry.
- Journals: `tools/gameplay/docs/journal.md` + `firmware/marvin/docs/journal.md` — record decisions.

## Non-goals (explicit)

- No right-highway (P2) detection — P2 is human.
- No second detector task/instance, no full detector vtable.
- No `detector_state_t` / `state.bin` / perf-log schema change (single detector identity, single
  highway on the bus and host viewer).
- No two-guitar actuation.

## Verification

- **Host (Phase 2):** `cd tools/gameplay && UV_CACHE_DIR=$TMPDIR/uv-cache uv run pytest`; `gameplay
  eval` shows 1p `in_song` and the 2p frames classify to the correct classes; `gameplay classify` on a
  2p snapshot prints `in_song_2p`.
- **Firmware compile:** the pure units (`cv_marvin_v1.c` geometry read) compile under `cc -Wall
  -Wextra` where applicable; Greg builds the full image in MPLAB.
- **On hardware (Phase 1 gate):** live 2-player game → `detect cv on`, `cvcfg 2pl` → host viewer SENSING
  overlay rings sit on the left highway's five gems; fret P/E flags fire on notes; matches the
  host-calibrated overlay. `cvcfg 1p` restores single-player behavior (regression check on a 1p game).
- **Integrated (Phase 3):** start a 2p run via the normal play path; confirm the controller switched to
  `2P_LEFT` config automatically (log line) and marvin actuates the left highway.

  a `s_pending_cfg`. `CvMarvinV1_SetConfig` stores to `s_pending_cfg`. The task, at the top of each
  loop iteration, picks up a changed pending config, swaps `s_active_cfg`, **resets the per-fret latch
  state** (`s_hold_dist/s_edge_dist/s_pressed/s_edge_active/s_press_count`), and re-publishes detector
  config. Lock-light; a config change is a rare event.

  `sensor`/strip ROIs from `s_active_cfg` instead of the removed statics. `publish_detector_config`
  keeps emitting the (shared) thresholds/color filters unchanged.

  `CV_SENSING_MAX_W/H` constant, so a config swap can't overflow it.
- `detector_id` stamping (`DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1`) and the enable/active gate are unchanged — still one

```h
#ifndef CV_MARVIN_V1_H
#define CV_MARVIN_V1_H

#include <stdint.h>

#include "game/fret.h"

/* Reference vision detector. Owns its FreeRTOS task; subscribes to the video
 * module's frame queue; publishes detector_state_t records onto the detector-
 * state bus (spec §4.2).
 *
 * Geometry (per-fret sample points + host-viewer strip regions) is a passed-in
 * config so the one detector can read either the single-player centered highway
 * or the 2-player left (robot) highway. Note colors and thresholds are shared
 * across configs (the gems are identical); they stay module-internal. */

/* Per-fret sample points in native 720×480 capture space: (hx,hy) = brightness
 * sensor, (ex,ey) = color-filtered edge sensor. */
typedef struct { uint16_t hx, hy, ex, ey; } cv_sensor_xy_t;

typedef struct
{
    const char     *name;         /* "1p" / "2p-left" — logged, not on the wire */
    cv_sensor_xy_t  sensor[FRET_COUNT];
    /* Host-viewer strips (capture-frame coords). SENSING spans the sensor row
     * (rings painted here); STRIKE spans the strum zone below (no rings). */
    uint16_t sensing_x, sensing_y, sensing_w, sensing_h;
    uint16_t strike_x,  strike_y,  strike_w,  strike_h;
} cv_marvin_v1_config_t;

extern const cv_marvin_v1_config_t CV_MARVIN_CFG_1P;
extern const cv_marvin_v1_config_t CV_MARVIN_CFG_2P_LEFT;

void CvMarvinV1_Initialize(void);

/* Swap the active geometry. Takes effect on the next processed frame; the
 * detector resets its per-fret latch state and re-publishes config on change.
 * Safe to call from another task. */
void CvMarvinV1_SetConfig(const cv_marvin_v1_config_t *cfg);
const cv_marvin_v1_config_t *CvMarvinV1_GetConfig(void);

#endif

```

395	static void reset_detector_state(void)
396	{
397	    memset(s_hold_dist,   0, sizeof(s_hold_dist));
398	    memset(s_edge_dist,   0, sizeof(s_edge_dist));
399	    memset(s_pressed,     0, sizeof(s_pressed));
400	    memset(s_edge_active, 0, sizeof(s_edge_active));
