```text
404	/* ─── Task ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
405	
406	static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
407	{
408	    (void)param;
409	
410	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
411	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
412	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
413	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
414	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
415	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
416	    configASSERT(subscribed);
417	
418	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
419	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
420	
421	    LOG_INFO("CV: cv_marvin_v1 started\r\n");
422	
423	    publish_detector_config();
424	
425	    for (;;)
426	    {
427	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
428	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
429	
430	        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
431	        if (!Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)) { continue; }
432	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                       { continue; }
433	        if (frame.width == 0u || frame.height == 0u)    { continue; }
434	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL){ continue; }
435	
436	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_START, frame.frame_count, 0u);
437	        detect_frame(&frame, bus);
438	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_END, frame.frame_count, 0u);
439	
440	        /* Re-emit detector config at ~1 Hz so a mid-stream host attach
441	         * picks it up within a second of frames flowing. Cheap (~188 B/s
442	         * × 1 record/s). When config becomes runtime-tunable, this becomes
443	         * the heartbeat — on-change emits land via publish_detector_config
444	         * directly from the setter path. */
445	        if ((frame.frame_count % 60u) == 0u) { publish_detector_config(); }
446	
447	        const uint32_t fstride = (uint32_t)frame.width * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
448	
449	        /* STRIKE: the strum trigger zone, copied straight from the frame (no
450	         * sensors there → no rings). */
451	        PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_STRIKE,
452	                                   (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer, fstride,
453	                                   CV_STRIKE_X, CV_STRIKE_Y, CV_STRIKE_W, CV_STRIKE_H);
454	
455	        /* SENSING: copy the sensor row into scratch and (when the overlay sink
456	         * is on) paint the target rings onto the copy before shipping it. The
457	         * source frame is never written, so snapshots and the LVDS panel stay
458	         * clean. Gate the copy on the STRIP mask so it costs nothing when the
459	         * host isn't consuming strips. */
460	        if ((PerfLog_GetEnabledMask() & (1u << PERF_REC_STRIP)) != 0u)
461	        {
462	            const uint8_t *src = (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer
463	                               + (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_Y * fstride
464	                               + (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_X * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
465	            const uint32_t row_bytes = (uint32_t)CV_SENSING_W * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
466	            uint8_t *dst = s_sensing_scratch;
467	            for (uint16_t row = 0u; row < CV_SENSING_H; row++)
468	            {
469	                memcpy(dst, src, row_bytes);
470	                src += fstride;
471	                dst += row_bytes;
472	            }
473	            if ((PerfLog_GetOverlayFlags() & PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP) != 0u)
474	            {
475	                draw_overlay(s_sensing_scratch, CV_SENSING_W, CV_SENSING_H,
476	                             CV_SENSING_X, CV_SENSING_Y);
477	            }
478	            PerfLog_EmitStripPacked(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_SENSING,
479	                                    CV_SENSING_X, CV_SENSING_Y,
480	                                    CV_SENSING_W, CV_SENSING_H, s_sensing_scratch);
481	        }
482	
483	        /* REGION: host-selected sub-region (e.g. the score block), streamed one
484	         * strip per frame when the host has started the stream. No-op otherwise. */
485	        PerfLog_EmitRegionIfEnabled(frame.frame_count, (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer,
486	                                    fstride, frame.width, frame.height);
```

```text
=== screens.py ===
"""Canonical GH3 screen identifiers and the corpus filename -> id mapping.

Single source of truth aligning the prototype's screen ids with the screen names
in `firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md`. The classifier emits one of these ids
(or the sentinel UNKNOWN); the firmware `gameplay_engine` port will reuse the same
names.

Corpus files are named `<prefix>__<selection>.png` (or just `<prefix>.png` for
single-shot screens). The screen *class* is the prefix; the selection suffix is
the highlighted item, which a later slice (the highlight reader) handles. Two
prefixes are renamed here to match the nav-doc node names.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

# Sentinel for "no recognized screen" — the navigator's recovery path keys off it.
UNKNOWN = "unknown"

# Canonical screen ids, matching the gh3_navigation.md catalog. Order is the
# nominal practice-run flow, then the overlays/dialogs.
SCREEN_IDS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "main_menu",
    "training_menu",
    "tutorials_menu",
    "song_select",
    "part_select",
    "difficulty_select",
    "section_select",
    "speed_select",
    "loading",
    "in_song",
    "pause_menu",
    "quit_confirm",
    "practice_end_menu",
)

# Corpus filename prefixes whose canonical id differs from the prefix itself.
# Everything else maps by identity.
_PREFIX_RENAMES: dict[str, str] = {
    "difficulty": "difficulty_select",
    "speed": "speed_select",
}


def screen_id_for_filename(filename: str) -> str:
    """Map a corpus PNG filename to its canonical screen id.

    `main_menu__training.png` -> `main_menu`; `difficulty__hard.png` ->
    `difficulty_select`; `loading.png` -> `loading`. Raises ValueError if the
    resulting id isn't a known screen.
    """
    stem = filename.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    if stem.endswith(".png"):
        stem = stem[: -len(".png")]
    prefix = stem.split("__", 1)[0]
    screen_id = _PREFIX_RENAMES.get(prefix, prefix)
    if screen_id not in SCREEN_IDS:
        raise ValueError(f"{filename!r}: unknown screen prefix {prefix!r}")
    return screen_id
```

```text
# each frame is a scoring-block crop whose 3-digit value is in the filename (with
# `x` for a mid-roll/unreadable wheel). See metadata.streak_from_filename.
_DEFAULT_STREAK_CORPUS_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "data" / "streak"


def corpus_dir() -> Path:
    """Resolve the corpus directory (overridable via $GAMEPLAY_CORPUS_DIR)."""
    env = os.environ.get("GAMEPLAY_CORPUS_DIR")
    return Path(env) if env else _DEFAULT_CORPUS_DIR


def score_corpus_dir() -> Path:
    """Resolve the score corpus directory (overridable via $GAMEPLAY_SCORE_CORPUS_DIR)."""
    env = os.environ.get("GAMEPLAY_SCORE_CORPUS_DIR")
    return Path(env) if env else _DEFAULT_SCORE_CORPUS_DIR


def streak_corpus_dir() -> Path:
    """Resolve the streak corpus directory (overridable via $GAMEPLAY_STREAK_CORPUS_DIR)."""
    env = os.environ.get("GAMEPLAY_STREAK_CORPUS_DIR")
    return Path(env) if env else _DEFAULT_STREAK_CORPUS_DIR

class Sample:
    screen_id: str
    path: Path

def load_bgr(path: str | Path) -> np.ndarray:

    with Image.open(path) as im:
        rgb = np.asarray(im.convert("RGB"), dtype=np.uint8)
    return rgb[:, :, ::-1].copy()  # RGB -> BGR
```

```text
463	                if (st->act != ACT_WAIT)

466	                }
467	                recover = 0;
468	                confirm_fail = 0;
469	            }

471	            {
```

```text
13	 * engine reports and recovers with RED on a mismatch — a port of the offline

15	 * FretboardLink_Send, so they drive both the T1S guitar and fauxmote. See
16	 * firmware/marvin/docs/gh3_navigation.md.

18	 * Initialize once in App_StartServices, after the gameplay engine, timing pipeline,
19	 * and manual_control (it drives their setters). */
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 19:26:17Z)**_

Done. I added a **`play attach`** console command for exactly your workflow — manually set up the 2-player game, then let marvin's CV detector + actuator play it through.

**What it does** (`GameController_StartAttach` → new attach mode in `game_controller.c`):
1. Skips all menu navigation (unlike plain `play`, which drives the 1p Training→Practice path).
2. Owns the wire (manual off, timing off) and runs the existing fauxmote pre-flight (`ensure_wii_connected`).
3. Waits (up to 2 min) for a gameplay screen to appear.
4. When it sees `in_song_2p` (or `in_song`), auto-selects the matching highway config (2p → left/robot, 1p → centered).
5. Runs `play_until_done()` — the timing pipeline actuates the whole song and releases at the end (or on `play stop`).

**Console surface:**
- `play attach` — start a manually-set-up playthrough (the new 2p path)
- `play` — unchanged (auto-navigate the committed 1p selection)
- `play stop` / `play status` — unchanged
- `cvcfg 1p|2pl` — still there if you want to force the geometry directly for detector-only bring-up

**Typical 2p bench sequence:** get marvin's fauxmote into the match as P1 → start the song on the Wii → `play attach`. It'll pick up `in_song_2p`, switch to the 2p-left coords, and actuate to the end.

Two notes:
- It waits for the game to *reach a gameplay screen* — it does not press START in the GH3 menus for you (that's the manual-setup part). If you'd rather it also confirm through a 2p pre-song menu, that's a small addition once we know that screen.
- Same **lead-time caveat** as before: the 2p sense row is at y=311 like 1p; if actuation timing looks early/late on the shorter 2p highway, we adjust the 2p-left `sensing` row.

All firmware-side (needs your MPLAB build). Journals updated. Nothing committed.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 22:38:40Z)**_

Good news — it's already off in 2-player mode; no change needed.

The 1p score/multiplier/streak readers run in exactly one place, [gameplay_engine.c:139-146](firmware/marvin/default/src/game/gameplay_engine.c#L139-L146), gated on:

```c
if (screen == GP_SCREEN_in_song)   // 1p only
{
    gp_read_score(...); gp_read_multiplier(...); gp_read_streak(...);
}
else
{
    gp_streak_reset(&s_streak);
}
```

Since `in_song_2p` is a **distinct screen id**, that block never runs for a 2p frame — it falls to the `else` (streak reset). So in 2p mode `score`/`multiplier`/`streak` stay at their sentinels (-1/0/0) and the 1p score-block reader is never pointed at a 2p frame (which is what you'd want to avoid, since 2p uses the separate amp scoreboards).

The `game_controller.c` play loop is consistent: the `in_song_2p` branch I added deliberately posts no score/multiplier/streak to the dashboard, so those tiles just hold their reset (0) values during a 2p run.

So it's already disabled by construction. If you'd like it more defensive — e.g., have the dashboard show a "—"/blank for score in 2p instead of 0, or a one-line comment at the gate spelling out that `in_song_2p` intentionally skips the readers — I can add that. Otherwise nothing to do here.

```text
117	/* Iterator helpers for the release-suppression check below: is this fret
118	 * needed again by an outstanding entry whose deadline falls at or before

120	 * separate notes (clean per-note command) and holds it only across genuinely

122	static bool note_q_needs_by(uint8_t bit, uint32_t by_ms)
123	{
124	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_note_count; i++)
125	    {
126	        uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_note_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
127	        const pending_note_t *n = &s_note_q[idx];
128	        if ((n->fret_mask & bit) && (int32_t)(n->assert_at_ms - by_ms) <= 0)
129	        {
130	            return true;
131	        }
132	    }
133	    return false;
134	}

141	        const pending_strum_t *s = &s_strum_q[idx];
142	        if ((s->fret_mask & bit) && (int32_t)(s->strum_at_ms - by_ms) <= 0)
143	        {
144	            return true;
145	        }
146	    }
147	    return false;
148	}

160	/* Edge derivation:
161	 *   - presses_mask: rising edge of pressed
162	 *   - releases_mask: falling edge of pressed */
163	static void derive_edges(const detector_state_t *state,
164	                         uint8_t *presses_mask, uint8_t *releases_mask,
165	                         uint8_t *pressed_mask)
166	{
167	    uint8_t pm = 0u;
168	    uint8_t rm = 0u;
169	    uint8_t cm = 0u;
170	
171	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
172	    {
173	        bool pressed = state->fret[i].pressed != 0u;
174	        if (pressed) { cm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
175	
176	        bool was_pressed = (s_prev_pressed_mask & s_fret_bit[i]) != 0u;
177	        if (pressed && !was_pressed) { pm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
178	        if (!pressed && was_pressed) { rm |= s_fret_bit[i]; }
179	    }
180	
181	    s_prev_pressed_mask = cm;
182	    *presses_mask  = pm;
183	    *releases_mask = rm;
184	    *pressed_mask  = cm;
185	}

187	static void chord_commit(void)
188	{
189	    if (note_q_full() || strum_q_full())
190	    {
191	        s_chord_open = false;
192	        s_chord_mask = 0u;
193	        return;
194	    }
195	
196	    uint32_t assert_at = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS - TP_FRET_EARLY_MS;
197	    uint32_t strum_at  = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
198	
199	    if (!strum_q_empty())
200	    {
201	        uint8_t  last_idx = (uint8_t)((s_strum_tail + TP_FIFO_CAP - 1u) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
202	        uint32_t earliest = s_strum_q[last_idx].strum_at_ms + TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS;
203	        if ((int32_t)(assert_at - earliest) < 0)
204	        {
205	            assert_at = earliest;
206	            strum_at  = assert_at + TP_FRET_EARLY_MS;
207	        }
208	    }
209	
210	    pending_note_t  n = { .assert_at_ms = assert_at, .fret_mask = s_chord_mask };
211	    pending_strum_t s = { .strum_at_ms  = strum_at,  .fret_mask = s_chord_mask };
212	    note_q_push(n);
213	    strum_q_push(s);
214	
215	    s_chord_open = false;
216	    s_chord_mask = 0u;
217	}
218	
219	static void process_notes(void)
220	{
221	    while (!note_q_empty())
222	    {
223	        const pending_note_t *n = &s_note_q[s_note_head];
224	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - n->assert_at_ms) < 0) { break; }
225	
226	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
227	        {
228	            uint8_t bit = s_fret_bit[i];
229	            bool need = (n->fret_mask & bit) != 0u;
230	            bool have = (s_frets_active & bit) != 0u;
231	            if (need && !have)      { s_frets_active |= bit; }
232	            else if (!need && have) { s_frets_active &= (uint8_t)~bit; }
233	        }
234	        note_q_pop();
235	    }
236	}
237	
238	static void process_strums(void)
239	{
240	    while (!strum_q_empty())
241	    {
242	        const pending_strum_t *s = &s_strum_q[s_strum_head];
243	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - s->strum_at_ms) < 0) { break; }
244	
245	        s_strum_active        = true;
246	        s_strum_direction     = !s_strum_direction;
247	        s_strum_release_at_ms = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_PULSE_MS;
248	
249	        strum_q_pop();
250	    }
251	}
252	
253	static void process_releases(uint8_t live_pressed_mask)
254	{
255	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
256	    {
257	        uint8_t bit = s_fret_bit[i];
258	        if ((s_release_pending_mask & bit) == 0u) { continue; }
259	        if ((int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_release_at_ms[i]) < 0) { continue; }
260	        if (live_pressed_mask & bit) { continue; }
261	        /* Hold only if re-needed at/before this release (back-to-back); a need
262	         * further out releases now for a clean per-note command. */
263	        if (note_q_needs_by(bit, s_release_at_ms[i]) ||
264	            strum_q_needs_by(bit, s_release_at_ms[i])) { continue; }
265	
266	        s_frets_active        &= (uint8_t)~bit;
267	        s_release_pending_mask &= (uint8_t)~bit;
268	    }
269	}
270	
271	static void advance(uint8_t live_pressed_mask)
272	{
273	    if (s_chord_open && (int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_chord_start_ms) >= (int32_t)TP_CHORD_WINDOW_MS)
274	    {
275	        chord_commit();
276	    }
277	
278	    if (s_strum_active && (int32_t)(s_now_ms - s_strum_release_at_ms) >= 0)
279	    {
280	        s_strum_active = false;
281	    }
282	
283	    process_notes();
284	    process_strums();
285	    process_releases(live_pressed_mask);
286	
287	    uint8_t mask = s_frets_active;
288	    if (s_strum_active)
289	    {
290	        mask |= s_strum_direction ? TIMING_BIT_STRUM_UP : TIMING_BIT_STRUM_DOWN;
291	    }
292	    publish_mask(mask);
293	}

295	/* Build the per-frame TIMING snapshot from current pipeline state. Called
296	 * once per process_frame after advance() has settled all queues and the
297	 * publish_mask. Deadlines for empty queues are zeroed; host inspects the
298	 * count fields before treating *_at_ms as meaningful. */
299	static void fill_timing_snapshot(perf_timing_snapshot_t *snap)
300	{
301	    memset(snap, 0, sizeof(*snap));
302	    snap->now_ms = s_now_ms;
303	
304	    snap->chord_open   = s_chord_open ? 1u : 0u;
305	    snap->chord_mask   = s_chord_open ? s_chord_mask : 0u;
306	    snap->chord_age_ms = s_chord_open
307	                       ? (uint16_t)(s_now_ms - s_chord_start_ms)
308	                       : 0u;
309	
310	    snap->note_q_count = s_note_count;
311	    if (s_note_count > 0u)
312	    {
313	        const pending_note_t *head = &s_note_q[s_note_head];
314	        snap->note_head_mask  = head->fret_mask;
315	        snap->note_head_at_ms = head->assert_at_ms;
316	        uint8_t tail_union = 0u;
317	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < s_note_count; i++)
318	        {
319	            uint8_t idx = (uint8_t)((s_note_head + i) % TP_FIFO_CAP);
320	            tail_union |= s_note_q[idx].fret_mask;
321	        }
322	        snap->note_tail_mask = tail_union;
323	    }
324	
325	    snap->strum_q_count = s_strum_count;
326	    if (s_strum_count > 0u)
327	    {
328	        const pending_strum_t *head = &s_strum_q[s_strum_head];
329	        snap->strum_head_mask  = head->fret_mask;
330	        snap->strum_head_at_ms = head->strum_at_ms;
331	    }
332	    /* strum_dir toggles each fired strum; report the *next* direction
333	     * (what would fire if the front of strum_q reaches its deadline now). */
334	    snap->strum_dir_next = s_strum_direction ? 2u /*up*/ : 1u /*down*/;
335	
336	    snap->frets_active         = s_frets_active;
337	    snap->strum_active         = s_strum_active ? 1u : 0u;
338	    snap->release_pending_mask = s_release_pending_mask;
339	    snap->publish_mask         = s_output_mask;
340	    snap->strum_release_at_ms  = s_strum_active ? s_strum_release_at_ms : 0u;
341	
342	    if (s_release_pending_mask != 0u)
343	    {
344	        uint32_t min_at = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
345	        for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
346	        {
347	            if ((s_release_pending_mask & s_fret_bit[i]) == 0u) { continue; }
348	            if (s_release_at_ms[i] < min_at) { min_at = s_release_at_ms[i]; }
349	        }
350	        snap->release_min_at_ms = (min_at == 0xFFFFFFFFu) ? 0u : min_at;
351	    }
352	}

354	static void process_frame(const detector_state_t *state)
355	{
356	    /* Detector frame timestamps drive the clock so this is replay-
357	     * deterministic. timestamp_us is monotonic per spec §4.2.3. */
358	    s_now_ms = (uint32_t)(state->timestamp_us / 1000ull);
359	    s_last_frame_us = state->timestamp_us;
360	
361	    uint8_t presses, releases, pressed_mask;
362	    derive_edges(state, &presses, &releases, &pressed_mask);
363	
364	    if (presses)
365	    {
366	        if (!s_chord_open)
367	        {
368	            s_chord_open     = true;
369	            s_chord_start_ms = s_now_ms;
370	            s_chord_mask     = 0u;
371	        }
372	        s_chord_mask |= presses;
373	    }
374	
375	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < FRET_COUNT; i++)
376	    {
377	        if (releases & s_fret_bit[i])
378	        {
379	            s_release_at_ms[i]      = s_now_ms + TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS;
380	            s_release_pending_mask |= s_fret_bit[i];
381	        }
382	    }
383	
384	    advance(pressed_mask);
385	
386	    PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_TP_TICK, state->frame_epoch,
387	                      (uint32_t)s_output_mask);
388	
389	    perf_timing_snapshot_t snap;
390	    fill_timing_snapshot(&snap);
391	    PerfLog_EmitTiming(state->frame_epoch, &snap);
392	}
393	
394	static void timing_pipeline_task(void *param)
395	{
396	    (void)param;
397	
398	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
399	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
400	
401	    LOG_INFO("TIMING: pipeline started\r\n");
402	
403	    for (;;)
404	    {
405	        detector_state_t state;
406	        if (xQueueReceive(bus, &state, pdMS_TO_TICKS(TP_TICK_MS)) == pdTRUE)
407	        {
408	            if ((detector_id_t)state.detector_id != Detector_GetActive())
409	            {
410	                continue;
411	            }
412	            process_frame(&state);
413	        }
414	        else
415	        {
416	            /* No new frame; advance the clock so deadlines that fell
417	             * between frames (strum pulses, release timers) still fire. */
418	            s_now_ms += TP_TICK_MS;
419	            advance(s_prev_pressed_mask);
420	        }
421	    }
422	}
423	
424	void TimingPipeline_Initialize(void)
425	{
426	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(timing_pipeline_task,
427	                                       "Timing",
428	                                       TP_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
429	                                       NULL,
430	                                       TP_TASK_PRIORITY,
431	                                       s_task_stack,
432	                                       &s_task_tcb);
433	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_TIMING, h);
434	}
435	
436	void TimingPipeline_SetEnabled(bool enabled)
437	{
438	    if (enabled == s_pipeline_enabled)
439	    {
440	        return;
441	    }
442	    s_pipeline_enabled = enabled;
443	    if (!enabled)
444	    {
445	        /* Release the wire on disable so no frets stay held (the actuator's own
446	         * heartbeat would otherwise keep re-sending the last mask). */
447	        FretboardLink_Send(0u, (uint8_t)PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_TIMING);
448	    }
449	}
450	
451	bool TimingPipeline_IsEnabled(void)
452	{
453	    return s_pipeline_enabled;
454	}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 22:47:45Z)**_

That confirms it. Here's what I found — and the short answer is **no, nothing we changed touches this path.**

## What our changes touched (and didn't)
Diff vs HEAD is `cv_marvin_v1.{c,h}`, `console.c`, `game_controller.{c,h}`, `gameplay_metadata.h`. **None** touch the timing pipeline, `fretboard_link.c`, or the fauxmote transport. (`timing_pipeline.c` shows in `git status` but has an empty diff — just an IDE mtime touch; it's byte-identical to HEAD.)

## Why the dashboard and the physical press disagree — by design, not a regression
The dashboard fret display is **not a measurement of the physical press**. It's mirrored from the *same* `FretboardLink_Send()` call that feeds fauxmote, microseconds apart:

- [fretboard_link.c:328](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L328) → `Fauxmote_SendGuitarMask(v)`
- [fretboard_link.c:333](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L333) → `DashboardFeed_PostFret(v)`

So the dashboard shows **command-issue time** = detection + timing-pipeline delay. The physical Wii press is always *later* than that, by the fauxmote tail: `Fauxmote_SendGuitar` just latches the latest mask and pokes a TX task ([fauxmote_link.c:246](firmware/marvin/default/src/net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.c#L246)) → UART to the ESP32 → Bluetooth HID → the Wii's own input polling. That tail is inherently variable and the dashboard can't reveal it. "Dashboard shows the delay, the press is inconsistently later" is the expected relationship — it would look the same on the committed firmware.

## The most likely 2p-specific factor
In a **2-player match the Wii is servicing two Bluetooth controllers**; marvin's emulated Wiimote can get less frequent / jitterier polling than when it's the only controller. That shows up exactly as *inconsistent extra delay, only in 2p*. The clean A/B is the **1p test you haven't run yet** — same firmware, if 1p is tight and 2p is jittery, it's BT/2p contention downstream of our code, not the code.

## Two things worth checking on your side
1. **Your 150 ms may not be in the build.** On disk `TP_STRUM_DELAY_MS = 250u` ([timing_pipeline.c:21](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/timing_pipeline.c#L21)) and there's no diff — so a "150" edit isn't saved to the file being compiled (unsaved buffer or reverted). Confirm the flashed build actually has 150. Also note frets assert at `delay − 50 ms` (`TP_FRET_EARLY_MS`) and the strum at the full delay, so the fret dashboard leads the strum by 50 ms by design.
2. **There's already an ACK path to measure the fauxmote tail.** `PerfLog_EmitActuator` logs `s_last_ack_result` + `s_last_ack_ts_counter` ([fretboard_link.c:339](firmware/marvin/default/src/actuator/fretboard_link.c#L339)) — the marvin-perf actuator record can quantify send→ack latency and its jitter, which would directly confirm whether the variable delay is in the fauxmote/BT path.

Want me to pull the actuator ACK timing out of a perf capture (1p vs 2p) to quantify the tail, or add a targeted log of send→ack latency in `fretboard_link.c` so you can watch it live?

```text
# fauxmote — Working Journal

Running log of planning, decisions, open questions, and work-in-progress for fauxmote. Newest entries at the top. For *what fauxmote is* (purpose, hardware, interfaces, milestones), read [`../SPEC.md`](../SPEC.md) — this journal does not duplicate it.

---

## Current focus

**Phase 1 DONE — the Wii pairs with fauxmote and opens both HID channels.** Custom
Wiimote SDP record (built via Bluedroid's internal `SDP_*` API in `wiimote_sdp.c`,
with SDP buffers raised to 512/1024) + raw `esp_bt_l2cap` servers on PSM 0x11/0x13.
On a red-SYNC press the Wii: accepts our SDP, completes legacy PIN pairing
(`auth OK`), and opens both HID L2CAP channels (control CID 0x40 / interrupt CID 0x41,
both `mtu 640`), then starts sending us data. Wii BD_ADDR `00:17:ab:07:2c:21`.

**Phase 2 DONE — the Wii fully initializes fauxmote as an assigned Wiimote.**
`wiimote.c` answers the Wii's output reports (`0x17` read→`0x21`, `0x15`→`0x20`
status, `0x16` write→`0x22` ack, `0x11` LEDs, `0x12` reporting mode, `0x13`/`0x1a`
IR-enable acks) and streams `0x30` core-button reports (~15 ms) for keep-alive.
On hardware: clean full handshake, the Wii assigns a player slot (`0x11`), and the
GPIO13 status LED (no real player LEDs on a Feather) goes **solid = assigned**
(heartbeat=waiting, fast-blink=connected). IR is acked but not implemented (only
needed for the pointer, not guitar gameplay).

**Core-Wiimote + test-CLI workstream (before guitar).**

- **Step A DONE — manual test CLI + connection management.** `esp_console` REPL
  (`console_cli.c`): `pair`/`stop`/`reconnect`/`unlink`/`status`/`btn`/`tap` — all
  thin pass-throughs over the module API (logic lives in `wiimote.c`/`bt_hid_device.c`,
  so Marvin can drive the same API later). Boots idle; `pair` arms the HID listeners
  for that sync window and `stop` tears them down; servers are **armed per pairing
  window**, not at boot or auto-re-armed (re-arming leaked L2CAP slots, since
  `reconnect` uses client connects). Honors the Wii's requested reporting mode
  (`0x12` → builds that report ID; buttons populated, accel/IR/ext zeroed). Disconnect
  fully resets state (`Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected`) and readers exit by L2CAP handle
  (robust to fd reuse). Bond persists in NVS (recalled at boot via
  `esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_list`); `unlink` removes it. Status LED on GPIO13:
  blip/~3 s = idle, fast blink = pairing/connecting, N flashes = assigned player N.
- **Step B DONE — IR pointer.** Pointer `(x,y)` is a state variable in `wiimote.c`
  (`Wiimote_SetPointer`/`ClearPointer`), CLI `point x y` / `point off`. `build_ir_extended`
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 22:54:51Z)**_

Right — this is fauxmote/Wii-slot territory, and it clears our marvin work (detector geometry, `in_song_2p`, attach mode). Here's what the code says about *how* a second Wiimote messes with fauxmote:

## Mechanism
- Fauxmote has **no notion of its player identity of its own** — the slot is whatever the **Wii** tells it via output report `0x11` (player LEDs). `s_leds` is set purely from that ([wiimote.c:200-201](firmware/fauxmote/main/wiimote.c#L200-L201)); `Wiimote_IsAssigned()` = `s_leds != 0` and the player number is derived from which LED bit is lit ([wiimote.c:423](firmware/fauxmote/main/wiimote.c#L423)).
- When you sync a second Wiimote, the Wii **re-runs slot assignment and re-sends `0x11`** to the existing controllers. So fauxmote's slot can change out from under it (e.g. P1→P2, or momentarily unassigned). In GH3 2p the slot picks the **highway**, so if fauxmote gets bumped, marvin is detecting the left highway but actuating the wrong player — exactly "control messed up," and connect-order-dependent.
- Secondary effect: two HID devices now share the ESP32↔Wii Bluetooth link, so fauxmote's ~15 ms keep-alive/button reports get jittered/delayed — which matches the *inconsistent extra press delay* you saw earlier.
- Neither side has multi-controller handling: the fauxmote SPEC has no two-controller model, and marvin's `fauxmote_link` just **caches** `STATUS` (flags/`player_slot`/`report_mode`) without reacting ([fauxmote_link.c:289-307](firmware/marvin/default/src/net/fauxmote/fauxmote_link.c#L289-L307)) — the only reconnect logic is `ensure_wii_connected()` in the play preflight, not during play.

## Fastest diagnostic
On the fauxmote console, run `status` (it reports `flags / player_slot / report_mode`) **before and after** you connect the second Wiimote — and ideally again once the 2p game starts:
- If `player_slot` changes (or `ASSIGNED` drops), it's slot reassignment → the robot is on the wrong highway / lost its slot.
- If slot holds but inputs still lag, it's BT-airtime contention on the shared link.

That one check tells us which of the two it is. Want me to dig into the fauxmote firmware's connect/slot handling and propose a fix (e.g. pinning/holding fauxmote's slot, or making marvin track fauxmote's actual `player_slot` and pick the matching highway), or are you set to run the `status` check first?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 23:04:15Z)**_

That asymmetry is the tell — and it points hard at **Bluetooth role / scatternet**, not simple airtime sharing.

## The domain knowledge you asked for
The Wii is the Bluetooth **master** of one piconet; every Wiimote is a **slave** in that *same* piconet, all sharing the Wii's clock. The master round-robin-polls its slaves, and HID reports are tiny (1–2 of the 625 µs slots each), so 4 slaves still get serviced within a couple ms — no perceptible lag. That only holds because **all four are slaves in one piconet.**

The failure mode that produces *lag on one link only*: if a device is the **master of its own link to the Wii** (Wii = slave to it), while the Wii is simultaneously master of the real Wiimote's piconet, the Wii becomes a **scatternet** node — two piconets, two clocks, one radio. It has to time-division-hop between them, and the *foreign* piconet (fauxmote's) gets serviced only intermittently → noticeable, irregular lag **on the fauxmote link specifically**, while the Wii's own piconet (the real Wiimote) stays crisp. That matches your data exactly:
- Slot stable ✔ (role is independent of player slot)
- Only fauxmote lags, real Wiimote fine ✔
- Single fauxmote is fine ✔ (no second piconet to hop to)
- Real Wii runs 4 Wiimotes fine ✔ (all slaves, one piconet)

## Why fauxmote would be master
A real Wiimote **never initiates** — the Wii always pages it, so the Wii is master. Fauxmote's `reconnect` does the opposite: `Fauxmote_Reconnect()` / the reconnect path call `esp_bt_l2cap_connect(...)` — **device-initiated** ([bt_hid_device.c:178](firmware/fauxmote/main/bt_hid_device.c#L178), [:274](firmware/fauxmote/main/bt_hid_device.c#L274)). The initiator is master by default, and there's **no role-switch call anywhere** in the fauxmote BT code. So any connection established via `reconnect` leaves **fauxmote as master / Wii as slave** → scatternet as soon as a real Wiimote joins.

A fresh **red-SYNC pair** is the opposite: the Wii pages fauxmote → Wii is master → no scatternet. (The journal even notes the workaround "restart fauxmote after the game has started — a fresh boot reconnects cleanly" — a fresh boot re-pairs with the Wii as master.)

## The cheap confirming test
Get fauxmote connected via a **fresh red-SYNC pairing** (not `reconnect`), *then* sync the second Wiimote and check the fauxmote lag on the wiimotes screen.
- **Lag gone** → confirmed role/scatternet. Fix: make fauxmote always end up **slave** — either request a role switch to slave right after a device-initiated reconnect, or prefer Wii-paged connection and never rely on `reconnect` for gameplay.
- **Lag still there** → it's genuinely airtime/link-parameter (then we look at the active-vs-sniff decision — fauxmote deliberately keeps the link active/sniff-off per the 2026-06-13 idle-disconnect fix, whereas real Wiimotes let the Wii sniff-schedule them).

Want me to dig into the ESP32 role-switch path (whether Bluedroid will let us force slave after connect, e.g. an HCI role-switch / "allow role switch" on the connect) so we have the fix ready if the fresh-pair test confirms it?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 23:11:26Z)**_

Good push — no, I shouldn't have stated that as fact. Let me correct it.

**Who pages is only the *initial* master; it can flip.** In classic Bluetooth the pager (the Wii, on a red-SYNC) starts as master, but during/after connection setup **either side can trigger a role switch**, gated by each side's link-policy "allow role switch" bit. Many Bluedroid/ESP32 configurations have the accepting device **request master** on connect — so fauxmote can end up master *even on a fresh Wii-paged pairing*. Your fresh-pair-still-lags result is actually consistent with that: it doesn't rule out the scatternet theory, it just means the connection direction didn't determine the final role.

So the honest state is: I was inferring role from who paged, which is wrong. We need to **read the actual ACL role** rather than assume it. Let me check what fauxmote can query.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 23:12:11Z)**_

No — and I was wrong to state it as fact. The role isn't decided by who paged: **either side can role-switch during/after connection**, gated by the link-policy "allow role switch" bit, and ESP32/Bluedroid commonly has the accepting device **request master**. So fauxmote can be master even on a fresh Wii-paged pair — which is exactly consistent with your "fresh pair still lags." Connection direction tells us nothing definitive here.

The only way to know is to **read the actual ACL role**, and fauxmote can do that cheaply — it already reaches into Bluedroid internals for the SDP record ([wiimote_sdp.c](firmware/fauxmote/main/wiimote_sdp.c) includes `stack/sdp_api.h`), so `stack/btm_api.h`'s `BTM_GetRole(bda, &role)` is reachable the same way. The public `esp_gap_bt` API doesn't expose role, which is why it hasn't been visible.

(Note: the `CONFIG_BTDM_CTRL_PCM_ROLE_MASTER` in sdkconfig is the **PCM/SCO audio** interface, not the ACL role — red herring.)

Concrete next step I'd suggest: add a one-line role log right after both HID L2CAP channels open (in `bt_hid_device.c`), printing `BTM_GetRole()` for the Wii's BD_ADDR. That definitively splits the diagnosis:
- **role == master** → scatternet confirmed (Wii is slave to fauxmote, hops piconets, starves the fauxmote link when the real Wiimote's piconet also needs the radio). Fix: `BTM_SwitchRole(wii_bda, SLAVE, cb)` after connect (+ allow role switch in link policy) so fauxmote behaves like a real Wiimote.
- **role == slave** → scatternet theory is dead; we pivot to link parameters (the active-vs-sniff choice, `Tpoll`, or an ESP32-controller scheduling limit with 2 ACLs — note `MAX_ACL_CONN=2`).

Want me to write that role-logging instrumentation (and stage the `BTM_SwitchRole`-to-slave fix behind it, so if it prints master you can flip it in the same build)? I'll confirm the exact internal symbol/signature against your installed ESP-IDF before finalizing.

```text
94	static void hid_reader_task(void *arg)

97	    while (!l->stop) {

104	        } else if (n < 0) {
105	            break;                          /* genuine close of our fd */
106	        } else {
107	            vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(10));  /* non-blocking VFS: 0 = no data yet */
108	        }
109	    }
110	    l->in_use = false;
111	    vTaskDelete(NULL);

129	
130	static void hid_link_stop(uint32_t handle)
131	{
132	    for (int i = 0; i < HID_LINK_MAX; i++) {
133	        if (s_links[i].in_use && s_links[i].handle == handle) {
134	            s_links[i].stop = true;
135	            return;
136	        }
137	    }
138	}
139	
140	/* Bluedroid consumes the listening server slot when a connection opens, so the
141	 * HID PSMs are armed per pairing window (EnterPairing) and torn down in StopPairing
142	 * — re-arming on every disconnect leaks slots when reconnect uses client connects. */
143	static void start_hid_servers(void)
144	{
145	    esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_CONTROL);
146	    esp_bt_l2cap_start_srv(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_INTERRUPT);
147	}
148	
149	static void l2cap_cb(esp_bt_l2cap_cb_event_t event, esp_bt_l2cap_cb_param_t *param)
150	{
151	    switch (event) {
152	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_INIT_EVT:
153	        /* The L2CAP data path is fd-based; the VFS must be registered before a
154	         * server can allocate a slot/fd. */
155	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP init status=%d; registering VFS", param->init.status);
156	        esp_bt_l2cap_vfs_register();
157	        break;
158	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_VFS_REGISTER_EVT:
159	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP VFS registered status=%d", param->vfs_register.status);
160	        break;
161	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_START_EVT:
162	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "L2CAP server up status=%d handle=%u",
163	                 param->start.status, (unsigned)param->start.handle);
164	        break;
165	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_OPEN_EVT:
166	        log_bda("L2CAP OPEN from", param->open.rem_bda);
167	        ESP_LOGI(TAG, "  status=%d handle=%u fd=%d mtu=%d",
168	                 param->open.status, (unsigned)param->open.handle,
169	                 param->open.fd, (int)param->open.tx_mtu);
170	        hid_link_start(param->open.fd, param->open.handle);
171	        /* Connected — stop being discoverable (stay connectable for reconnects),
172	         * matching a real Wiimote which doesn't advertise once connected. */
173	        esp_bt_gap_set_scan_mode(ESP_BT_CONNECTABLE, ESP_BT_NON_DISCOVERABLE);
174	        s_discoverable = false;
175	        if (s_reconnecting) {
176	            /* control channel re-opened — now open the interrupt channel. */
177	            s_reconnecting = false;
178	            esp_bt_l2cap_connect(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_INTERRUPT, s_wii_bda);
179	        }
180	        break;
181	    case ESP_BT_L2CAP_CLOSE_EVT:
182	        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "L2CAP CLOSE handle=%u async=%d",
183	                 (unsigned)param->close.handle, param->close.async);
184	        /* Signal this channel's reader to exit (by handle, robust to fd reuse). */
185	        hid_link_stop(param->close.handle);
186	        /* Stop streaming + reset controller state immediately so the sender
187	         * doesn't write into the dying channel and the LED returns to idle.
188	         * Recovery is via the `reconnect` command — no automatic reconnect. */
189	        Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected();
190	        break;
191	    default:
192	        ESP_LOGD(TAG, "l2cap event %d", event);
193	        break;
194	    }
195	}
196	
197	void Fauxmote_BtStart(void)
198	{
199	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_mem_release(ESP_BT_MODE_BLE));
200	    esp_bt_controller_config_t cfg = BT_CONTROLLER_INIT_CONFIG_DEFAULT();
201	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_init(&cfg));
202	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_controller_enable(ESP_BT_MODE_CLASSIC_BT));
203	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bluedroid_init());
204	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bluedroid_enable());
205	
206	    const uint8_t *bda = esp_bt_dev_get_address();
207	    if (bda) {
208	        /* Our BD_ADDR — also the 1+2 temporary-pairing PIN (this, reversed). */
209	        log_bda("BD_ADDR", bda);
210	    }
211	
212	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_gap_register_callback(gap_cb));
213	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_gap_set_device_name(FAUXMOTE_BT_NAME));
214	
215	    /* Legacy PIN pairing (SSP disabled in sdkconfig): we answer each PIN request. */
216	    esp_bt_gap_set_pin(ESP_BT_PIN_TYPE_VARIABLE, 0, NULL);
217	
218	    /* Serve the exact Wiimote SDP record, then listen for the Wii's HID L2CAP
219	     * connections on PSM 0x11 (control) / 0x13 (interrupt). */
220	    if (!WiimoteSdp_Register()) {
221	        ESP_LOGE(TAG, "Wiimote SDP registration failed");
222	    }
223	    Wiimote_Start();
224	
225	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_l2cap_register_callback(l2cap_cb));
226	    ESP_ERROR_CHECK(esp_bt_l2cap_init());
227	
228	    /* The stack persists the bond (link key) in NVS and reloads it at boot — recall
229	     * the bonded Wii's address so `reconnect` works after a power cycle. */
230	    int bonded = esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_num();
231	    if (bonded > 0) {
232	        esp_bd_addr_t devs[8];
233	        int n = bonded > 8 ? 8 : bonded;
234	        if (esp_bt_gap_get_bond_device_list(&n, devs) == ESP_OK && n > 0) {
235	            memcpy(s_wii_bda, devs[0], sizeof(s_wii_bda));
236	            s_have_wii = true;
237	            log_bda("recalled bonded Wii", s_wii_bda);
238	        }
239	    }
240	
241	    /* Stay idle (not discoverable/connectable) until the operator runs `pair`. */
242	    esp_bt_gap_set_scan_mode(ESP_BT_NON_CONNECTABLE, ESP_BT_NON_DISCOVERABLE);
243	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "fauxmote up (idle). Use the `pair` console command to sync with a Wii.");
244	}
245	
246	void Fauxmote_EnterPairing(void)
247	{
248	    if (s_discoverable || Wiimote_IsConnected()) {
249	        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "pairing: already discoverable/connected");
250	        return;
251	    }
252	    start_hid_servers();          /* arm the HID listeners for this sync window */
253	    set_wiimote_discoverable();
254	    s_discoverable = true;
255	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "pairing mode ON — limited-discoverable as a Wiimote (sync the Wii now)");
256	}
257	
258	void Fauxmote_StopPairing(void)
259	{
260	    esp_bt_gap_set_scan_mode(ESP_BT_NON_CONNECTABLE, ESP_BT_NON_DISCOVERABLE);
261	    esp_bt_l2cap_stop_all_srv();  /* tear down any armed (unconsumed) HID listeners */
262	    s_discoverable = false;
263	    ESP_LOGI(TAG, "pairing mode OFF (idle)");
264	}
265	
266	void Fauxmote_Reconnect(void)
267	{
268	    if (!s_have_wii) {
269	        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "reconnect: no bonded Wii yet — run `pair` first");
270	        return;
271	    }
272	    log_bda("reconnect: connecting to", s_wii_bda);
273	    s_reconnecting = true;
274	    esp_bt_l2cap_connect(ESP_BT_L2CAP_SEC_NONE, PSM_HID_CONTROL, s_wii_bda);
275	}
276	
277	void Fauxmote_Unlink(void)
278	{
279	    if (!s_have_wii) {
280	        ESP_LOGW(TAG, "unlink: no bonded Wii");
281	        return;
282	    }
283	    log_bda("unlink: removing bond", s_wii_bda);
284	    esp_bt_gap_remove_bond_device(s_wii_bda);   /* erases the link key from NVS */
285	    s_have_wii = false;
286	    memset(s_wii_bda, 0, sizeof(s_wii_bda));
287	}
288	
289	bool Fauxmote_IsDiscoverable(void) { return s_discoverable; }
290	
291	const uint8_t *Fauxmote_WiiAddr(void) { return s_have_wii ? s_wii_bda : NULL; }
```

```text
tBTM_STATUS BTM_GetRole (BD_ADDR remote_bd_addr, UINT8 *p_role)
{
    tACL_CONN   *p;
    BTM_TRACE_DEBUG ("BTM_GetRole\n");
    if ((p = btm_bda_to_acl(remote_bd_addr, BT_TRANSPORT_BR_EDR)) == NULL) {
        *p_role = BTM_ROLE_UNDEFINED;
        return (BTM_UNKNOWN_ADDR);
    }

    /* Get the current role */
    *p_role = p->link_role;
    return (BTM_SUCCESS);
}

#if (CLASSIC_BT_INCLUDED == TRUE)
/*******************************************************************************
**
** Function         BTM_SwitchRole
**
** Description      This function is called to switch role between master and
**                  slave.  If role is already set it will do nothing.  If the
**                  command was initiated, the callback function is called upon
**                  completion.
**
** Returns          BTM_SUCCESS if already in specified role.
**                  BTM_CMD_STARTED if command issued to controller.
**                  BTM_NO_RESOURCES if couldn't allocate memory to issue command
**                  BTM_UNKNOWN_ADDR if no active link with bd addr specified
**                  BTM_MODE_UNSUPPORTED if local device does not support role switching
**                  BTM_BUSY if the previous command is not completed
**
*******************************************************************************/
tBTM_STATUS BTM_SwitchRole (BD_ADDR remote_bd_addr, UINT8 new_role, tBTM_CMPL_CB *p_cb)
{
    tACL_CONN   *p;
    tBTM_SEC_DEV_REC  *p_dev_rec = NULL;
#if BTM_SCO_INCLUDED == TRUE
    BOOLEAN    is_sco_active;
#endif
    tBTM_STATUS  status;
    tBTM_PM_MODE pwr_mode;
    tBTM_PM_PWR_MD settings;
#if (BT_USE_TRACES == TRUE)
    BD_ADDR_PTR  p_bda;
#endif
    BTM_TRACE_API ("BTM_SwitchRole BDA: %02x-%02x-%02x-%02x-%02x-%02x\n",
                   remote_bd_addr[0], remote_bd_addr[1], remote_bd_addr[2],
                   remote_bd_addr[3], remote_bd_addr[4], remote_bd_addr[5]);

    /* Make sure the local device supports switching */
    if (!controller_get_interface()->supports_master_slave_role_switch()) {
        return (BTM_MODE_UNSUPPORTED);
    }

    if (btm_cb.devcb.p_switch_role_cb && p_cb) {
#if (BT_USE_TRACES == TRUE)
        p_bda = btm_cb.devcb.switch_role_ref_data.remote_bd_addr;
        BTM_TRACE_DEBUG ("Role switch on other device is in progress 0x%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x\n",
                         p_bda[0], p_bda[1], p_bda[2],
                         p_bda[3], p_bda[4], p_bda[5]);
#endif
        return (BTM_BUSY);
    }

    if ((p = btm_bda_to_acl(remote_bd_addr, BT_TRANSPORT_BR_EDR)) == NULL) {
        return (BTM_UNKNOWN_ADDR);
    }

    /* Finished if already in desired role */
    if (p->link_role == new_role) {
        return (BTM_SUCCESS);
    }

#if BTM_SCO_INCLUDED == TRUE
    /* Check if there is any SCO Active on this BD Address */
    is_sco_active = btm_is_sco_active_by_bdaddr(remote_bd_addr);

    if (is_sco_active == TRUE) {
        return (BTM_NO_RESOURCES);
    }
#endif

    /* Ignore role switch request if the previous request was not completed */
    if (p->switch_role_state != BTM_ACL_SWKEY_STATE_IDLE) {
        BTM_TRACE_DEBUG ("BTM_SwitchRole busy: %d\n",
                         p->switch_role_state);
        return (BTM_BUSY);
    }

    if ((status = BTM_ReadPowerMode(p->remote_addr, &pwr_mode)) != BTM_SUCCESS) {
        return (status);
    }

    /* Wake up the link if in sniff or park before attempting switch */
    if (pwr_mode == BTM_PM_MD_PARK || pwr_mode == BTM_PM_MD_SNIFF) {
        memset( (void *)&settings, 0, sizeof(settings));
        settings.mode = BTM_PM_MD_ACTIVE;
        status = BTM_SetPowerMode (BTM_PM_SET_ONLY_ID, p->remote_addr, &settings);
```

```h
#ifndef BT_ROLE_H
#define BT_ROLE_H

#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

/* Classic-BT ACL role helpers for the link to the Wii.
 *
 * A real Wiimote is always the Bluetooth *slave* (the Wii is master of the
 * piconet and schedules all its Wiimotes). If fauxmote ends up master, the Wii
 * becomes a scatternet node once a second (real) Wiimote joins — its radio must
 * hop between piconets, which starves fauxmote's link and adds noticeable input
 * lag. These helpers read / correct the role.
 *
 * Isolated in its own translation unit because they call Bluedroid's internal
 * BTM_* API (stack/btm_api.h), which clashes with the public esp_* Bluetooth
 * headers if both are included in one file (same pattern as wiimote_sdp.c). */

/* ACL role for the link to `bda`: 0 = master, 1 = slave, 0xFF = unknown/no link. */
uint8_t BtRole_Get(const uint8_t *bda);

/* Request an ACL role switch (to_slave = become slave, like a real Wiimote).
 * Returns true if already in the target role or the switch was started; the
 * outcome is logged on completion. */
bool BtRole_Switch(const uint8_t *bda, bool to_slave);

#endif /* BT_ROLE_H */

```

```c
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdbool.h>

#include "esp_log.h"

#include "stack/bt_types.h"
#include "stack/btm_api.h"

#include "bt_role.h"

static const char *TAG = "fauxmote.role";

static const char *role_name(uint8_t r)
{
    switch (r) {
    case BTM_ROLE_MASTER: return "MASTER";
    case BTM_ROLE_SLAVE:  return "SLAVE";
    default:              return "UNKNOWN";
    }
}

static void role_switch_cmpl(void *p)
{
    const tBTM_ROLE_SWITCH_CMPL *r = (const tBTM_ROLE_SWITCH_CMPL *)p;
    if (r == NULL) { return; }
    ESP_LOGW(TAG, "role switch complete: now %s (hci_status=0x%02x)",
             role_name(r->role), r->hci_status);
}

uint8_t BtRole_Get(const uint8_t *bda)
{
    UINT8 role = BTM_ROLE_UNDEFINED;
    if (BTM_GetRole((UINT8 *)bda, &role) != BTM_SUCCESS) {
        return 0xFFu;
    }
    return (uint8_t)role;
}

bool BtRole_Switch(const uint8_t *bda, bool to_slave)
{
    UINT8 want = to_slave ? BTM_ROLE_SLAVE : BTM_ROLE_MASTER;
    tBTM_STATUS st = BTM_SwitchRole((UINT8 *)bda, want, role_switch_cmpl);
    ESP_LOGW(TAG, "role switch to %s: st=%d", role_name(want), (int)st);
    /* BTM_SUCCESS = already in role; BTM_CMD_STARTED = switch issued to controller. */
    return (st == BTM_SUCCESS || st == BTM_CMD_STARTED);
}

```

```text
137:| 2026-07-02 | **marvin↔fauxmote link = UART first, layered message protocol (spec: [`docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md`](../../../docs/marvin-fauxmote-link.md)).** Three layers: transport-agnostic message layer (`TYPE`+fixed payload), a UART framing layer (`SOF 0x7E`/`TYPE`/`LEN`/`CRC8`), UART PHY (1 Mbaud 8-N-1 on a **second** UART, not the CDC console). Messages are **independent state-slice updaters**: `GUITAR` (3 B hot: fret/strum mask + whammy + aux), `WIIMOTE` (4 B nav: core buttons/D-pad/stick), plus planned `ACCEL` (3 B, tilt→star power) and `POINTER` (3 B, IR) slices, `LINK_CMD` (1 B: pair/stop/reconnect/unlink/ext), and `STATUS` (4 B f→m). fauxmote latches each slice and assembles the Wii report from all of them; each slice is absolute/latest-wins. A **single** 200 ms link watchdog (reset by any control message) reverts *all* slices to safe defaults when the link goes fully quiet. `GUITAR` byte 0 is bit-identical to marvin's T1S guitar mask. The link is a second front-end over the existing `Wiimote_*`/`Guitar_*`/`Fauxmote_*` APIs (a `marvin_link.c` beside the CLI). | Primary purpose is low-latency GH gameplay, so the hot path is one tiny fixed message with no handshake/ack. Absolute state matches both ends (marvin's bitmask + fauxmote's ~15 ms streaming) and self-heals dropped frames. Layering keeps the message bytes identical when the transport later moves to T1S — only the framing binding changes (Ethernet FCS replaces `SOF`/`CRC`). Reusing the CLI's module APIs avoids duplicating any behavior. Resolves Q5. |
138:| 2026-06-13 | **Removed the persistent auto-reconnect task; recovery is the manual `reconnect` command only.** Drops just reset state (`Wiimote_NotifyDisconnected`); no automatic re-initiation. | Auto-reconnect neither survived the GH3 game-launch handoff nor served as a keep-awake mechanism (reconnecting ≠ staying awake). Keeping the Wii awake is better done with occasional input/state changes, which Marvin's command stream provides during use. Removing it also drops the slot-leak/backoff complexity. The sniff-delay override (idle→sniff = 65 s) stays — that genuinely prevents idle supervision-timeout drops. |
139:| 2026-06-13 | **Extension encryption is mandatory for GH3 and implemented in the base Wiimote (`ext_crypto.c`); the guitar module stays plaintext.** GH3's real key handshake (register trace): `0x55`→`0xf0` (disable) → read ID `0xfa` in clear → `0xAA`→`0xf0` (enable) → 16-byte key to `0x40`-`0x4f`. The base captures the key, derives ft/sb, and encrypts outgoing ext data (streamed bytes @ offset `0x08`; reg reads @ `addr & 7`). | Everything GH3 reads from the extension is decrypted with that key, so plaintext is garbage (the "green/red worked unencrypted" observation was a decryption coincidence). Encryption is a generic Wiimote feature (nunchuk/classic encrypt too), so it belongs in the base, not the guitar. Corrects the plan's guess that GH3 used the old `0→0x40` init. |
140:| 2026-06-13 | **Cipher tables come from Dolphin's 1st-party set, not `rnconrad/WiimoteEmulator`'s `wm_crypto.c`.** rnconrad's S-boxes are corrupted (sbox[3]@0x60, [4]@0xd8, [6]@0x88/0xec are `0xD0`/`0xF0` & `0xD2`/`0xE2` transcription flips → not valid permutations). Used Dolphin's `keygen_sbox_1st_party` + `sboxes_1st_party[8]`; verified the key-schedule/encrypt algorithm term-for-term against Dolphin and round-tripped GH3's real key (idx 0, encrypt→decrypt identity). | Wrong table bytes silently corrupt the keystream → undebuggable "notes are garbage." _**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 23:31:55Z)**_
```

Great question — and you've put your finger on the actual bug. Let me answer the mechanics precisely, then confirm what our code does.

## How BT-Classic HID transmit actually works
Fauxmote is the ACL **slave**; the Wii is **master**. In BR/EDR a slave can only physically transmit **when the master polls it** — the Wii grants fauxmote a slot, and only then does a queued packet go out. Fauxmote can't "send whenever it wants"; every `write()` to the L2CAP interrupt channel goes into the **controller's outbound queue** and leaves on the next poll the Wii gives us.

So with one controller, the Wii polls fast → the queue never builds. With two controllers, the Wii's poll rate *to fauxmote* drops → if we keep stuffing the queue at a fixed 15 ms, it backs up. HID reports are a **FIFO**, so the Wii drains *stale* snapshots first and the fresh button-press report sits behind them → exactly your "press a button, big delay" symptom. You're right that this is wrong: an input device should keep **one** current-state packet and send that when it's polled, never a backlog.

## What our code does today
- `sender_task` writes a full report **every 15 ms unconditionally** while streaming ([wiimote.c:442-467](firmware/fauxmote/main/wiimote.c#L442-L467)).
- `wm_send` just does `write(fd, …)` and **ignores the result** ([wiimote.c:74-83](firmware/fauxmote/main/wiimote.c#L74-L83)) — no check for whether the previous packet has actually gone out, no coalescing.

So we *are* queueing: 67 writes/sec into the L2CAP tx buffer regardless of whether the Wii has drained the last one. That's the design flaw you're describing. Let me confirm two details that determine the exact failure (blocking vs. drop-newest, and whether there's a congestion signal we can gate on).

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 23:34:46Z)**_

That's the whole story. The L2CAP tx path is a **10-deep FIFO with a blocking writer**:

- `SLOT_TX_QUEUE_SIZE = 10` ([btc_l2cap.c:39](file:///Users/gregmrozek/.espressif/v6.0.1/esp-idf/components/bt/host/bluedroid/btc/profile/std/l2cap/btc_l2cap.c)) — each channel queues up to 10 outbound reports.
- `l2cap_vfs_write` enqueues; when the queue is **full it blocks** on `xEventGroupWaitBits(… SLOT_WRITE_BIT …, VFS_WRITE_TIMEOUT)` until a slot drains ([btc_l2cap.c:1108-1116](file:///Users/gregmrozek/.espressif/v6.0.1/esp-idf/components/bt/host/bluedroid/btc/profile/std/l2cap/btc_l2cap.c)).

So your instinct is exactly right, and here's the precise failure:

**Today** `sender_task` `write()`s a full report **every 15 ms no matter what** ([wiimote.c:458-465](firmware/fauxmote/main/wiimote.c#L458-L465)). When the Wii polls fast (one controller) the FIFO drains instantly and stays empty. When the Wii polls slowly (two controllers), the FIFO **fills with 10 identical, stale snapshots**, and a fresh button-press report gets enqueued *behind* those 10 — so the Wii delivers 10 old frames before the new state. At a reduced poll rate that's your multi-hundred-ms lag. It's not that we send on poll — we blindly push, and the FIFO hoards stale duplicates.

## The fix (your model, achievable without touching IDF)
We can't reorder/flush Bluedroid's FIFO from the app, and the VFS write ignores `O_NONBLOCK` (it always waits on the event group), so the clean lever is to **stop enqueueing stale duplicates**: send a report **only when the state actually changed**, plus a low-rate keepalive (e.g. every ~100 ms, well inside the 1 s supervision timeout).

Why that fixes it: with on-change, the FIFO sits **empty** while nothing changes, so when you press a button the report enqueues into an empty queue and goes out on the **very next poll** — minimal lag, independent of contention. It also matches "send the current state when it's our turn," because at any poll the queue holds at most the latest change, not a backlog of duplicates. Bonus: it cuts our BT airtime ~10× (67 Hz → a few Hz idle), which is friendlier to the shared piconet anyway.

Residual: a *burst* of distinct changes (fast strumming) could still enqueue a few real states under heavy contention, but those are genuine inputs, not stale copies, and it's bounded by input rate (~10–20/s), not 67/s.

Want me to implement send-on-change + keepalive in `sender_task` (dedupe against the last-sent bytes, keepalive timer)? It's contained to `wiimote.c` and preserves the honor-the-Wii's-reporting-mode behavior.

Correct concern, and yes — that's exactly the intent: `s_last_tx_at` gets updated on **every** send (change-driven *or* keepalive-driven), so the keepalive measures "time since the last packet of any kind." _**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 23:39:19Z)**_

Done — `SENDER_KEEPALIVE_MS` is now 250. Still well within the ~1 s supervision timeout you saw in the log (`supv_to 1600` = 1000 ms), so ~4 keepalives per supervision window — plenty of margin, and much less idle chatter than 100 ms.

So the current behavior in `sender_task`:
- **On change** → send immediately, reset the timer.
- **No change** → resend once every 250 ms (keepalive), timer resets on that send too.
- Steady input stream → never hits the keepalive; the tx FIFO stays shallow so a fresh press ships on the next Wii poll.

```bash
fauxmote: fix two-controller input lag (send-on-change, not fixed-rate stream)

With a second real Wiimote connected, fauxmote's inputs lagged badly while the
real Wiimote stayed crisp. Root cause: sender_task streamed a full report every
15 ms unconditionally. Bluedroid's L2CAP tx path is a 10-deep FIFO with a
blocking writer, and fauxmote (ACL slave) only transmits when the Wii polls it.
One controller: the Wii polls fast, FIFO drains. Two controllers: the Wii's poll
rate to fauxmote drops, the FIFO fills with 10 identical stale snapshots, and a
fresh press queues behind them -> multi-hundred-ms lag.

- wiimote.c: send a report only on change; otherwise resend at a 250 ms
  keepalive (well under the ~1 s supervision timeout). Keepalive timer resets on
  every send, so a steady input stream never triggers it; on-change keeps the tx
  FIFO empty so a press ships on the next poll. Reset the last-sent tracker on
  disconnect so the first report after reconnect always ships.
- bt_role.{c,h} + console `role [slave|master]` + open-time ACL-role log:
  instrumentation added to rule out the scatternet/role hypothesis first (role
  came back SLAVE, so the fix is the tx path, not the role).

Confirmed on hardware: significant improvement to two-controller latency.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-14 23:42:34Z)**_

Committed as `b172894` on `gui` — 7 files, fauxmote-only, no unrelated noise.

**Summary of the fix:**
- **Root cause:** `sender_task` streamed a report every 15 ms unconditionally. Bluedroid's L2CAP tx path is a 10-deep FIFO with a blocking writer, and fauxmote (ACL slave) only transmits when the Wii polls it. A second real Wiimote halves the Wii's poll rate to fauxmote → the FIFO filled with 10 stale duplicates → a fresh press queued behind them.
- **Fix (`wiimote.c`):** send-on-change + 250 ms keepalive (timer resets on every send). The tx FIFO stays empty while idle, so a press ships on the next poll regardless of contention. Last-sent tracker resets on disconnect.
- **Also committed:** the `bt_role.{c,h}` module + `role` console command + open-time ACL-role log — the instrumentation that ruled out the scatternet/role theory (role came back `SLAVE`), leaving the tx path as the culprit. Worth keeping as a permanent diagnostic.

Journal updated with root cause, fix, and the "confirmed on hardware" note, plus the role-investigation entry beneath it.

Two follow-ups you may want to consider later (not done, not blocking):
- **Auto-slave at connect** is now moot for this bug, but the `role` lever stays useful if a future setup ever pages differently.
- If heavy strumming under contention still shows any residual lag, the next lever would be bounding in-flight further (the on-change path already keeps it shallow, so this is unlikely to be needed).

Both branches of today's work — the 2p CV detector geometry and the fauxmote latency fix — are now committed on `gui`.
